title: macOS: move application menus to the system menu bar
author: reoniazx
body:
SoundCraft currently draws its application menus inside the main window on macOS. This change installs them in the macOS system menu bar and removes the duplicate in-window strip, so File, Edit, View, Track and the remaining menus appear at the top of the screen when SoundCraft is active.

The native menu is built from the existing catalog and shares command resolution, enabled/checked state and menu-style dispatch with egui, including commands that open dialogs. It adds macOS Services and Hide actions, and moves the session name, dirty indicator and Edit/Mix mode into the window title. The macOS dependency and host integration are platform-gated; other desktop platforms, web and offscreen renders retain the egui menu.

Keyboard shortcuts remain handled by egui; native menu items do not register accelerators.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci`: formatting, workspace Clippy, all 439 tests, asset attribution, architecture layers and WASM checks passed.
- `cargo build --release -p soundcraft` passed.

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does, via `WebLogger`; `main` even had an empty `if RUST_LOG is none {}` block), so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` is discarded, including audio stream errors and plugin failures. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/soundcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/soundcraft.log` in the settings directory, next to `ui.json`, `Autosave/` and `Presets/` (Linux `~/.config/soundcraft/logs/`). `SOUNDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` runs log to standard error only.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `soundcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512).
- **Levels:** `info` for `soundcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

### Realtime safety

A logger that takes a mutex and writes files must never run on the audio thread, and several records can originate there: cpal error callbacks (ALSA repeats `audio stream error` in a loop), `synth.rs` "instrument event queue full", hosted CLAP/VST3/AU `process` errors, CLAP's `host_log`, and the engine panic hook. Because `MixEngine::render` fans strips out to rayon workers (4+ strips), patching each call site would miss records from worker thread…

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![SoundCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/soundcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the SoundCraft colour field, SoundCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small SoundCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 28 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, SoundCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.
- `package.sh` copies the TIFF and the layout into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`, and nothing extra runs in the signing job.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `SoundCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `SoundCraft`; the DMG file name still c…

title: Release: Flatpak x86_64/aarch64, AppImage zsync updates, README Downloads
author: echelon

Completes the release platform set for SoundCraft (Windows arm64 and FreeBSD x86_64 were already in place).

title: Fix the crash on quit after a VST3 scan: run module exits on the entry thread
author: ebbicott
body:
Closes #16.

On macOS, any process that had loaded VST3 plugins could segfault on exit when Steinberg's HALion Sonic is installed: the app on quit, `soundcraft-cli`, and the `soundcraft-engine`, `soundcraft-mix` and `soundcraft-vst3-host` unit tests. The VST3 host ran each module's entry but never its exit. The issue has the full diagnosis and crash stacks.

## What changes

All `unsafe` stays in `crates/vst3-host/src/ffi.rs`, each block with a `// SAFETY:` comment.

- **Module exits run, after the factory is released.** For each loaded module, newest first, the host releases the cached factory and then calls the module exit (`bundleExit` / `ExitDll` / `ModuleExit`), as the VST3 SDK's own host does.
- **Up front, before the process exits.** `soundcraft_vst3_host::shutdown()` runs the exits. `soundcraft_engine::shutdown_plugin_hosts()` calls it, and so covers every plugin host in one place.
  - The app calls it from `on_exit`, after releasing its player and with it the plugin instances. `on_exit` runs on every way out, including the system Quit (⌘Q), which calls `exit()` from inside the event loop, so `run_native` never returns.
  - The CLI calls it after its subcommand returns.
- **An exit handler as the fallback.** For any other exit (test binaries, for example), an `atexit` handler runs the exits. It is registered again after each new module, so it runs before the static destructors of every module loaded so far. That is enough after a scan, but too late once a plugin has been used (see testing).
- **On the thread that ran the entry.** Massive X crashes in `bundleExit` on any other thread. Modules asked for on the main thread are entered there, which covers the app and the CLI. Requests from any other thread go to a long-lived `vst3-modules` thread, which also runs their exits, because the requesting thread may be gone by then.
- **Modules still in use are left alone.** That means a module with a live instance, or one whose editor view `EditorLink::kill` had to le…

title: Fix keyboard shortcuts on Windows and Linux: Ctrl is the Cmd key (#15)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #15.

On Windows (and Linux), keyboard shortcuts did not work. No Cmd+ shortcut fired, and Ctrl+S opened Search instead of saving. egui reports a held Ctrl as both `ctrl` and `command` there. The shortcut matcher wanted `ctrl` to be off for a Cmd+ shortcut, and Ctrl+S matched the Cmd+Ctrl+S Search chord.

What changed (crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs):
- Off macOS, a held Ctrl counts as the shortcut's Cmd, so Ctrl+S saves and Ctrl+X cuts. Shortcuts that also need the Mac Control key (Cmd+Ctrl+...) have no key of their own off macOS, so they no longer steal plain Ctrl chords.
- The Cmd+Ctrl+S Search chord works only on macOS. On other platforms, Search is still in the Window menu.

Tests: unit tests in shortcuts.rs check the modifier matching and the Search chord for both macOS and non-macOS. The platform is a parameter, so both cases run on every CI host.

title: Plugin menus by vendor (scrollable), Audio Units inserts, and an instrument picker
author: ebbicott
body:
Closes #21. Closes #22.

> **Stacked on #17.** Its three commits show up here until #17 merges, because loading and closing instruments needs that crash fix. This PR's own changes are the last two commits, `2a8c609` and `ed47ec0`.

On a composer's Mac with 75 VST3 plugins and 123 Audio Units, there were three problems:
- the insert menus ran off the screen;
- choosing an Audio Unit did nothing;
- there was no way to choose a third-party instrument (Kontakt, BBC Symphony Orchestra, Synchron, NotePerformer and so on) or to open its editor.

### `2a8c609` Plugin menus by vendor, scrollable; Audio Units insert (#21)

  - In `crates/ui-egui/src/mix_window.rs`: `hosted_menus` and `vendor_menus`.
  - Each format is still scanned the first time its submenu opens.
- **Audio Units insert.** The engine's plugin lookup (`cmd::clap::plugin_info`, used by `mix.insert`) now includes Audio Units, so `au:` ids resolve. Before, they failed with "unknown plugin" and the UI dropped the error. A failed insert now shows in the status bar.

### `ed47ec0` Instrument picker (#22)

- **`mix.instrument {track?, plugin}`.** A new command module, `cmd/instrument.rs`, that sets an instrument track's instrument with the plugin's default parameters. It is undoable, and it refuses effects and other track kinds.
- **The `INST` label** on an instrument track's header (Edit window) opens the instrument menu:

- **The Mix window's INSTRUMENT row** (View › Mix Window Views › Instruments) shows the track's instrument. It used to look for an instrument among the inserts. A click opens a hosted instrument's plugin window, and a right-click …

title: Make the Click option audible: metronome in live playback
author: Garygunn94
body:
## What changed
Options > Click set a flag, but nothing rendered sound, so a click track was silent. The mix engine now plays a short synthesized blip on every beat of the tempo map, accented on beat 1 of each bar. Level, pitch and velocity come from the existing `click.*` settings in Setup > Click/Countoff. "Only during record" is respected.

## Why it is playback-only
The metronome is mixed in only when `MixEngine::metronome` is set. Live playback sets it; offline renders (bounce, stems, exports) leave it off, so the click is never printed into a file. Bounces and stems are unchanged by this PR.

## Other changes
- `midi_to_hz` moves from the engine demo into `soundcraft-dsp`, so the mix and demo share one tuning formula. Demo output is unchanged.

## Reviewer notes
- Not heard on a real audio device. Live playback goes through the same render path the tests cover, but please listen once before merging.
- Not implemented: Count Off. The Setup count-in settings and the Options > Count Off toggle exist but do nothing.
- "Create Click Track" still makes an empty aux track. It also turns the click on, so the click is audible, but the track itself carries no audio.
- Tests: `cargo test` for `soundcraft-mix`, `soundcraft-engine`, `soundcraft-dsp` and `soundcraft-playback` passes; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean on the touched crates.

title: Fix input monitoring pitch and dropouts when input and session rates differ
author: Garygunn94
body:
## Problem
Input monitoring fed raw input-device samples to the output callback as if they were at the session rate. When the input device runs at a different rate (e.g. 16 kHz or 44.1 kHz into a 48 kHz session), monitored audio plays too fast (higher pitch) and the buffer runs dry between bursts, so it sounds very quiet.

## Change
- `InputRing` knows the input rate and converts to the session rate with linear interpolation inside `pop_into`. Allocation-free and non-blocking, so the audio thread rules still hold.
- The buffer cap is computed once in `new()`, replacing two formulas that had drifted apart.
- `render_next` passes the session rate into `pop_into`.

## Not in this PR
- Monitoring can start up to 0.5 s behind the input, because the ring keeps filling while monitoring is off.
- There is no jitter cushion, so input bursts can still cause dropouts. Fixing this needs a target fill level, which is a latency decision.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback`: 10/10, including new tests for up-conversion (16 kHz to 48 kHz), down-conversion (96 kHz to 48 kHz), equal rates and underrun.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm all pass.
- Not tested with real audio hardware.

title: Keep the clip context menu open while moving onto it
author: Garygunn94
body:
## Problem
Right-clicking a recorded clip opened the clip menu, but it vanished as soon as the pointer moved onto it, so Delete could not be reached.

## Cause
The clip menu was attached at the end of `lane_interaction`. That function returns early when the lane has no pointer position. Once the menu is open, the pointer is over the popup, the lane loses its hover, and the menu is never drawn again.

## Change
- Attach the clip menu before the early return.
- Remember the right-clicked clip so the menu keeps its target while in use. The stored id is dropped if the clip no longer exists.
- Add a kittest regression test (`crates/ui-egui/tests/clip_menu.rs`): right-click a clip, move onto the menu, click Delete, and assert the clip is removed. It fails on the previous code.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No SoundCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to SoundCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.

## Problem

SoundCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/soundcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p soundcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo check -p soundcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles.
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

title: Fix debug overflow panic on the first automation-write pass
author: reoniazx
body:
write_automation gates passes on (pos - last_write_at).abs(), but last_write_at starts (and resets) at i64::MIN, so the first playing frame subtracts with overflow and panics in debug builds. Extracted the gate into automation_step_due with saturating arithmetic: the never-written marker is always due, and restarts and loop wraps stay overflow-free with no behavior change in release builds.

Repro: cargo run -p soundcraft-ui-egui --example ui_shot -- out.png script.jsonl with transport.play in the script panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs (attempt to subtract with overflow); the same script now renders cleanly.

Validation:
- cargo xtask ci: fmt, workspace Clippy, tests, asset attribution, architecture layers and WASM checks passed.
- New automation_step_due regression tests (3) cover first-pass-due, throttle step and loop wrap.

title: fix(Play Audio): Resume the web AudioContext on the first user gesture
author: hamada147
body:
cpal (wasm) creates its output stream at startup, before any user gesture, so the browser leaves the WebAudio AudioContext 'suspended'. As a result no audio plays, and the transport clock never advances because the audio callback drives it.

Wrap the AudioContext constructor before the wasm module loads so that every context cpal creates is captured. On the first pointer, mouse, touch or key event, resume any context that is still suspended.

Edit 1:
The issue happens on macOS using Google Chrome through web assembly inside of a docker container and connected to SoundCraft on HTTPS using self signed certificate

title: Add disk-backed PCM WAV frame reader
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
- Add `DiskWavReader` for native PCM and IEEE-float WAV. It walks chunk headers, keeps the data-chunk length from the header, and reads one frame window at a time. A chunk after `data` is not treated as samples. A data chunk that starts past 1 MiB is reached by seeking over the preceding chunk. Compressed WAV stays on the existing decoder.
- This branch is only `crates/audio-io`. The Play/Stop transport edits stay on #33.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io` (52 tests), including window reads against the in-memory decoder for 16-bit, 24-bit, and float, reads at and past the end, a trailing `LIST` chunk, a data chunk past 1 MiB, and a truncated header.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-audio-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`

- Rust gates could not start because `cargo` is not installed in the local environment.

title: Fix drag selection and the insertion point in the Edit window
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #166: dragging a selection up from the last track deselected it and selected every track above instead. Fixed, along with related Edit-window drag problems:

- Drag selection spans exactly the tracks between the press and the pointer, in either direction, and the whole window updates in the same frame.
- Shift+click in another track adds it to the selection with the same range, as in Pro Tools, so the selected tracks no longer have to be adjacent.
- Track names follow Pro Tools' rules in the Edit window, the Mix window and the Tracks list: Shift+click selects every track between the nearest selected one and the clicked one, and Cmd+click (Ctrl+click on Windows and Linux) adds or removes one. A click on a name used to replace the selection.
- Dropping a track's name plate lower down no longer sends the track to the end.
- Drags act where you pressed: a quick drag from a clip edge now trims instead of moving the clip.
- Dragging past the edge of the track area scrolls, and a flick past the last track selects down to it.
- The insertion point moves on press, shows immediately, and only on the selected tracks.
- `edit.select` no longer makes a new document revision when nothing changed (each one is resent to the audio engine).
- Fixes a panic when a fade drag's clip shrinks to zero length.

Tested: 21 new tests (20 UI tests driving real pointer events through `egui_kittest`, one engine test), each failing before its fix. fmt, workspace clippy, `xtask layers`/`assets` and the wasm check pass, and I tried the drags by hand on macOS with the demo session. Not run: the VST3 host tests that abort on machines with third-party VST3s installed.

title: soundcraft-cli --help: stop at the closing code fence, no Rust source lines (#48)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #48

`soundcraft-cli --help` built its text from the module doc comment with `.skip(3).take(14)`, but the usage block is only 11 lines long. So the output ended with the closing code fence, `#![deny(...)]`, a blank line and `use serde_json::{Value, json};`.

This adds a small `help_text()` that takes doc lines until the closing fence (`take_while(|l| l.trim_end() != "//! ```")`) instead of a fixed count. `--help` now uses it. The help still follows the doc comment if commands are added or removed later.

Test: `help_text_is_only_the_usage_block` checks that the help starts with the `info` line, ends with the `plugins` line, and has no code fence and no Rust source. It fails with the old `take(14)` slice.

Only the help output changes.

title: CLI: run --cmd and app reject malformed JSON instead of using empty params (#50)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #50

`soundcraft-cli run --cmd ID=JSON` parsed the params with `serde_json::from_str(p).unwrap_or(json!({}))`. With malformed JSON (for example a missing closing brace) the command ran with default params and exited 0, or failed later with a misleading missing-parameter error. `app METHOD [JSON]` did the same with `.ok().unwrap_or(json!({}))`.

This adds a small `parse_cmd_spec()` for the `--cmd` argument. `ID` alone still gives `{}`. `ID=JSON` with invalid JSON now returns `ID: bad JSON: <serde error>`, and `run` exits 1 before it executes that command. `app` now fails the same way when its JSON argument is given but does not parse; an omitted argument still gives `{}`. The message matches the one `script` already prints.

Tests: `cmd_spec_parses_id_and_json` checks a bare id and a valid `ID=JSON`. `cmd_spec_rejects_truncated_json` checks that `a.b={"x":` is an error; with the old `unwrap_or` it would have given `{}`.

Only the parsing of these JSON arguments changes. Valid and omitted params work as before.

title: convert and bounce: refuse output extensions the encoder cannot write instead of saving WAV data (#47)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #47.

`soundcraft-cli convert in.wav out.mp3` and `run --bounce mix.mp3` (and `.ogg`, `.m4a`, `.xyz`, ...) used to fall through to the WAV encoder, write PCM WAV under that name and exit 0.

- `soundcraft-audio-io` gets `encode_format_for(name)`, which maps an extension or format name (case-insensitive, leading dot allowed) to the `FileFormat` that `encode` really writes (`wav`, `aif`/`aiff`, `flac`), or `None`. `ENCODE_EXTENSIONS` lists them for error messages.
- `convert` uses it and fails before writing anything: ``out.mp3: cannot write `.mp3` files (supported: wav, aif, aiff, flac)``, non-zero exit code.
- `file.bounce_mix` (which `run --bounce` calls) uses it for both the `format` param and the path extension and returns a bad-params error, so no file is written and the CLI exits non-zero.

A path with no extension still bounces/converts to WAV, as before.

Tests:
- `crates/audio-io/tests/encode_format.rs`: the mapping accepts wav/aif/aiff/flac and rejects mp3/ogg/m4a/xyz.
- `cmd::file::tests::bounce_refuses_formats_it_cannot_write`: bouncing to `.mp3`/`.ogg`/`.xyz` errors and leaves no file; `.flac` still works. Without the fix the `.mp3` bounce succeeds and the test fails.

title: Report session audio health without changing the session
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
- Window → Session Audio Health asks `session.audio_health` and shows the report. Closing the window clears the snapshot.
- The query checks every audio clip, including inactive playlists. It does not read files, analyse the signal, or change the session.
- Reported problems are a zero session sample rate, missing source metadata, audio that is not loaded, a sample-rate mismatch, empty or uneven channel buffers, invalid clip length or stretch, and a clip that extends outside the loaded audio.

## Validation
- `rtk cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib health:: --offline` — 5 passed
- `rtk cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --lib window_command_renders_report --offline` — 1 passed

title: Scan third-party plugins in child processes
author: grovebit
body:
Reading what a VST3 or CLAP file holds runs its code, and SoundCraft did that in-process for every installed plugin, so one bad plugin could take the app down. On a machine with UAD, Waves and NI plugins even `cargo test` aborted, and Kontakt crashed the app on quit.

Now each plugin file is read by a short-lived child (the app run as `--scan-plugin <format> <path>`), a few at a time, with a timeout. A crash or hang costs only that file. It's listed under the CLAP/VST3 insert menus and in `engine.plugin_scan_failures`. Results are cached per user, and only inserted plugins are ever loaded into the app. Scanning stays off until an app calls `soundcraft_engine::plugins::init()`, so tests never load the machine's plugins.

**Policy question:** the children's `_exit` and macOS `LSBackgroundOnly` calls need `unsafe`, so they live in `vst3-host/src/ffi.rs`, and AGENTS.md now says so. Happy to move them into a `plugin-scan` exception instead.

**Tested** on macOS: fmt, clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `xtask layers`, `xtask assets` and `xtask wasm`. That includes an end-to-end test where a plugin kills its scan child. Not run: Windows, Linux.

title: Trackpad-friendly Edit window: smooth panning, pinch and Cmd+scroll zoom
author: grovebit
body:
Trackpad gestures barely worked in the Edit window: pinch and Cmd+scroll didn't zoom, Shift+wheel didn't pan, and slow swipes didn't move at close zoom.

- Pinch and Cmd/Ctrl+scroll zoom around the pointer; Shift+wheel pans sideways.
- Two-finger swipes pan smoothly at any zoom, in the Edit window and the MIDI editor.
- Zoom and scroll no longer create a new document revision, journal entry or undo step every frame (each revision was resent to the audio engine).
- Control channel: `ui.scroll` and `ui.zoom`, to drive these from tests.

Tested: 6 new tests, 3 of them driving real input through the UI. CI checks pass locally, apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed. Tried by hand on macOS.

title: Warn about missing media when opening a session (#57)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #57.

`io::open_session` already finds the media files that a session refers to but cannot load, and returns them. The callers ignored that list, so a session with missing audio opened without any message, and `run --in ... bounce` wrote a silent WAV.

Changes:

- `soundcraft-cli`: `info FILE.scraft`, `run --in` and `script --in` (both use `load_engine`) now print one `warning: missing media: <path>` line to stderr for each missing file. Exit codes and stdout do not change.
- `session.open` (and so the MCP `open_session` tool) now returns `"missing": [...]` with the same list. The list is empty when all files are found.
- `docs/mcp.md`: documents the new `missing` field.

Tests:

- `missing_media_gets_one_warning_each` (CLI): checks the warning lines made from the list.
- `session_open_reports_missing_media` (engine): saves the demo session to a temp directory, opens it (`missing` is empty), deletes the audio files, opens it again and checks that `missing` is not empty. Without this change, `missing` is not in the result and the test fails.

title: Honor `file.import_audio new_tracks` (#60)
author: salignatmoandal
body:
## Summary
- `file.import_audio` advertised `new_tracks` but never read it; the flag is now honoured.
- Explicit `track` still wins. `new_tracks: true` (default) creates a new track. `new_tracks: false` imports onto the selected audio track, or returns a clear error when neither `track` nor a selection is available.
- Params docs updated to match the behaviour. Regression test covers true / false / omitted / explicit track.

Fixes #60.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::file::tests::import_audio_honours_new_tracks`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --lib -- -D warnings`
- [ ] Confirm `soundcraft-cli describe file.import_audio` shows the updated params text
- [ ] Manual: `run --cmd 'track.new={"name":"Target"}' --cmd 'file.import_audio={"path":"tone.wav","new_tracks":false}'` after selecting Target (or pass `"track":"Target"`)

title: inspect: report `sources[].loaded` for agents
author: salignatmoandal
body:
## Summary
- `session.inspect` / MCP `inspect_session` now include `"loaded": bool` on every `sources[]` entry (`pool.contains(id)`).
- Agents can distinguish “source listed in the session” from “decoded audio actually in memory” without a separate health window.
- Complements [#57](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/issues/57) / PR [#58](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/58) (`open_session` → `missing`) and PR [#54](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/54) (`session.audio_health`): this is the lightweight field on the path agents already use.
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md`, `docs/mcp.md`.
- `contributors/people.toml`: credit for `@salignatmoandal`.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib inspect::tests::sources_report_whether_audio_is_loaded`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings`
- [ ] After open with missing media: `inspect_session` shows `loaded: false` while path/frames remain

title: Show Ctrl instead of Cmd in shortcut text off macOS (#62)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #62.

The command registry stores shortcuts in macOS form ("Cmd+N", "Cmd+Shift+W"), and the UI printed them as stored, so Windows, Linux and the web build showed "Cmd" for keys that are really Ctrl there.

This adds a small `shortcut_label(s, mac)` helper in `shortcuts.rs` and uses it everywhere a registry shortcut is displayed: menu items, the command palette and Setup > Keyboard Shortcuts.

- The platform is decided at runtime with `ctx.os().is_mac()`, not `cfg!(target_os)`, so the web build follows the browser's user agent.
- On macOS the text is unchanged.
- Off macOS, `Cmd` becomes `Ctrl` ("Cmd+Alt+B" shows as "Ctrl+Alt+B").
- Mac Control-key chords that hold both Cmd and Ctrl ("Cmd+Ctrl+X", "Cmd+Ctrl+D") have no key of their own off macOS, so they show no shortcut text there instead of "Ctrl+Ctrl+X".

Only display text changes. Shortcut matching is untouched.

Tests: `shortcut_label` unit tests cover Cmd to Ctrl, plain shortcuts with no Cmd, the Cmd+Ctrl case, and that macOS text is unchanged.

title: Add Ukrainian UI translation
author: dmatviichuk
body:
SoundCraft’s UI currently has only English captions. This adds Ukrainian across the built-in editor/mixer controls, menus, command palette, dialogs, floating windows, and audio-processing parameter captions, with a 1,300-entry catalog and English fallback.

Users can select System, English, or Ukrainian from SoundCraft → Language or UI Customization. System uses the native OS locale or browser language; the explicit choice persists in the existing desktop preferences (web choice is session-only). Translation stays in the UI layer: original command IDs, routing/parameter values, and user-assigned session, track, clip, bus, preset and plugin names remain intact. Engine/external diagnostic messages retain their original wording. New Tracks uses two compact rows so Ukrainian captions leave room for its name field.

- Visually checked the Ukrainian editor, preferences, New Tracks, mixer/compressor, and Bounce Mix using the bundled fonts. Temporary validation artifacts stay outside the repository; no screenshots or new Markdown files are included.

Dictionary/context review:
- Checked 2,717 Cyrillic tokens (1,150 distinct) against the official [VESUM Hunspell 6.8.6 dictionary](https://github.com/brown-uk/dict_uk/releases/tag/v6.8.6). [ULIF](https://lcorp.ulif.org.ua/dictua/) confirms exact headwords for панорама, мікшер, еквалайзер, дискретизація and надсилання.

title: Shift+Cmd+K exports clips as files
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #7: ⇧⌘K did nothing, because Export Clips as Files had no shortcut.

- ⇧⌘K (Ctrl+Shift+K on Windows and Linux), Pro Tools' key for it, opens the folder prompt, and OK exports the selected clips.
- Browse… in folder prompts now picks a folder instead of an audio file.
- The status bar confirms the export, and with nothing selected it says "no clips selected" instead of silently writing nothing.

Tested: 519 tests pass, and the fmt, clippy, layers, assets and wasm checks pass on macOS. 6 tests that load this Mac's installed VST3 plugins abort here, on `main` too, and were skipped. Checked ⇧⌘K, the prompt and the status message in the running app on macOS.

title: Add semantic-release automation on main
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
- run semantic-release 25 on every push to `main`, with conventional major/minor analysis and a patch floor
- create a draft GitHub Release, update `release`, and explicitly dispatch the existing packaging workflow
- pin semantic-release packages exactly and Actions to immutable revisions

## Validation
- same semantic-release/plugin lifecycle already dry-run validated in the sibling Craft apps
- focused `actionlint`, JSON parsing, and `git diff --check`
- exactly one commit over current upstream `main`

This PR intentionally contains no Flatpak or Pages changes; those are proposed separately. Aikido was not run at the contributor's request.

## Repository setup required
Repository rules must allow the workflow token to push generated release commits/tags to `main`, update `release`, and dispatch Actions.

title: Publish Flatpak repository through GitHub Pages
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
- add a standalone workflow triggered only by a published GitHub Release or manual selection of an already-published release
- require a strict `v<SemVer>` tag and verify checksums for the exact x86_64 and aarch64 Flatpak assets
- validate each bundle's `app/ai.storyteller.soundcraft/<arch>/stable` ref
- preserve prior OSTree history, import both architectures, and deploy a Flatpak repository under `/flatpak/`
- use immutable GitHub Pages Action revisions

## Validation
- focused `actionlint`, embedded Bash syntax/static assertions, strict SemVer tests, and `git diff --check`
- exactly one commit over current upstream `main`

This PR contains no semantic-release changes and is independently mergeable. Aikido was not run at the contributor's request.

## Repository setup and Pages coordination
1. Enable GitHub Pages with **GitHub Actions** as the source and permit the `github-pages` environment.
2. Published releases must contain `SHA256SUMS.txt` plus both exact `soundcraft-<version>-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.flatpak` assets.
3. This repository soundcraft may also have an existing or proposed docs/OpenWiki Pages deployment. GitHub Pages has one deployment target; coordinate a single composed artifact/deployment owner before merging both workflows, or the most recent deployment can replace the other site's files.

The OSTree repository is unsigned, matching the existing standalone Flatpak bundles; persistent signing requires a separate key-management design.

title: Clear clips and audio files from the Clip List (#4)
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #4: nothing in the Clip List could be removed.

- Clear… on any Clip List row's right-click menu, or Cmd+Shift+B, the Pro Tools shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows and Linux), on the selection. A clip leaves its track; a file leaves the session but stays on disk.
- As in Pro Tools, Clear asks first. For a file that timeline clips still use, the dialog says those clips go too. One undo restores everything.
- File rows can be selected now. Agents get `clip.clear {clips?, sources?, with_clips?}`, with no dialog; clearing a file still in use needs `with_clips: true`.

Tested: 7 new tests; fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; workspace tests pass except 5 VST3 tests skipped because they load this Mac's installed plugins. Tried by hand on macOS.

title: Change clip gain with Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down and a fader on the clip
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #2: there was no way to change a clip's gain.

- ⌃⇧↑ / ⌃⇧↓, Pro Tools' keys for it, nudge the selected clips' gain by 1 dB, and each nudge can be undone.
- With View > Clip > Clip Gain Info on, audio clips show a fader icon and their gain. Dragging the icon pops up a small fader, from −144 to +36 dB with ⌘ for fine moves, and each drag is one undo step.
- Clip Gain Info no longer depends on Clip Gain Line being shown, matching Pro Tools.
- ⌃↑/⌃↓ (extend selection) no longer take over the Shift versions of those keys.

Tested: 437 tests pass, and the fmt, clippy, layers, assets and wasm checks pass on macOS. 5 tests that load this Mac's installed VST3 plugins abort here, on `main` too, and were skipped. Checked in the app on macOS.

title: ci: Add RISC-V Linux build with deb, rpm, and tar.gz packaging
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Adds cross-compiled RISC-V (`riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu`) Linux builds to the release workflow using Ubuntu 26.04, packaging native `.deb` and `.rpm` files alongside standalone `.tar.gz`, with `qemu-user-static` smoke testing. Also upgrades `flatpak` runners to `ubuntu-26.04`.

### Changes

- **CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**:
  - Upgraded `flatpak` runner matrix to `ubuntu-26.04` and `ubuntu-26.04-arm`.
  - Added `linux-riscv64` cross-compilation job running on `ubuntu-26.04`.
  - Added `nfpm` to generate `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` packages for `riscv64`.
  - Added `linux-riscv64` to `needs:` in draft release job.
  - Smoke-tests `soundcraft-cli --version` under `qemu-riscv64-static`.
  - Uploads all assets via `dist/release/*`.
- **Packaging (`packaging/linux/package.sh`)**:
  - Added `CROSS_ARCH`, `CROSS_TARGET`, `CROSS_COMPILE`, and `EMULATOR` support.
  - Added `riscv64` to `DEB_ARCH` mapping.
- **Documentation (`README.md`, `docs/releasing.md`)**:
  - Documented `riscv64` `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` release assets and build requirements.

title: Record takes straight to disk
author: grovebit
body:
Takes were kept only in memory until Stop, in a buffer the audio thread kept reallocating, so a crash mid-take lost the whole recording.

- The input callback copies into a preallocated lock-free ring and never locks or allocates; samples that don't fit become silence, and the loss is reported.
- A writer thread streams each armed track's inputs to `<track>_<NN>.wav` in the session's Audio Files (the autosave folder until the session is first saved), rewriting the header every second; if a file can't be created, Record doesn't start and says why.
- At Stop the files become the clips' sources, and Save and autosave use them in place instead of copying them.
- Loop recording keeps one file per track, with one clip per pass on its own playlist, in one undo step.

Tested: 507 workspace tests pass (6 tests that load this Mac's installed VST3 plugins skipped), plus fmt, clippy -D warnings, layers, assets and wasm. Recorded live takes on macOS; a SIGKILL mid-take leaves a playable file.

title: fix(ui): follow live system appearance changes

The unchanged wasm gate passed after selecting rustup stable with its installed target.

title: Nudge clip gain with Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down on Windows and Linux too
author: grovebit
body:
Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down (#76) only nudged clip gain on macOS: on Windows and Linux the keys did nothing, though the Shortcuts window lists them.

- Off macOS, Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down now nudge the selected clips' gain: the same keys as on the Mac, and what the labels already show.
- Pro Tools for Windows uses the Start key for this, but egui doesn't report that key, and Windows and GNOME already use Win/Super+Shift+arrows to place windows.
- macOS is unchanged, and Ctrl+Up/Down without Shift still extends the selection.

title: Add a built-in Sampler instrument
author: scottcampbelldata
body:
Adds a sampler as a third built-in instrument next to the synth and drum synth. Roadmap focus #3, plugin depth.

What it does:
- plays one sample across the keyboard, 32 voices, cubic interpolation
- root note, transpose, fine tune, key tracking on or off
- key range and velocity range
- ADSR with velocity sensitivity
- sample start, forward or ping-pong loop
- gate or one shot

How you use it:
- mix.sampler_load {track, path, params?} loads WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 or OGG (same decoder as file.import_audio). It gets resampled to the session rate and saved in Audio Files with the session, so it reopens fine
- mix.sampler_clear {track}
- mix.instrument_param {track, param, value} works for any built-in instrument

While doing this I noticed built-in instrument params never got applied in the mix, so the synth and drum synth always ran on defaults. They get applied now. Hosted instruments are left alone.

No UI in this one. Sampler shows up in the instrument menu but you can't load a sample from the app yet. Planning that next (drag a file in, waveform with loop points, param sliders), then a step drum machine on top.

Tests: 19 in dsp, 10 in engine, all with generated audio, no bundled samples. cargo xtask ci passes locally (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Stop playback when replacing the session
author: reoniazx
body:
Creating a new session while playback is running leaves the old audio player or simulated clock running, so the playhead continues moving in the new project.

Reset transport status and discard pending transport requests whenever the session document is replaced. The UI stops and resets the old playback/capture state before sending the new session to the audio thread, without applying stop-time insertion or scrolling edits to the replacement document. This also covers opening, closing and reverting a session through the shared replacement path.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch independently of the other fixes.
- Regression tests cover ongoing playback, a Play request queued before the next frame, replaying the new session, preserving the replacement session's selection and clean state, and an invalid New Session request leaving the existing transport unchanged.
- Playback regressions use the simulated clock; they do not open an audio device.

title: Keep the playhead visible while playback is stopped
author: reoniazx
body:
The red playhead disappears when playback stops; the remaining insertion cursor blinks and requires a track selection.

Draw a persistent playhead across the Edit window's rulers and track area, and in the Universe overview. It follows the transport while playing and marks the edit insertion while stopped, including an empty session or a range selection. Playback auto-scrolling keeps its existing behavior.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch independently of the other fixes.
- A rendering regression checks the full-height line with no tracks, point and range selections, stopped and playing transport states, and different frame times.
- Offscreen screenshots were inspected in Dark and Light themes and with an empty session.

title: Support anchored trackpad zoom and smooth timeline navigation
author: reoniazx
body:
Pinch events do not zoom the Edit timeline, scrolling over rulers is ignored, and Shift+scroll is remapped a second time after egui has already converted it to horizontal movement.

Handle continuous pinch and Cmd/Ctrl+scroll zoom around the pointer through a new shared `view.zoom_at` command. Consume two-axis scrolling in the hovered Edit viewport, including rulers and track headers, preserve small deltas and native momentum input, and pause playhead following when manually panning away during playback. Timeline scrolling now uses saturating arithmetic at extreme offsets.

Add validated `ui.scroll` and `ui.zoom` control-channel methods for exercising the same pointer-input path, and document the gesture mappings and command parameters.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch independently of the other fixes.
- Six UI regressions cover anchored ruler pinch, two-axis scrolling and movement after finger release, Shift scrolling, continuous Cmd scrolling, isolation from other panels, and manual panning during playback.
- Engine tests cover anchor preservation, invalid zoom parameters and numeric limits; control-channel tests reject malformed gestures without queuing partial input.
- Before/after zoom and pan screenshots were inspected. Gesture tests use synthetic events; physical trackpad testing has not been performed.

title: Keep the MIDI editor dock at its resized height
author: reoniazx
body:
Dragging the MIDI Editor’s top edge could not retain the chosen height: its painter-only contents never claimed the resized space, so egui collapsed the dock to its 260-point minimum on subsequent frames.

Call `ui.take_available_space()` before painting, including the empty state. The dock now starts at its configured 320-point height, resizes in both directions, and preserves its chosen height when closed and reopened during the same app session.

Regression tests exercise the real editor with and without a selected MIDI clip. They cover enlargement, shrinking, the existing minimum height, persistence after release and reopening, timeline separation, and unchanged session data.

Validation:
- Both new regression tests reproduced the failure before the fix and pass afterward.
- Local workspace checks passed: formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, asset attribution, architecture layers, and WASM compilation. Stale build caches were rebuilt for the native and WASM engine checks.
- Offscreen renders verified enlargement and shrinking at 1600×1000 and 1200×800.
- Formatting and diff checks also passed on this isolated PR branch.

Give same-named clip exports their own files.

author: vbasky
body:

Keep each consolidation in its own audio file.

A second consolidate of the same track reused Audio Files/{name}.wav, and saving then skipped the rename because that path already belonged to the earlier source. New sources now take a free name, and a save splits sources that already share a path instead of overwriting one file.

author: vbasky
body:

Save a session copy without retargeting the open document.

author: vbasky
body:

Export MIDI controllers and honour the tracks filter.

file.export_midi copied notes only, so controller, pressure, and pitch-bend events were dropped, and the tracks parameter was ignored. The file now includes those events, and a tracks list limits the export. Naming only non-MIDI tracks is an error instead of exporting every other MIDI track.

Fixes #98

title: Keep going when the CLI's stdout is closed.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Keep going when the CLI's stdout is closed.

outln! treated a failed write as success and returned immediately, so run and script stopped before --bounce or --save whenever a pipe reader had gone away. A write error is now ignored and the exit code comes from the work itself.

Fixes #96

title: Treat dotted command ids as engine.execute in the CLI app shorthand.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Treat dotted command ids as engine.execute in the CLI app shorthand.

app used to leave every ui., engine., session., and app. method untouched, so engine.history, ui.theme, and session.new were sent as unknown control methods. Only the real control-channel methods stay methods. Every other dotted id is engine.execute.

title: Import multichannel audio onto a track of the same width.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Import multichannel audio onto a track of the same width.

A new track for an imported file was clamped to stereo, so a 5.1 file lost every channel past the left and right. The track now follows the file's channel count. Importing onto an existing track is unchanged.

Fixes #89

title: Restore full playback speed when transport stops.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Restore full playback speed when transport stops.

Half-Speed Playback stored 0.5 on the player, and a manual Stop left that rate in place, so the next ordinary Play stayed at half speed. Stopping now resets the player to 1.0. Half-speed itself still plays at 0.5, and a pass that ends on its own still returns to full speed.

Fixes #101

title: Keep clip gain when AudioSuite inverts or duplicates.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Keep clip gain when AudioSuite inverts or duplicates.

Both processes rendered a unity-gain file and then cleared the clip's gain and envelope, so the result was quieter than the clip the user heard. Invert and Duplicate now leave that gain on the new clip. Processes that bake a new level still write a unity-gain clip.

Fixes #88

title: Render a named bus when bouncing, and reject an unknown one.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Render a named bus when bouncing, and reject an unknown one.

file.bounce_mix advertised a source but always wrote the main mix, so an empty bus and a missing bus both succeeded with the whole mix.

Fixes #59

title: Bake varispeed into rendered clip gain, then stop stretching it again.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Bake varispeed into rendered clip gain, then stop stretching it again.

Clip gain and clip effects renders wrote the clip as it already sounded and left the old ratio in place, so the new file was stretched a second time and its tail went silent.

Fixes #92

title: Compensate for an aux insert's latency on the same block that measures it.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Compensate for an aux insert's latency on the same block that measures it.

The bounce probe read aux latency before the aux had processed, so a lookahead compressor shifted the export and dropped audio at the end of the range.

Fixes #103

title: Convert only the selected volume automation into clip gain.
author: vbasky
body:
Split from #114 so this can be reviewed on its own.

Convert only the selected volume automation into clip gain.

The command wrote the lane onto the whole clip and cleared points only inside the selection, so the old curve still played and the clip got quieter on both sides. The selection now holds the fader, with anchors so the surrounding curve stays put. Volume and clip-gain windows take their end value from the last sample inside the window, so a breakpoint on the next sample does not ramp the audio before it.

Fixes #104

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping audio files, MIDI files, or session projects from desktop file managers onto SoundCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `SOUNDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `SOUNDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p soundcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Open Edit and Mix simultaneously with Tile and Cascade

Opening Window > Mix currently replaces Edit in the only main window. This change keeps Edit/Timeline and Mix/Mixer open simultaneously as independent views of one session, and reduces the stalls caused by rapidly switching between them with Cmd+= / Ctrl+=.

Paint only visible Mixer strips and borrow session/plugin data instead of cloning tracks during drawing. Read shared meter snapshots once per root tick.
- On macOS, temporarily hide a view fully covered by the other main view to avoid Metal drawable waits during focus changes, retaining its viewport and session. Restore visibility before switching to it. Partially overlapping and tiled windows remain visible together; VSync remains enabled.
- Support Tile, Tile Horizontal, Tile Vertical and Cascade within the original workspace, accounting for UI zoom and decorations. Keep narrow tiles usable with scrolling toolbar/Mixer and adaptive sidebars.
- Close either view while retaining the other and the session, including root-window close requests; reopen closed views and process commands while occluded/minimized.

- `cargo xtask ci` on the local implementation and …

title: Add plugins from the Edit window's Inserts columns.
author: TaleWarden
body:
Add plugins from the Edit window's Inserts columns.

title: Play built-in instruments with their saved parameters (#152)
author: joshuamontierth
body:
Fixes #152.

## Cause

The mixer never pushed a built-in instrument's session parameters into the plugin. Inserts get `apply_params` before every block. The instrument branch of the strip render went straight to `schedule_notes` + `process`, so the instance kept its factory defaults. Every saved built-in instrument parameter was ignored, not only `level` (cutoff, envelopes, drum tuning...). This affected bounces and realtime playback alike, since both use `MixEngine`.

## Fix (`crates/mix/src/lib.rs`)

- **Per block:** the instrument branch calls `apply_params` for built-in instruments, the same way inserts do. Only changed values are pushed, so session edits still reach a live instance.
- **At creation:** `SlotCtx::make` sets a new built-in instance's session parameters and resets it. Without this, smoothed parameters (the instruments' `level`) start at the default and glide to the saved value over the first ~20 ms. The new test fails at sample 1 without this step. This also applies to built-in inserts. A Gain insert at −12 dB now starts the bounce at −12 dB instead of fading down from 0 dB.
- **Automation:** `apply_params` found plugin automation lanes with `u8::try_from(i).unwrap_or(0)`, so `INSTRUMENT_SLOT` (`usize::MAX`) would have read insert **a**'s lanes. It now matches insert slots only. Inserts behave exactly as before (their index always fits in `u8`).
- **Hosted (CLAP/VST3/AU) instruments are unchanged.** Their sound comes from the restored state and their own editor, and `instrument.params` isn't kept in step with them (the plugin window says so). Pushing those values would overwrite a loaded patch.

## Tests

- `built_in_instruments_play_their_session_params`: Subtractive Synth and Drum Synth at −6 and −12 dB. The −12 render must equal the −6 render × 10^(−6/20) on every sample (1e-6). A slot-a `plugin:a:level` automation lane on the −12 track must not leak into the instrument.
- `hosted_instruments_keep_their_own_sound`: an adopted third-party instrum…

title: Web: open, import, save and export files in the browser (fixes #63, fixes #64)
author: natocool2
body:
Fixes #63, fixes #64.

## The problem

In the browser the web app could not reach any file. File > Open Session…, Import > Audio… and Import > MIDI… showed a text box for a path that a page can't read, and every save or export failed with «operation not supported on this platform». Work was lost when the tab closed.

## Changes (web only; native builds keep files and session folders as before)

- **Picking and dropping files.** `apps/soundcraft-web`: the path prompts of Open Session, Import Audio and Import MIDI are replaced by the browser's file picker (`rfd::AsyncFileDialog`). Files dropped on the page open (`.scraftz`/`.scraft`) or import (audio, MIDI) by extension. Files are read as bytes into an inbox that is drained on the next frame. Imports go through `io::import_audio_bytes`/`import_midi_bytes` and push one undo step each, like the import commands.
- **A session is one file in the browser: a bundle `<name>.scraftz`.** It is a zip with stored entries holding `<name>.scraft` plus `Audio Files/*.wav` (32-bit float), the same layout as a session folder. `io::session_bundle` writes it and `io::open_session_bytes` opens a bundle or a bare `.scraft`, whose audio is then reported missing as `open_session` does. Bundles are treated as hostile input: the entry count (10 000) and unpacked size (4 GiB) are capped, and declared entry sizes are never read past. On wasm, `save_session` saves a bundle.
- **Every single-file output works in the browser.** Save, Save As Template, Bounce, MIDI/score/text exports and track presets go through a new `io::write_file`. Natively it writes the file; in the browser it hands the bytes to a delivery hook (`io::set_deliver`) that only the web app installs (a hidden `<a download>`). Folder outputs (stems, clip exports) are still not available on the web.
- **Save As in the browser** suggests `<name>.scraftz` instead of a folder path.
- New dependency: `zip` (MIT), `default-features = false` (stored entries only, no compression crates).

title: Tag MP3 files with ID3v2.4: text, cover and chapters
author: Multipad-cyber
body:
## What

- **`soundcraft-audio-io::id3`** (new, pure Rust, no dependencies):
  - an ID3v2.4 encoder for text (`T***`), `TXXX`, `COMM`, URL (`W***`), `WXXX`, `APIC` (picture), `CHAP` and `CTOC` (chapter) frames, all text in UTF-8;
  - a frame reader (v2.3/v2.4);
  - `strip_id3v2()` and `retag()`, which replaces a file's leading tag and leaves the audio untouched.
- **New command `file.tag_mp3`** `{path, out?, title?, artist?, album?, album_artist?, genre?, date?, track?, disc?, language?, comment?, url?, cover?, chapters?, offset?}`:
  - `cover` is a JPEG or PNG file, embedded as the front cover.
  - `chapters` is either a list (`[{start, end?, title, url?, image?}]`, times in seconds) or `"markers"`, which turns the session's memory locations into chapters. Chapters run to the next chapter, or to the end of the file when the MP3 can be probed.
  - It writes to `<out>.tagging` and then renames, so a failed write never truncates the original.
- **Docs:** a row in `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

## Why

SoundCraft reads MP3 but couldn't write any metadata into one. MP3 export is still missing (G-21), so for now this tags MP3s encoded elsewhere. It's also the base for podcast chapter export. Once an MP3 encoder lands, `encode_id3v2()` can prepend the tag directly.

## Robustness

- No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or `unsafe` outside tests; sizes are checked.
- The syncsafe size field is enforced (tags over 256 MiB are rejected), as are a 255-chapter table-of-contents limit, 16 MiB image and 4 GiB input caps, and element-id validation.
- The reader is tested against every truncation of a tag and against an oversized size field.
- `file.tag_mp3` takes a path, so the hostile-params proptest skips it like the other file commands; bad input is covered by its own tests instead.

## Tests

title: Title-bar performance readout: audio load, RAM, FPS
author: tuttopassastudios
body:
Shows `AUDIO 1.5%   RAM 166 MB   FPS 56` at the top right of the window.

## What
- **macOS:** the content runs under a transparent title bar (egui's `with_fullsize_content_view` + hidden title/titlebar) and SoundCraft draws the strip: title after the system window buttons, readout on the right. Dragging the strip moves the window; double-click zooms. When narrow, the title shortens to the session name, then hides, so the readout stays.
- **Windows/Linux:** the readout sits on the right of the egui menu bar.
- **Audio load** (`Player::audio_load`): callback time over the audio duration it produced, averaged over 100 ms. Per-callback figures swing wildly because the mix renders whole 512-sample blocks into smaller device buffers. Yellow at 60 %, red at 80 %. No allocation or blocking added to the callback; untimed on wasm.
- **RAM:** process resident memory via the `memory-stats` crate (MIT/Apache-2.0; not built for wasm).
- **FPS:** frames drawn per second. egui redraws on demand, so idle reads low; a repaint every 0.5 s keeps the readout live.
- Agents: `ui.inspect` now includes `perf: {audio_load, ram_bytes, fps}`.

## Testing
- New tests: windowed load publication (incl. empty buffers), readout resampling (fps, NaN load, clock going backwards), text formatting.
- Locally green: `fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `xtask assets`, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, playback + ui-egui test suites.

title: fix(mix): push an instrument's stored params to its plugin before each block (#152)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

`process_strip` for instrument tracks calls `inst.plugin.process(...)` directly but never `apply_params(...)`, so the values stored on the track's `instrument.params` (e.g. `level = -12 dB`) never reach the live plugin instance. Both `s2` and `s3` (loudest) bounces are sample-identical: the plugin keeps its defaults.

Fix: call `apply_params(inst, ins, t, INSTRUMENT_SLOT, pos)` before each instrument's `process()` — the same pattern the inserts loop uses for non-instrument slots. The active document's units still get set via the existing `set_document_units(default_units())` path; this PR only addresses the per-block param push.

`crates/mix/src/lib.rs`: one added line in `process_strip`.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across SoundCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for SoundCraft.

title: Keyboard shortcuts: Cut/Copy/Paste and Delete, Pro Tools keys and a shortcut editor
author: grovebit
body:
Several everyday keys did nothing in the desktop app, many Pro Tools shortcuts were missing, and shortcuts couldn't be changed.

- Cmd+X/C/V (Ctrl+X/C/V on Windows and Linux) cut, copy and paste from the keyboard. egui reports them only as clipboard events, and Cmd+V only while the clipboard holds text, so a V release whose press never arrived also counts as Cmd+V. The system clipboard is never written.

- Setup > Keyboard Shortcuts is now an editor (fixes #24): commands grouped by menu, search, and new keys set by pressing them. It asks before taking a key another command has, and offers Reset and Reset All. Choices are saved with the UI preferences and show in the menus.

title: Let the desktop app sleep when idle or covered
author: grovebit
body:
The desktop app sent the window title to egui on every frame, and each viewport command asks for another frame, so it never slept: 35–43% of a CPU core and 13–20% GPU per idle window on a 120 Hz Mac, and a full core while the window was covered.

- The title is sent only when it changes. It's remembered in egui's context data, because X11 and Wayland can't read a title back.
- An idle window still wakes once a second, or every 30 ms while a plugin editor is open, for the work that only runs on frames: autosave, the macOS menu bar, and plugin editors, which are native windows egui never hears from.
- Playback and falling meters ask for the next frame from `ui()`, which eframe skips for a covered or minimized window, so a hidden window no longer spins a core.
- Autosave is timed by the wall clock, so it also runs while the window is hidden; egui's clock stands still then.

Tested: on a 120 Hz MacBook (release build, demo session, audio off), an idle Edit window went from 35–43% CPU and 13–20% GPU to 1.5% and 0.4%, and a covered window, idle or playing, from ~100% CPU to 0%. fmt, clippy, assets, layers, wasm and 545 tests pass, including new ones for the title, the wake-ups and autosave while hidden, apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: i18n: add Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese and German menu catalogs
author: pechnikov2026-star

## Summary

Introduces the interface translation infrastructure for SoundCraft from scratch and adds **five complete menu catalogs: Russian (ru), Spanish (es), French (fr), Portuguese pt-BR (pt), German (de)** — 565 menu labels each. Following the EffectCraft precedent, these are **menu-only catalogs**: panel and dialog strings keep English for now.

## Changes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs` — new module: a thread-local `CURRENT` language, a per-language catalog (565 entries in a `(&str, &str)` const array per module), `tr()` lookup with English fallback, `resolve()` for the `auto`/code preference, system-locale detection via `sys-locale`
- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/{ru,fr,de,es,pt}.rs` — five new catalog modules (565 entries each)

- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` — `mod i18n;`, a `language: String` field in `UiState` (default "auto", `#[serde(default)]`)

title: macOS: build the DMG with hdiutil create so the app passes codesign --strict
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #176.

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` puts a `com.apple.FinderInfo` on every file it writes into the image. The app is signed before that, so SoundCraft.app inside the released DMG, and any `ditto` copy of it, fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` with "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed". The script only re-checked the DMG's own signature after imaging, so this went unnoticed.

This is the fix PdfCraft and LightCraft already shipped (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/823, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/959), ported to `packaging/macos/package.sh`:

- The image is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies and can hit "Resource busy" on CI runners, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses.
- `xattr -cr` on the bundle before signing, so nothing picked up during the build ends up under the signature.
- After the DMG is signed, the script mounts it read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside and on a `ditto` copy of it, plus `spctl --assess` on the copy when notarizing. Any failure stops the release and prints the app's xattrs.
- The volume name stays `SoundCraft` and `.DS_Store` / `.background` are copied as before, so the window layout is unchanged.
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` no longer says the DMG is built with `makehybrid`.

Testing: I don't have a Mac, so this was not run. I checked the script with `bash -n` and shellcheck 0.11 (clean) and compared it line by line with the PdfCraft change, which was verified on macOS (the new gate passes, and fails with the old `makehybrid` lines put back). The release workflow's macOS job is what will actually exercise it; the new check after imaging makes that job fail loudly if something is off.

title: Windows: compile DX12 shaders with FXC
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Windows the app quit right after the window appeared with "Parent device is lost". wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` it finds on the DLL search path. SoundCraft ships none, and without a matching `dxil.dll` DXC warns that the DXIL is unsigned. wgpu treats that warning as a compile error, its indirect-validation pipeline fails and the device is lost.

The fix sets the DX12 compiler to FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) in `graphics::configure`, next to the existing DX12-only backend default. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still overrides it for troubleshooting, the same way `WGPU_BACKEND` overrides the backends. This is the same change as storytold/cadcraft#613 (and storytold/lightcraft#484, storytold/gridcraft#382). The README's Windows troubleshooting section mentions it.

Tested with a unit test in graphics.rs that starts from `Auto` and checks `configure` leaves FXC. It failed before the change and passes now, and a second test checks an explicit compiler choice is kept. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 6 steps).

Not verified: I built on Linux only, where the `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` call in main.rs isn't compiled (no Windows target installed here), so Windows CI is what checks that line. Nobody ran it on a Windows machine.

Fixes #185

title: Consolidate covers the whole edit selection (#164)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Consolidate clamped its range with `bounded_to_track`, which stops one second after the last clip on the track. On an empty track a 0-5 s selection gave a 1 s clip, and a 2-7 s selection gave no clip at all while the command still reported success.

`io::consolidate` no longer uses that bound. It turns the selection into a start and length in samples once and uses the same range for the render, the clear and the new clip, so it never clears more than it places. Empty tracks get a silent clip the length of the selection. If the selection is longer than the render cap (`MAX_RENDER_SAMPLES` divided by the track's channel count, about 93 minutes for stereo at 48 kHz), the command returns an error and leaves the session as it was, instead of placing a shorter clip.

Prepare DPE tracks also calls this function. It now applies `bounded_to_track` itself, so each track still consolidates to its own material plus a second, as before. Strip Silence, transient detection and audio-to-MIDI keep the bound too.

Tests in `crates/engine/tests/consolidate_selection.rs`:
- empty tracks with a 0-5 s and a 2-7 s selection get one clip each covering the selection
- a 1 s clip with a 0-5 s selection becomes one 5 s clip that keeps the audio
- multi-track consolidate with a clip on one track is one undo step, and undo restores every track
- a selection over the render cap is refused and nothing changes
- Prepare DPE with existing clips gives the same lengths as before

Five of these fail when the old clamp is put back. The Prepare DPE one passes either way, since it checks that the old behaviour stays.

I ran fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, the tests for soundcraft-engine, the wasm check for soundcraft-engine and `xtask layers`. I left the full workspace run to CI. I haven't tried it by hand in the app.

Fixes #164

title: control server: bound request lines and concurrent connections
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs` (the opt-in `--control` loopback channel) read request lines with `BufRead::lines`, which buffers an entire line before anything checks its size, and spawned one thread per accepted connection with no limit.

- **Bounded line reads:** each line is read with `take(MAX_LINE + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`. A line longer than `MAX_LINE` = 256 MiB (generous, since requests can carry documents or media as base64) gets an error reply and the connection is closed, without buffering the rest. Previously there was no line limit at all.
- **Connection cap:** at most `MAX_CONNECTIONS` = 16 connections are served at once; further ones get `{"ok": false, "error": "too many control connections"}` and are closed. A slot is released when its connection ends, including if its thread can't start or panics (`Drop` guard).

Everything else in request handling is unchanged (blank lines skipped, same replies, same timeouts). The approach mirrors DesignCraft's control server.

## Tests

New tests in `control_server.rs`:
- `lines_are_read_up_to_the_limit`: line at the limit accepted, CRLF stripped, final line without newline read, then end of stream
- `an_overlong_line_is_refused_without_reading_the_rest`: at most limit+1 bytes buffered, remainder left unread
- `requests_are_answered_with_their_ids`: end to end over a loopback socket with a stand-in UI
- `extra_connections_are_refused`: the 17th concurrent connection gets the error line

## How this was verified

On my Windows machine, Smart App Control blocks a dependency's build script (`parking_lot_core`), so I couldn't build the full app locally. Instead I compiled **this exact file**, unmodified, as a module of a small harness crate with stand-ins for `egui::Context` and `ControlRequest`. All four new tests pass there, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic` is clean on it. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes in the repo.
