title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: File › Open Recent: the last 10 sessions, newest first
author: woodgrain816
body:
Pro Tools has **File › Open Recent**. SoundCraft had no way back to a session except browsing for it, which is slow for sessions on a network share.

## What it does

- **File › Open Recent ▸**, right under File › Open: the last 10 sessions, newest first.
  - Each entry reads `name — folder`, with the full path on hover.
- A session that has moved or been deleted shows greyed out as **(missing)** instead of failing on click.
  - While the menu is open, existence is re-checked at most every 3 s. A path on a network share costs a round trip per file, so this isn't done every frame.
- **Clear Recent** empties the list.
- Opening goes through `dialogs::run_or_ask`, so unsaved changes are asked about first, as with File › Open.

## How

- **Storage:** the list lives in `UiState.recent_sessions` and is saved with the rest of `ui.json`. An older `ui.json` without the field still loads (`#[serde(default)]`, with a test for it).
- **Recording:** entries come from `Engine::path` whenever it changes, checked once per frame in `SoundApp::logic`, not from the individual commands. One rule then covers every way a session gets a path: menu, control channel, MCP, a dropped file, Save As.
- **Saving:** the desktop host saves `ui.json` as soon as the list changes (`SoundApp::take_recent_changed`), instead of only in `on_exit`. The list matters most after a crash, and a crash skips `on_exit`.
- **Duplicates:** on Windows, paths are compared case-insensitively and with either separator, so the same session isn't listed twice.
- **New module:** `crates/ui-egui/src/recent.rs`, with 4 unit tests (ordering, de-duplication and cap, Windows path matching, labels, old `ui.json`).

## Known gap

The **macOS system menu bar** (`apps/soundcraft/src/native_menu.rs`) doesn't show the submenu yet. The egui menu bar on Windows and Linux does. A dynamic submenu in the muda menu needs rebuilding when the list changes. I can't test that without a Mac, so it's left for a follow-up rather than shipped un…

title: Stream bounces to disk and keep the app responsive while bouncing
author: grovebit
body:
Bounce Mix renders the whole mix in memory, silently stops at 2^29 samples (about 93 minutes of stereo at 48 kHz), and freezes the app until the file is written.

- Bounces (main mix, a bus and stems) are written block by block to `<name>.part` and renamed when complete; in the browser they're encoded in memory and downloaded as before.
- Bounce Mix renders a slice per frame behind a progress window with Cancel (or Esc); the Task Manager lists it.
- A plugin's reported latency is capped at 2^20 samples, so a bogus value can't stall offline renders.
- New, Open, Close and Revert wait until the bounce finishes or is cancelled.

Tested: 689 tests pass (6 VST3 tests skipped locally because they load this machine's installed plugins), plus fmt, clippy, layers, assets and wasm; a 100-minute bounce writes all 288,000,000 frames with 84 MB peak memory.

title: Preserve audio and history when healing ordinary clip separations
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Heal Separation plans compatible audio joins before changing the document. Accepted joins keep the left clip identity, remap selections and form one Undo step. Refused or empty operations preserve the document Arc, revision, dirty state and pending Redo without sorting playlists. Incompatible pairs report explicit reasons.

The planner preserves current upstream support for source-contiguous cut gaps, matching positive stretch factors and gain-envelope joins. It adds checked source-length and envelope-offset arithmetic while refusing malformed data, fades, locks, groups, loop identities and recognized per-clip processing references. Exact rendered-sample equality is covered for adjacent unprocessed joins; gap joins deliberately restore removed source material, and processed joins retain upstream behavior.

The scope is audio Heal planning and command application.

Validation after rebase onto `aa74bff` (2026-10-24):

- Exact-source isolated Linux `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed all seven gates: formatting, strict Clippy, workspace tests, doctests, assets, layers and WASM. Test summaries report 1,289 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing ignored and 0 filtered.
- macOS workspace/all-target compilation passed on Rust 1.95.0. All 24 focused Heal cases passed, including 11 existing library cases and 13 integration cases; strict engine/all-target Clippy also passed.

title: fix(macos): allow UADx plugins in signed builds
author: IfritisZ
body:
Signed macOS builds can discover UADx plugins but macOS kills the host during their runtime initialization with `CODESIGNING / Invalid Page`. The hardened-runtime entitlements currently declare that SoundCraft loads no unsigned code, although it hosts third-party plugins.

Allow libraries signed by other developers (`disable-library-validation`) and the executable memory used by the UADx/PACE runtime (`allow-unsigned-executable-memory`). Keep the hardened runtime and executable-page protection enabled. Both exceptions are documented in the plist; no plugin binaries, license checks, or system-wide security settings are changed.

Validation:
- A/B test of the same signed host: library validation exception alone fails; adding `allow-jit` still fails; adding `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` succeeds.
- Against the unmodified `main` host source with this entitlement file, all nine previously failing UADx plugins load, process non-silent finite stereo audio at 44.1/48/96 kHz, save/restore state, and attach/detach their editors: Brigade Chorus, Dream, Lion, Paradise, Pultec EQP-1A, Ruby, Showtime, LA-2A, and 1176.
- `plutil -lint` and strict code-signature verification pass.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, Clippy, 685 tests (one existing ignored), assets, layers, and WASM. For this run, a process-local sandbox hid installed VST3 directories because an unrelated leftover AmpliTube installation crashes the in-process enumeration test. The UADx probes above ran separately with plugin access enabled.

Native validation was performed on Apple Silicon with local ad-hoc signing. Developer ID notarization and Intel runtime behavior have not been tested. The change contains only the shared macOS entitlement plist.

title: VST3: hand host-set parameter values to the controller before saving state
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #257.

`Vst3Plugin::set_param` only queues the normalized value for the processor and never tells the controller. For a parameter the processor doesn't keep in its state (the fixture's Freq), processing can't bring the value over either, so `save_state` snapshotted the controller's old 0.5 and the restored instance read back ~632 Hz. `set_param` can run on the audio thread, so it doesn't call the controller now either: it marks the value as unsynced, and `save_state`, which already calls into the controller for `getState`, pushes the marked values with `setParamNormalized` just before taking the snapshot. A state load clears the marks. I picked the save as the sync point because it doesn't add any controller call on a thread that wasn't already making one. Happy to switch to a different sync point (e.g. an explicit main-thread flush) if you'd prefer.

Validation:
- `host_set_controller_param_survives_state_round_trip` (fixture_e2e, the issue's scenario: set Gain 1.5 and Freq 200, process on another thread, save, load into a fresh instance): fails on main (`Some(632.4555)`), passes here; also run alone with `--test-threads=1`
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-vst3-host --test fixture_e2e` (9 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-vst3-host --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Make clip.loop / clip.unloop self-consistent (loop_id tag)
author: Claudio911015
body:
Part of #273

## Problem
`clip.loop` creates independent duplicates, and `clip.unloop` detected a loop only by comparing the content of back-to-back clips. Once the source clip's MIDI notes were edited, the content no longer matched the copies and `clip.unloop` failed with `the selection is not a looped clip` on a loop that `clip.loop` had just made.

## Fix
- New optional `Clip::loop_id` (`#[serde(default)]`, so existing sessions load unchanged).
- `clip.loop` tags the origin and all its copies with one shared id.
- `clip.unloop` treats adjacent equal-length clips with the same `loop_id` as one loop; the old content comparison remains as a fallback for untagged loops. `mode=flatten` clears the tag so the copies become ordinary independent clips.

## Not in this PR
Edits to the source clip still do **not** propagate to the loop copies: that needs linked/shared clip content (a larger data-model change), so the second half of #273 stays open. This PR only makes the loop/unloop pair consistent.

## Tests
- `unloop_recognises_loops_after_source_edit`: loops a MIDI clip, edits the source note, then unloops. Fails without the change with `the selection is not a looped clip` (verified), passes with it.
- `unloop_flatten_turns_loop_into_independent_clips`.
- Ran `cargo test -p soundcraft-model -p soundcraft-engine` (all pass), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-model -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean).
- Not run: full `cargo xtask ci`, other crates, UI.

title: Mix: a bus bounce compensates the aux returns onto it (#246)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #246

## Cause

With Delay Compensation on, the mix aligns every track to the slowest track insert and every aux return to the slowest aux return, and the main mix drops the sum of the two (`MixEngine::latency`). `render_bus` (used by `file.bounce_mix` with a `source` bus) dropped only `track_latency`, which is right for a bus that only tracks write to. A bus that an aux *returns onto* is also delayed by the aux return's latency, and nothing removed it: bouncing bus B in the issue's routing (track → bus A → aux with a 5 ms lookahead compressor → bus B) came out 240 frames late, so the last impulse fell past the requested end.

A bus fed by both tracks and an aux had a second problem: tracks routed to the main mix wait for the slowest aux return (`out_extra`), but tracks routed to a bus did not, so on a bus where both arrive the direct signal was 240 frames ahead of the aux return.

## Fix

- The engine records which busses an aux returns onto (`aux_fed`) and the slowest aux return (`aux_latency`) each block.
- `render_bus` drops `bus_latency(bus)`: the track latency, plus the aux latency when an aux returns onto that bus.
- A track whose output is such a bus waits for the aux latency, the way a track routed to the main mix already does (`route_strip` applies `out_extra` to `Route::Bus` as well as `Route::Main`; it is zero for every other bus).

The main mix, busses no aux returns onto and sessions without Delay Compensation behave as before.

## Verified

The issue's fixture (impulses at 0, 2048, 8000; compressor with 5 ms lookahead on the aux), bounce of bus B over 0–8192, positions of the impulses:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| bus B after the aux | `[240, 2288]` (last impulse cut off) | `[0, 2048, 8000]`, identical to the no-insert control |
| bus A before the aux, no-insert control, main mix | `[0, 2048, 8000]` | `[0, 2048, 8000]` |
| bus B with a second track routed straight to it | `[0, 240, 2048, 2288, 8000]` | `[0, 2048, 8000]`, each at 0…

title: Mix: delay compensation covers the master faders' inserts (#351)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #351 (the bounce delay, point 1 of the report)

## Cause

The master faders process the main mix after every track and aux return has been summed, so a lookahead insert on a master fader delays the whole main mix. `MixEngine::latency`, the compensation latency that `render_range` drops from the head of a bounce, was `slowest track + slowest aux return` and left the master inserts out. The Maximizer reports its lookahead (`latency()`, 71 samples at 48 kHz), but the bounce kept it: the voice came out 71 samples later than in the same mix without the Maximizer, as measured in the report (+69 vs −2 samples).

## Fix

The latency of the master faders' inserts is now part of the mix latency: each master strip's insert latency is read before the block is routed (`note_insert_latency`, as for aux returns) and added up (the faders run one after the other), when Delay Compensation is on. With it off, nothing changes.

## Verified

New `crates/mix/tests/master_insert_latency.rs`: one stereo track with an impulse at sample 2000 routed to the main mix, a master fader with a Maximizer, `render_range` over 12,000 frames:

| | peak of the bounce |
|---|---|
| no master insert (control) | 2000 |
| `main`, Maximizer on the master | 2071 (+71, the number in the report) |
| this branch | 2000 |

- `a_master_insert_with_lookahead_does_not_delay_the_bounce` fails on `main` (2071 vs 2000) and passes here; it also checks that `MixEngine::latency` now includes the Maximizer's lookahead and that with Delay Compensation off nothing is dropped (the peak is 71 later again).
- `master_inserts_without_latency_change_nothing` (a Gain on the master) is a control that passes both ways.

The 32 `soundcraft-mix` lib tests pass and `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- Point 2 of the report (the Maximizer's ceiling is a sample-peak ceiling, so the true peak ends up above it) is a separate change: it needs an oversampled true-peak mode in the Maximizer, or a statement in the UI and docs.
- R…

title: Engine: mix.instrument takes the instrument's parameters and refuses unknown fields (#265)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #265

## Cause

`mix.instrument` reads `track` and `plugin` and nothing else. Every other field is ignored, so synth settings written beside `plugin` (`cutoff`, `amp_sustain`, `level`…) came back as `ok`, `track.save_preset` read the instrument's own (default) values, and the render never changed, as in the report. The command that does set one parameter, `mix.instrument_param`, works; what was missing is a way to pass the settings together with the instrument, and an error for anything the command does not read.

## Fix

- `mix.instrument` takes `params: {id: value}` for the built-in instrument. The parameters are validated before anything is changed (an unknown id for that plugin and a value that is not a number are errors; values are clamped into the parameter's range), then applied on top of the instrument's defaults, the same way `mix.sampler_load` takes `params`.
- Any other field is refused with a message that says where the setting belongs: `unknown field `cutoff`: an instrument's parameters go in `params` ({id: value}), or one at a time in mix.instrument_param`. `track`, `tracks`, `plugin` and `params` are the fields the command reads (the app sends `track` and `plugin`).
- The command's parameter text now says so.

## Verified

CLI on `main` (a subtractive synth track, one A7 note, 2 s bounce, `mix.instrument` with `cutoff` beside `plugin`): the command returned success and the bounce was identical to the default (−27.35 LUFS). The same note with `mix.instrument_param` `cutoff` 200 gave −50.0 LUFS and with 12000 gave −24.5 LUFS, so the parameter itself reaches the render; only `mix.instrument` dropped it.

New test `parameters_given_with_the_instrument_reach_the_render_and_unknown_fields_are_refused` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/instrument.rs`:

- `params: {cutoff: 200}` is stored and a high note through it is at least 3× quieter (RMS) than with `cutoff: 12000`; a huge value is clamped to 20000 and the other parameters stay at their defaults.
- A field …

title: Keep end and length in midi.new_clip when start is omitted
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #411.

`midi.new_clip` reads its range through the shared `range_param` helper, which only looked at `end`/`length` when `start` was given; without `start` it fell back to the edit selection and the clip got the 1-bar default, as @Sirli01 narrowed down in the issue. Now an `end` or `length` without `start` counts from the start of the edit selection (the insertion point, which is 0 in the issue's script), so `{"track":1,"length":192000}` gives 0..192000. Since the helper is shared, the same fix reaches the other range commands (e.g. `event.insert_time` with only `length` had the same hole). Two cases that used to be silently resolved now fail with a clear error instead: `end` and `length` together that disagree (before, `length` was ignored), and, without `start`, a range that ends before the insertion point. An explicit `start` with an `end` before it is still accepted and swapped as before, since UI drags may pass the two ends in either order. Happy to switch to a stricter or more lenient rule if you prefer. The rule is also written down in `docs/control-protocol.md` and in the command's params doc.

Validation:
- `cmd::midi::tests::new_clip_keeps_length_and_end_without_start`: fails on main (gets 0..96000, the 1-bar default, instead of 12000..42000), passes here
- `cmd::midi::tests::new_clip_rejects_inconsistent_ranges`: fails on main (`{"end":6000}` is accepted), passes here
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Drag across checkboxes to check or uncheck several (#399)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
Fixes #399

### What changed

Press on a checkbox and drag over its neighbours. Each checkbox the pointer goes over takes the new state of the first one, until you release the button. A click toggles one checkbox, as before. Same design as VectorCraft (#1600) and PhotoCraft (#3521).

- SoundCraft had no shared checkbox, so this adds `widgets::checkbox`: egui's checkbox plus the drag. All 15 `ui.checkbox` calls in ui-egui use it (Group, New Session, Bounce, Score Setup, Automation, Playback Engine, send options, Beat Detective, Video, UI Customization).
- Only checkboxes the pointer can see are set. Rows scrolled out of a list, or under another window, stay as they are. A list scrolls along when the drag reaches its edge.
- The label takes `impl Into<WidgetText>`, so the translation PRs (#143, #302, #68, #337) only need `ui.checkbox(` → `crate::widgets::checkbox(ui, ` on the lines they already change.
- SoundCraft has no mixed (dash) checkboxes, so that part of the issue doesn't apply.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: a new row and a revision entry.

### Trade-offs (as in the other apps)

- A drag also sets neighbouring checkboxes that mean different things, such as Mute and Pre-fader in the send options. Checkboxes that run a command (send options, Automation, Delay compensation) make one undo step each.
- On touch, dragging on top of a checkbox no longer scrolls its list. The scroll bar and the gaps between rows still do.

### How to test

1. Select a track, then Track › Group... (Cmd+G).
2. Press on the checkbox of an unselected track under Tracks and drag down over a few more. Make sure they are all checked.
3. Drag back up from a checked box. Make sure they are all unchecked.
4. Drag down past the bottom of the list. Make sure the list scrolls and only the rows you pass change.
5. Click one checkbox. Make sure only that one changes. Click Cancel.

### Checks

- New tests: four in `widgets::tests` (drag sets, drag unchecks and stops at release, hidden rows untouched, a cli…

title: Double-click a MIDI clip with the Grabber to open it in the MIDI Editor
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #186 ("Clips on MIDI tracks cannot be … opened in a MIDI editor"). Double-clicking a MIDI clip in the Edit window only selected it, so the MIDI Editor had to be opened from the Window menu or the dock tabs. In Pro Tools, a Grabber double-click on a MIDI clip opens it in a MIDI Editor.

- A Grabber double-click on a MIDI or instrument clip selects it and opens the docked MIDI Editor on it. An editor that's already open switches to the clip.
- With the Smart Tool, the clip's lower half (Grabber) opens the editor; the upper half (Selector) still only selects the clip, as in Pro Tools.
- Audio clips are unchanged.

title: Tab to Transient: every selected track, Alt+Tab back, Shift+Tab extends
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #186 ("Tab does not navigate to audio transients"). Tab found transients only on the first selected track and only going forward, re-analysed from the cursor to the track's end on every press, and Shift+Tab did nothing.

- Tab and Alt+Tab (Option+Tab on a Mac, Ctrl+Tab on Windows and Linux) move to the next or previous clip start, end or sync point on the selected tracks; Shift+Tab and Alt+Shift+Tab (Ctrl+Shift+Tab) extend the selection, as in Pro Tools. One new command, `edit.tab`, does it.
- With Tab to Transient on, the stops also include the transients on every selected audio track and the notes on MIDI and Instrument tracks.
- Transients are analysed in fixed 10-second blocks and cached: a press takes 0.5 ms across the demo's five audio tracks (43 ms uncached).
- The Tab to Transient button gets its own icon instead of the Selector's.

Tested: fmt, clippy and the 368 engine and ui-egui tests pass on current main, 4 of them new (clip boundaries and sync points, the same hits both ways across analysis blocks, hits on any selected track and MIDI notes, Shift+Tab from the keyboard).

title: Transient detection: find quiet and legato onsets, place them on the attack
author: grovebit
body:
Tab to Transient, Separate at Transients and Beat Detective missed most onsets that weren't the loudest around, and put a note that starts over a ringing note 25–35 ms early, in the previous note's tail.

- The threshold no longer depends on the loudest hit in the analysed audio, so quiet hits count and the result doesn't change with where the analysis starts.
- Spectral flux on 24 bands per octave ignores vibrato and chorus, and stereo content that cancels in mono still counts.
- Each onset lands on the attack's step edge, 0.3–0.5 ms before percussive attacks.
- On 29 synthetic cases with known onsets, the F-measure went from 0.658 to 0.977: 1398 onsets found instead of 870, with 5 false ones instead of 315.

Tested: fmt, clippy, wasm and the 455 dsp, engine and ui-egui tests pass on current main, 6 of them new (each fails on the old detector).

title: Fall back to a system Hangul font so Korean names render in the UI
author: Momentum96
body:
Korean session, file, track and clip names were drawn as tofu boxes: none of the UI font
families (egui defaults + system Helvetica/Segoe/DejaVu) has Hangul, regardless of the
interface language.

Following the maintainer's guidance on #141 (system fonts at runtime, nothing bundled),
this does the Korean part only:

- Linux/BSD: `fc-match "sans-serif:lang=ko"`, accepted only if the match lists `ko`
  (fc-match otherwise returns a Latin best match), then Noto Sans CJK KR (ttc face 1) /
  NanumGothic paths.
- macOS: Apple SD Gothic Neo, then AppleGothic.
- Windows: Malgun Gothic, then Gulim.

The face found is appended to every font family as `system-hangul`, so Latin text keeps
its current fonts. Loaded once with the other system fonts, honours
`SOUNDCRAFT_NO_SYSTEM_FONTS`, skips files over 64 MiB, and degrades to the current
behaviour when no Korean font is installed. wasm is unchanged (no system fonts).

Tests: a candidate-list test, and a glyph-coverage test that every family draws Hangul
(skips when the system has no Korean font).

title: MIDI Editor: holding a piano key or a note plays it on the instrument (#373)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #373.

In the MIDI Editor, holding a piano key now plays that pitch on the track's instrument until you let go, and sliding across the keys plays each one. Holding a note plays it at its velocity, and as you drag the note up or down you hear the pitch it's moving to. This works with the transport stopped or playing.

- **Playback:** `Player::note(track, pitch, velocity)` sends a note-on or note-off (velocity 0) to the audio thread. The callback keeps rendering while a note is held and for 2 s after it's released, so the release can ring out. When nothing is auditioned, it stays silent and idle as before.
- **Mix:** `MixEngine::live_note` passes the note to the strip's instrument. While stopped (`monitor_only`), instruments now run without their clips instead of being skipped. A position that stays still while stopped is no longer treated as a seek, which would have cut off the held note on every block.
- **UI:** `midi_editor.rs` replaces the placeholder comment. Any note still sounding is released as soon as the mouse button comes up.

Also adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry (`sync_github_name = true`), as `AGENTS.md` asks.

Tested: new `live_notes_sound_while_stopped_without_the_clips` in `soundcraft-mix`. With the transport stopped, the clip stays silent, the auditioned note sounds, and after release it dies away. Tests for `soundcraft-mix`, `soundcraft-playback`, `soundcraft-ui-egui` and `soundcraft-engine` all pass. `cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean on the touched crates. I didn't run the full `cargo xtask ci`, and I didn't play it by ear in the running app.

Note: PR #407 (Pencil-only note insertion) edits the same click handler in `midi_editor.rs`, so whichever lands second may need a small rebase.

title: Keep mute changes in place when thinning automation
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Follow-up to #354.

Mute and send-mute lanes are step lanes: the value holds until the next point. `thin()` measures error against a straight line between kept points, so on a step lane it can drop the point where the value changes. With points at (0, 0), (9000, 1), (10000, 1) and tolerance 0.1, the point at 9000 is removed and the mute turns on 1000 samples late.

This skips thinning for mute and send-mute lanes and adds a regression test for both that checks the value just before and at the change.

How it was tested:
- The new test fails on unchanged main c0cb993: at sample 9000, actual 0.0, expected 1.0.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-model`: 36 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy (warnings denied), workspace tests, assets, layers and wasm all pass.

title: Playback Engine: the ASIO driver's control panel, every installed driver listed, no lost driver
author: Limestudio90
body:
Follow-up to #319, found while testing it with more interfaces.

**What it does**
- **ASIO Control Panel…** in Setup › Playback Engine when the audio system is ASIO. It opens the driver's own settings: ASIO4ALL's choice of devices, an interface's buffer size and clock. Changes made there are picked up with the existing *Reconnect audio device*. The control channel gets `ui.audio_device {control_panel: true}` (and `{reopen: true}`).
- **Every installed ASIO driver is listed**, read from the registry, also while another driver is open, as REAPER does. Before, cpal could not describe other drivers while one was loaded, so going from ASIO4ALL to an interface's driver meant going through WASAPI first.
- **Fix: the open ASIO driver no longer gets unloaded.** The SDK has a single process-wide driver, and loading any driver unloads the current one, while each cpal ASIO host only tracks the drivers it loaded. With a fresh host per call, listing devices (Playback Engine opening) or reopening (Apply, and also *Reconnect audio device*) loaded or opened a driver through a new host. In the reopen case the old stream was dropped after the new one opened, and its teardown then unloaded the new driver. Audio kept playing, but the SDK no longer knew the driver (its control panel reported none). Now one cpal host per audio system is created once and reused, and Apply and Reconnect drop the old player before opening the new one.
- **Fix: arming a track no longer silences the ASIO output.** Arming a track (or input monitoring) opens the input. cpal keeps an ASIO driver's buffers per `cpal::Device` value, and the input was opened from a freshly listed `Device` that did not know about the running output, so cpal remade the driver's buffers for the input alone and the output went silent until another driver was loaded. Now the input on ASIO is opened from the output's own `Device` (`devices::device`), and cpal makes the buffers for both.

title: Portable mode: portable.txt beside the executable keeps settings next to it (#268)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #268.

If a `portable.txt` file sits beside the SoundCraft executable, everything that normally lives in the settings folder goes to `SoundCraftData` next to the executable instead of `%APPDATA%\SoundCraft` (or the macOS/Linux equivalent). author: Limestudio90
body:
**What it does**

- **Engine:** `file.import_audio` gains `clip_list` (sources only, no track or clip) and `sequential` (files onto one track go one after another; default true when a track is the target). The import is split into decoding a source and placing it.

title: VST3 host: IMessage and IAttributeList for plugins (Helix loads its database)
author: Limestudio90
body:
**The problem**
`IHostApplication::createInstance` returned nothing. So plugins whose controller and processor exchange `IMessage`s through `IConnectionPoint::notify` could not create one. Line 6 **Helix Stadium Native** reported *"Failed to get content database recovery info (Out of memory condition. [code -2])"*, loaded no models and exposed no parameters.

**The fix**
- The host now creates `IMessage` (an id plus its attribute list) and `IAttributeList` (ints, floats, UTF-16 strings and binary blobs, by NUL-terminated attribute id).
- Strings and blobs live in their own allocation, so pointers handed out by `getBinary` stay valid while the list holds the value (the VST3 contract).
- Bounds: strings are capped at 1M UTF-16 units and blobs at 256 MiB. Null arguments are refused rather than read. Other classes are still not provided.
- Everything is in `ffi.rs`, the crate's only `unsafe` module, with `SAFETY` comments.

**Tested on Windows** with Helix Stadium Native 1.03.3a: the error is gone, its model database and presets load, and its parameters now appear in the generic plugin window. A unit test drives both objects through the COM interfaces the way a plugin does: ids, every value type, truncating `getString`, `getBinary`, null and missing ids.

title: Mix: strips scroll with a visible bar and the wheel; an oversized window no longer closes the app
author: Limestudio90
body:
Two problems found using the Mix in a separate window (#322) with a 20-track session.

**1. You could not see that the Mix scrolls**
The strips sit in a horizontal `ScrollArea`, but with egui's default floating scroll bar: dark on dark, and shown only on hover. The vertical wheel did nothing. With many tracks, the only visible way to see every strip was a screen-wide window. Now:
- the bar is solid, always visible and drawn in the text colour (12 pt);
- the mouse wheel scrolls the strips sideways, as in Pro Tools' Mix window (no mixer control uses the wheel, and a wheel over a floating window on top is left alone).

This applies to the Mix in the main window and in the separate one.

**2. SoundCraft closed at launch**
A user with a tiling window manager (Komorebi) and the separate Mix saved in the preferences could not start the app. The log showed:
```
wgpu error: Validation Error
  In Surface::configure
    `Surface` width and height must be within the maximum supported texture size. Requested was (29423, 986), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192.
```
wgpu's default handler treats uncaught errors as fatal ("Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default"). Now:
- the app installs a `Device::on_uncaptured_error` handler that logs instead of panicking;
- a new `keep_window_drawable`, called every frame for the main window and the separate Mix, shrinks a window back within 8192 physical pixels when something makes it larger.

I could not reproduce the 29423-pixel size itself (it came from outside the app), so both layers are defensive.

**Tests:** `a_window_wider_than_the_gpu_can_draw_is_shrunk` (29423×986 → 8192 wide; ordinary sizes untouched; the limit halves at 200 %). The track-name-menu test now clicks the Mix name plate above the new bar. Checked by screenshot: the 20-track session's Mix shows the bar.

title: Input monitoring: a lock-free ring that follows the devices' clocks
author: alexandrucaraus
body:
This is part:
(c) the drift-following input monitoring ring of the [following comment.](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/418#issuecomment-6143836541)

So this needs to go first before pipewire and jack, without this there will be cracks when monitoring input from an instrument.

The live input went from the input callback to the output callback through a locked queue: either side that found it locked skipped its block, it could hold half a second, and nothing held its fill steady when the two devices ran on different clocks.

InputRing is now a lock-free single-producer single-consumer ring. The reader keeps about one callback of each side in reserve and steers its read speed by up to 0.5 % to hold that reserve, so input and output devices on separate clocks neither run dry nor pile up delay. It still converts the input rate to the session rate, counts the times it ran dry, and keeps a peak per input channel. A reader that was idle (nothing armed or monitored) starts afresh instead of playing what queued up meanwhile.

title: Opt-in JACK and PipeWire audio hosts (cpal 0.18), with JACK port wiring
author: alexandrucaraus
body:
This PR handles (a) JACK and PipeWire hosts with the cpal 0.18 bump, plus port rewiring from the [following comment](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/418#issuecomment-6143836541).

 Should go after [PR](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/490), otherwise there are cracks in audio when monitoring an instrument.

On Linux the only host was ALSA, reaching PipeWire and JACK through their ALSA plugins: no access to the sound server's own devices and latency, and on a machine where JACK owns the interface, no sound at all.

- cpal goes from 0.16 to 0.18, which has the PipeWire host. devices.rs, the output stream and the input stream are ported to its API (device ids, one error type, plain sample rates).
- crates/playback/src/host.rs picks the audio host: the system one first, then by preference. `jack` and `pipewire` are opt-in cargo features of the playback crate and the desktop app (`--features jack,pipewire`), so default and release builds need no new headers and packaging is unchanged. With `pipewire` built in it is the automatic choice on Linux when it runs; JACK is offered only when libjack can be loaded.
- AudioConfig stays the one device choice. `system` holds a host id and `output`/`input` hold device ids, which Setup > Playback Engine now lists per host, tidied (no ALSA channel-layout aliases, no other applications' streams). `--audio-host <id>` and SOUNDCRAFT_AUDIO_HOST choose the host for a run.
- JACK has no devices of its own and cpal connects to `system:*`: the dialog lists the interfaces behind the physical ports, and the streams are wired to the chosen one after they open (host/jack_ports.rs).
- Streams open in whatever sample format the device has (i8 to i64, u8 to u64, i24, f32, f64), converted, instead of f32, i32 and i16 only.
- A buffer size outside the device's range is brought into it rather than dropped for the device default.

Checked on Linux with a Scarlett 2i2 on PipeWire. The cpal 0.18 port is type-checked only on macOS a…

title: MIDI input devices: live play-through and MIDI recording
author: alexandrucaraus
body:
Separate PR for the part (b) MIDI input with midir, live play-through on armed tracks, and MIDI recording; mentioned in [comment.](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/pull/418#issuecomment-6143836541)

Keyboards and pads could not be used at all: there was no MIDI device layer (G-02).

- crates/playback/src/midi.rs opens every MIDI input port through midir (ALSA sequencer, CoreMIDI, WinMM), follows devices that are plugged in or removed, and passes channel messages to the audio thread over a lock-free ring, each with the time it arrived.
- The mix engine plays them on the instruments of record-enabled and input-monitored MIDI and instrument tracks (crates/mix/src/live_midi.rs): notes at their sample offset, the sustain pedal holding note-offs back.
- While recording, the events are kept with their timeline position and become MIDI clips on the record-enabled tracks, with controllers, pitch bend and aftertouch. A pass can be MIDI only: the audio input is opened for audio tracks alone.
- A MIDI or instrument track chooses a device and a channel at its input selector (kept in the track's input route as `MIDI:<channel>:<device>`).
- Setup > Playback Engine lists the input ports with a switch each and, on request, what arrives from one; Setup > MIDI > MIDI Input Devices opens it. The switches are app preferences.

On Linux, live play was checked with a hardware keyboard (Akai MPK mini 3) and recording with a virtual one (crates/playback/examples/midi_keys.rs). macOS and Windows are type-checked only; there is no MIDI input on FreeBSD or the web.

[Midi-record.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e322bd58-61b0-46b1-9874-32ae0d34cba9)

Note: big doubts about the configuration ui, need some advice there for sure.

title: fix(routing): remove folder bus on delete
author: Jafz2001
body:
## Summary

- remove the summing bus owned by a routing folder when that folder is deleted
- repair remaining inputs, outputs, and sends that referenced the removed bus
- preserve the surviving parent folder bus when deleting nested folders

This follows up on the post-merge note in #219 about the orphaned `<name> Bus`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine cmd::track::tests` (6 passed)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

title: fix(ui): add Fedora font paths so DejaVu and Liberation load on Fedora (#45)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #45 (part 2: the Fedora font paths).

**Cause.** `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`'s `REGULAR` / `BOLD` tables list the Debian/Ubuntu (`/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu`, `/usr/share/fonts/TTF`, `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu`) and Arch (`/usr/local/share/fonts/dejavu`) layouts for DejaVu, and one `truetype/liberation` path for Liberation. None of these match Fedora's `dejavu-sans-fonts` and `liberation-sans-fonts` package layout:

- `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu-sans-fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` (and `-Bold`)
- `/usr/share/fonts/liberation-sans-fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf`

On Fedora, `load_from_fontconfig` (called first in `load`) may also return `None` — e.g. when only Liberation Sans is installed, or when the `sans-serif` fontconfig alias doesn't point at DejaVu — so the direct-path fallback runs and finds nothing. The app falls back to egui's built-in fonts, which don't include the menu glyphs (`→ ▸ ▾ ♯ ✕`), so they render as empty boxes.

**Fix.** Add the two Fedora paths to the `REGULAR` and `BOLD` candidates, in the same order as the existing Debian and Arch paths. `load` still tries `load_from_fontconfig` first; the direct paths are the fallback when fontconfig doesn't surface a usable face.

**Build.** `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` → 105 passed, 0 failed. No new tests: the table is data, and exercising it on Fedora would require running a real `fc-match` against the actual system fonts.

title: fix(mcp): reject oversized batches before execution
author: euisuh
body:
MCP batches currently execute only the first 1,000 entries and can report success after silently omitting the remainder. Reject oversized batches before dispatching any command, for both keep_going values, and advertise the same limit in the tool schema and docs. Valid batches keep their existing order and error handling.

The regression initially created a track from a 1,001-entry batch. With the fix, the session, journal and undo history remain unchanged and the tool reports an error. Boundary coverage also checks empty and exactly 1,000-entry batches.

### Validation

- `cargo xtask ci`: PASS, including formatting, workspace all-target Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, layers and WASM.
- Workspace: 1,064 tests passed; one existing speed benchmark ignored.
- Targeted automation suite: all 18 tests pass; targeted all-target typecheck and Clippy pass.
- Independent parent source/test review completed. No dependencies, persistence schema or authentication changes.

Closes #460

title: WAV: an empty data chunk followed by metadata has no frames (#466)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #466

## Cause

`wav::parse` (`crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs`) reads a non-RF64 data chunk whose size is 0 as "everything that follows". That is meant for a recording that was never finalised (a streaming writer leaves the sizes at 0 until it finishes). But a finished, valid, empty WAV also has a data size of 0, and often a `LIST` or `bext` chunk after it: those bytes were then decoded as samples and the file reported frames it does not have.

## Fix

A zero data size is now read as empty when the file looks finished: the RIFF size is the file's size and everything after the data chunk is whole RIFF chunks (`only_chunks_follow`: printable-ASCII ids, sizes that fit, pad bytes, the last chunk's pad may be missing). Then the chunks after it are scanned normally, so `bext` is still read. In every other case the lenient behaviour is unchanged: an unfinalised recording (RIFF size 0, or audio that is not a run of chunks) still gives the audio that was written. Files with a non-zero data size are not touched.

## Verified

New `crates/audio-io/tests/wav_empty_data.rs`:

- `an_empty_data_chunk_followed_by_metadata_has_no_frames`: LIST + bext after an empty data chunk, metadata before it, and a last odd-sized chunk without its pad byte all give 0 frames through `probe` and `decode`. **Fails on `main`** (`probe` reports frames made of the metadata) and passes here.
- `a_recording_that_was_never_finalised_still_gives_its_audio`: RIFF and data size both 0 followed by 200 stereo frames still decode to 200 frames; so does a file whose RIFF size is right but that has raw audio (not chunks) after the empty data chunk. Passes on `main` and here (control).
- `a_data_chunk_with_audio_is_unchanged`: 100 frames, followed by metadata, still 100 (control).

The rest of the `soundcraft-audio-io` suite (including `malformed.rs`' truncation and corruption tests) passes. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- Recovery of unfinished recordings is still the same lenient read; I did not a…

title: Sampler: a ping-pong loop keeps its phase for steps wider than the loop (#463)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #463

## Cause

`advance` in `crates/dsp/src/plugins/sampler.rs` reflected a ping-pong voice at the loop's end (or start) once and then clamped it to the loop (`.max(ls)` / `.min(le)`). A step wider than the loop (a narrow loop with high transposition or sample-rate conversion) crosses the loop more than once in one output frame; the clamp threw away the rest of the travel, so the loop phase and the effective pitch were wrong.

## Fix

The distance travelled past the edge it was heading for is folded into the loop: an even number of crossings keeps the direction, an odd number turns it round, and the position is `edge ± the remainder`. Steps narrower than the loop move exactly as before (a single reflection gives the same position and direction as the old code). Non-finite positions are left to the existing check that stops the voice, and a loop whose width is not positive keeps going through the existing path.

## Verified

Tests in `plugins::sampler::tests`:

- `a_ping_pong_step_wider_than_the_loop_keeps_the_phase`: a voice in a 10-frame loop, moving forwards and backwards, with steps 0.37, 3, 9.99, 10, 10.5, 23.7, 25, 31.3 and 99.9, for 40 steps each, compared at every step with an independent triangle-wave reference (position within 1e-6, direction too, except exactly on an end where it is the direction it is heading next). **Fails on `main`** and passes here.
- `a_ping_pong_step_below_the_loop_width_moves_as_before`: reflections off the end and the start with step 5 in the same loop. Passes on `main` and here (control).
- The existing `ping_pong_loop_reverses_direction` still passes.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- The plain forward loop mode already folds with `%` and is untouched.
- Whether the voice's direction at an exact endpoint should be "arriving" or "leaving" is as it was: it turns at the edge.

## AI disclosure

This PR was prepared by an AI coding agent (Claude Code) on behalf of @Silvertree2010 and tested as described above.

title: Reject out-of-range signed Exp-Golomb codes instead of wrapping (#473)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #473.

`BitReader::read_se` mapped an odd `ue(v)` code `k` to `(k + 1) / 2` and cast it to `i32` without a range check. `read_ue` can return up to `u32::MAX`, and that code maps to `+2^31`, which does not fit in `i32`. The cast wrapped it to `i32::MIN`, so a malformed stream was accepted with the wrong sign.

The positive branch now uses `i32::try_from` and returns `BitError::InvalidExpGolomb`, the same error `read_ue` already returns when its own value does not fit in `u32`. The negative branch cannot overflow (its largest magnitude is `2^31 - 1`), so it is unchanged. The `InvalidExpGolomb` doc comment now also mentions out-of-range values.

Test: `read_se_rejects_unrepresentable_positive` writes the codes `u32::MAX`, `u32::MAX - 1` and `u32::MAX - 2` and reads them with `read_se`. The first now returns `InvalidExpGolomb` (without the fix it returns `Ok(i32::MIN)`). The other two still decode to the representable extremes, `-i32::MAX` and `i32::MAX`.

title: Reject invalid numeric prereleases and restore Cargo.toml when version update fails (#471)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #471.

`cargo xtask version set` accepted versions that Cargo rejects, and once it had rewritten the root `Cargo.toml` a failed `cargo update` left the broken manifest in place.

How each point of the issue is handled:

- **Leading-zero numeric prerelease ids** (`1.0.0-01`, `1.0.0-rc.01`): `validate()` now rejects a purely numeric prerelease identifier with a leading zero, as the semver crate Cargo uses does. Alphanumeric ids such as `01a` are still allowed, as SemVer allows.
- **Numeric bounds**: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` must fit in `u64` (`99999999999999999999.0.0` is now rejected). Numeric prerelease ids are not limited in length, because Cargo accepts them at any length, so `1.0.0-99999999999999999999` stays valid.
- **Manifest left changed on failure**: the write-then-update step is now a small `set()` helper. If `cargo update` fails (offline and then online), it writes the old manifest back with the same atomic write it used for the new one. The error message says whether the restore worked.

Tests:
- `rejects_what_cargo_rejects`: the invalid cases from the issue fail in `validate()` and `replace()`. Edge cases that Cargo accepts still pass.
- `a_failed_update_restores_the_manifest`: runs `set()` on a temporary manifest with a failing update step and checks that the file is byte-for-byte the original. A succeeding update step writes the new version.

Only `xtask/src/version.rs` changes.

title: Read MP4 ctts version 0 composition offsets as unsigned (#470)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #470.

`parse_stbl` threw away the `ctts` version and cast every composition offset through `i32`. In ISO BMFF, version 0 offsets are unsigned and only version 1 offsets are signed, so a version 0 offset above `i32::MAX` became negative and broke presentation timing.

The parser now keeps the `ctts` version:

- version 0: offsets are read as unsigned
- version 1: offsets are read as signed, as before
- QuickTime files (`is_quicktime`): offsets stay signed in every version, because the QuickTime spec defines `ctts` offsets as signed. Apple MOVs with negative version 0 offsets read the same as before.

This works the same way as the fragmented `trun` path in the same file, which already reads `v == 0` offsets as unsigned and `v == 1` as signed. Our own muxer writes `ctts` version 1 whenever an offset is negative, so files it writes still round-trip.

Test: `ctts_version0_offsets_are_unsigned` takes the handmade file, which has version 1 `ctts` with `-5` offsets, and changes it to version 0. It checks that the offsets now read as `0xFFFFFFFB`. Then it changes the major brand to `qt  ` and checks that they read as `-5` again. The existing `handmade_sample_table` test still covers negative version 1 offsets. The new test fails on main, where the version 0 file reads `-5`.

title: Reject invalid NAL length-field width in length_prefixed_nals (#469)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #469.

`length_prefixed_nals` with `length_size == 0` never advances the cursor and pushes empty slices forever, so a nonempty input loops while memory grows. Widths above 4 are also not valid AVCC/HVCC prefix sizes.

Changes (`crates/video/src/bitstream.rs`):
- Reject any `length_size` outside `1..=4` at entry with a new `BitError::InvalidLengthSize` ("invalid NAL length-field size").
- Check the payload bound as `len > data.len() - i` instead of `i + len > data.len()`, so a 4-byte length near `u32::MAX` cannot overflow on 32-bit targets (the issue's second suggestion, checked cursor arithmetic).
- Doc comment now says 1 to 4 bytes.

The only in-tree caller (H.264 decoder) passes the avcC `lengthSizeMinusOne + 1`, which is always 1 to 4, so its behaviour is unchanged.

Test: `length_prefixed_rejects_bad_width` checks that widths 0 and 5 return `InvalidLengthSize` and a valid 1-byte prefix still splits. Without the fix, the width-0 case never returns. The existing 2- and 4-byte tests are kept.

title: Count the partial quartet in the base64 decoded-size cap (#468)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #468.

`b64::decode` checked its `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` cap with `body.len() / 4 * 3`, which leaves out the 1 or 2 bytes from a final partial quartet. A valid encoding of `MAX_DECODED_BYTES + 1` or `+ 2` bytes got through. The check also ran only after every non-whitespace symbol had been copied into a `Vec`, however long the input was.

Changes, both in `crates/model/src/b64.rs`:

- Before allocating anything, `decode` counts the non-whitespace symbols and returns `None` if there are more than any in-cap encoding can have (`MAX_DECODED_BYTES.div_ceil(3) * 4`).
- The cap check now uses the exact decoded length, partial quartet included (`body.len() / 4 * 3 + body.len() % 4 * 3 / 4`). The output `Vec` is allocated with that same length.

Valid input under the cap decodes exactly as before. The only caller that reports the error (`mix.insert_state`) already says "not valid base64 (or is too large)", so nothing else changes.

Test: `size_cap_counts_the_partial_quartet` encodes cap-1, cap, cap+1 and cap+2 bytes and decodes each one padded, unpadded and with whitespace inside. On `main` the cap+1 cases are accepted, so the test fails there.

title: Return TooLarge when the WAV header size overflows u64 (#467)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #467.

`wav::header` computed the data length with `checked_mul`, but then added the container overhead and the odd-byte pad with plain `+`. A frame count just under `u64::MAX / block_align` passed the multiplication and overflowed on the addition: debug builds panicked, release builds produced a wrapped size.

The total is now built with `checked_add` and returns `AudioError::TooLarge` on overflow, the same error the multiplication above already returns. `wav_float_header` and `FileEncoder::check_room` / `write` for WAV both go through `wav::header`, so all of these paths now return the error instead.

Test: `float_wav_header_rejects_a_frame_count_whose_total_size_overflows` calls `wav_float_header(1, 48_000, u64::MAX / 4)`. Without the fix it panics on the overflow. With the fix it returns `TooLarge`.

title: Validate the full WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE fmt chunk (#465)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #465.

`parse_fmt` in `crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs` read only the first two bytes of the extensible subtype GUID and took them as the format tag. So a truncated extension, or a foreign subtype whose GUID starts with `01 00` / `03 00`, was decoded as native PCM/float.

The extensible branch now checks the points the issue lists:

- **Extension length:** the chunk must hold the whole 40-byte extensible layout (cbSize, valid bits, channel mask, 16-byte GUID). A shorter one is `Malformed`.
- **cbSize:** below 22 is `Malformed`.
- **Valid bits:** more valid bits than the container's `wBitsPerSample` is `Malformed`. A value of 0 still means "same as the container", as before.
- **Full GUID:** the subtype tag is used only when GUID bytes 2..16 match the `KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_*` tail (`GUID_TAIL`, the same constant the writer emits). Any other GUID keeps the extensible tag, so the file takes the existing `WavParse::Foreign` path to symphonia, like other codecs we don't decode natively. Malformed extensions and unsupported foreign subtypes are told apart, as the issue asks.

Files written by our own encoder (cbSize 22, valid bits = bits, standard GUID) parse as before.

### Tests

`extensible_fmt_is_checked_in_full` in `crates/audio-io/tests/malformed.rs` builds extensible WAVs through the public `probe`/`decode` API:

- standard PCM GUID → still `Int16`;
- GUID cut after the format code → `Malformed` (probe and decode);
- cbSize 0 → `Malformed`;
- 24 valid bits in a 16-bit container → `Malformed`;
- PCM prefix with a changed GUID tail → no longer read as native `Int16`.

Each of the last four cases is accepted as native PCM on current main, so the test fails without the fix.

title: Keep audio-io stream test limits as u64 so it compiles on 32-bit targets (#462)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #462.

The format-limit test in `crates/audio-io/tests/stream.rs` typed its format limits as `usize` (`1usize << 30`), so the FLAC limit `1 << 36` overflowed and the test failed to compile on 32-bit targets.

- The limits are now `u64`, and `check_room` takes them directly.
- The `write` call converts the limit with `usize::try_from`. It is skipped when the limit does not fit in `usize`. On 64-bit targets the test runs exactly as before.

This change is test-only. No library code changes.

title: Reject MOV PCM frame widths that overflow u32 (#461)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #461.

`PcmConfig::bytes_per_frame` multiplied bytes per sample by the channel count in plain `u32`. A huge channel count (a public writer config, or a QuickTime v2 sound description, where channels is a full `u32`) panicked in debug builds and wrapped in release, so the writer could keep a wrong frame width, including zero, and later divide sample data by it.

- `PcmConfig::checked_bytes_per_frame` returns `None` when the width does not fit in `u32`.
- `bytes_per_frame` now saturates at `u32::MAX` instead of panicking or wrapping. The demuxer uses it to size PCM chunks, so a file with a bogus channel count gets oversized chunks that fail to read instead of a panic or a wrapped size.
- `Mp4Writer`'s `validate_track` uses the checked width and returns `Error::Mux` when it overflows, like its other PCM checks. The existing `bits == 0 || channels == 0` check already rules out a zero width.

Tests: `pcm_frame_width_overflow` (codec) and `pcm_frame_width_overflow_is_rejected` (writer: `add_track` with `channels: u32::MAX` returns an error; without the fix it panics on the multiplication).

title: Do not retry remote-control commands that may already have run (#458)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #458.

`Remote::call` retried any request once after a "closed" / "Broken pipe" / "reset" error, even when the request line had already been written and the app may have executed it. A lost reply to `engine.execute` (for example `track.new`) could then apply the edit twice.

**Change** (`crates/automation/src/lib.rs` only):
- `roundtrip` now reports, together with the error, whether the request line was already written to the socket. Connect and write failures count as "not sent"; read, EOF, parse and app errors count as "sent".
- `call` still retries once on a fresh connection when the request was not sent, or when the method only reads state (`session.inspect`, `document.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `engine.parity`, `ui.inspect`, `ui.menu.list`; these are the read-only handlers in `ui-egui/src/control.rs`).
- In every other case it does not resend. It returns the original error plus a note that the command may or may not have been executed, so the caller can check the session before trying again.

**Tests:** a fake local TCP app reads one request and drops the connection without a reply, then answers ok on the next connection.
- `remote_does_not_repeat_a_mutation_after_a_lost_reply`: `engine.execute` returns the "may or may not have been executed" error, and the fake app sees the request only once. Without the fix the request is resent and the call succeeds, so the test fails.
- `remote_retries_a_read_after_a_lost_reply`: `session.inspect` is still retried and succeeds, with two requests seen.

No server-side deduplication was added. Stable operation IDs would need a protocol change in the app, which is a maintainer decision.

title: Keep controller-only tracks when importing MIDI (#454)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #454.

`import_midi_bytes` skipped every SMF track without notes, so a track holding only controller events (CC, pitch bend, program, aftertouch) was dropped on import, even though MIDI export now writes controllers.

Changes in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`:

- A track is skipped only when it has neither notes nor controller events. This matches `read_smf`, which drops the format-1 conductor track only when it has no notes and no controllers.
- The drum check (`all notes on channel 9`) was true for a track with no notes, so a controller-only track would have got a drum synth. It now needs at least one note, and a controller-only track gets the normal `subtractive_synth`.
- The imported clip now runs one tick past the last controller event. Playback only sends events that start before the clip end (`at < clip.end()` in the mixer), so a clip ending exactly on its last controller never played it. Before, a track with notes had the same problem when its last controller came after its last note end.

Test: `a_controller_only_midi_track_is_imported_with_its_events` writes an SMF with one track holding three CC7 events at ticks 0, 480 and 960. It imports the file and checks that one track is created with `subtractive_synth`, that the clip extends past the last event, and that the clip keeps the events with their kinds, values and ticks. Without the fix, the import returns no tracks and the test fails.

title: Scale fades, sync point and gain envelope when importing a clip group at another sample rate (#453)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #453.

`clip_group_file::import` already converts clip starts, lengths and audio source offsets from the file's sample rate to the session rate, but left the other sample-based clip fields as they were. A group saved at 48 kHz and imported into a 96 kHz session kept the right overall duration, but its fades lasted half as long and its sync point and gain-envelope breakpoints sat at half their positions.

The fix runs the same `scale` closure over `fade_in.len`, `fade_out.len`, `sync_point` and every gain-envelope breakpoint offset before `c.sanitize()`, so the existing clamping still applies. These are all the sample-based fields on `Clip`. MIDI note positions are in ticks, and `stretch` is a ratio, so neither needs converting.

Test: `fades_sync_point_and_envelope_follow_the_sample_rate` writes a group file saved at half the session rate. The file has a clip with uneven fades, a sync point and two envelope breakpoints. After import, the test checks that every one of those positions has doubled, the same as the clip length. Without the fix, the fade, sync-point and envelope assertions fail.

title: Keep overlapping clips of a clip group when importing it (#452)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #452.

`clip_group_file::import` inserted each clip of a lane with `edit::place_clip`, which clears the clip's range first. A later clip in the same lane therefore cut away the overlapping part of an earlier one, so crossfade partners (or any internal overlap) did not round-trip.

Now each lane is prepared first, the ranges of all its clips are cleared on the destination track (removing only material that was there before the import), and then the whole lane is added in one go and the playlist sorted, the same as `place_clip` does for a single clip. Pre-existing material under the group is still replaced as before.

Fade lengths are not touched here (that is #453).

Test: `overlapping_clips_of_a_group_keep_their_overlap_on_import` imports a group with two MIDI clips at 0..1000 and 600..1600 and checks both keep their start and length. Without the fix the first clip is cut to 0..600.

title: Reset clip stretch after AudioSuite bakes it into the new source (#451)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #451.

`audiosuite.process` renders the clip with its stretch applied, then builds the replacement clip as a clone of the original. The clone kept `stretch`, so playback stretched the already-stretched audio a second time (and could leave a silent tail).

The replacement clip now gets `stretch = 1.0`, the same as the other commands that bake stretch into a new source (`clip.rs` render, `clip_more.rs` commit stretch, `edit_more.rs`, `io.rs`). Fades and gain handling are unchanged; the gain question from #88 is left as is.

Test: `processed_clip_does_not_keep_the_stretch_it_baked` runs Invert and Duplicate on clips at stretch 0.5 and 2.0 and checks that the new clip has stretch 1.0 and a length equal to the new source's frame count. It fails without the fix.

title: Heal keeps each clip's gain envelope and skips clips whose mute or stretch differ (#450)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #450.

`heal()` compared only the source, the offset and the static `gain_db` before it extended the left clip and dropped the right one. That had three effects:

- **Mute:** a muted right half took on the left half's mute state, and the reverse.
- **Gain envelope:** the right clip's envelope was lost. The left clip's points past the seam (separate leaves them in place) then played over the right half.
- **Stretch:** a right half with a different stretch ratio was played at the left ratio.

What this PR changes:

- Clips whose `muted` or `stretch` differ are no longer joined. A single clip can't hold two mute states or two ratios, so heal leaves that seam alone. This works the same way as the existing `gain_db` check.
- Gain envelopes are joined instead of refused. Refusing would stop Heal from undoing Separate on any clip that has an envelope, and that case works today. The new `join_gain_env` keeps the left clip's points before the seam, adds the right clip's points shifted by the left length, and adds a breakpoint on either side of the seam only where interpolation across it would change the gain. A plain separate-then-heal therefore adds no extra points to the left half, and the right half keeps the point that separate put at its start.
- `Clip::env_db_at` is a small public reader for the envelope value, built on the existing private `env_value`.

Tests in `crates/engine/src/edit.rs`:

- `heal_skips_clips_with_different_playback`: a right-only mute and a right-only stretch both leave two clips.
- `heal_keeps_each_side_gain_envelope`: four cases (left envelope only, right envelope only, both with a negative right point, and the exact split that separate produces). Each one compares `gain_at` on every sample of the healed clip with the two original halves. The right-only and left-only cases fail on `main`.

title: Keep unrelated overlapping clips untouched when deleting fades (#449)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #449.

`delete_fades` cleared fades only on clips touching the requested range, but then trimmed every overlapping neighbour pair in the playlist back to its midpoint. Deleting one crossfade therefore also shortened a separate crossfade further down the track.

The function now records the clips it cleared (a `HashSet<ClipId>`, like the other edit ops in `edit.rs`) and trims an overlapping pair only when at least one of its two clips is in that set. Overlaps outside the selection keep their boundaries, source offsets and fades. Inside the selection the behaviour is the same as before. `edit.fades_delete` is the only caller.

Test: `delete_fades_leaves_unrelated_overlaps_alone` builds two separate crossfades and deletes only the first. It checks that the first pair is trimmed to its midpoint with its fades cleared, and that the second pair keeps its start, length, source offset and fades. Without the fix the second pair gets trimmed to its midpoint and the test fails.

title: Load older sessions whose track height is the bare Fit string (#447)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #447.

Zoom Toggle (e26a5f5) changed `TrackHeight::Fit` from a unit variant to `Fit(u16)`. A session saved before that with a track height of `"Fit"` no longer deserializes, so `Session::from_json` fails and the session does not open.

`TrackHeight` now deserializes through a small adapter (`#[serde(from = ...)]`): an untagged enum that accepts the current form or the bare `"Fit"` string. The legacy `"Fit"` maps to `Medium`, which is 88 points, the same height the old `Fit` was drawn at, so these tracks look the same as before. Serialization is unchanged: `Fit(120)` still writes `{"Fit":120}`, and every other variant writes as before.

Tests:
- `track::tests::legacy_fit_string_loads_as_default_height`: `"Fit"` loads as `Medium`; `{"Fit":120}`, `"Large"` and `{"Custom":50}` still load; `Fit(120)` still serializes as `{"Fit":120}`.
- `session::tests::session_with_legacy_fit_height_loads`: a complete saved session with a track height of `"Fit"` loads through `Session::from_json` (the regression test the issue asks for).

Both fail on main (the `"Fit"` string is rejected) and pass with this change.

title: Fix bundle opening losing audio for sources that share one file (#446)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #446.

`open_session_bytes` took each source's bundle entry with `files.remove(&src.path)`, so when two source IDs point at the same file (which native sessions allow and save that way), only the first one got audio; every later one was reported missing and its clips went silent.

Now each path is decoded once and the resulting `Arc<SourceAudio>` is shared by every source that uses that path. A path that is absent or fails to decode is still reported once, as before.

Test: `sources_sharing_one_file_all_load_from_a_bundle` builds a bundle from the demo session with two source IDs pointing at one WAV, opens it, and checks that nothing is reported missing and every source has audio. Without the fix the second source is reported missing.

title: Keep MIDI note selection valid across clip, session and note-order changes (#443)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #443.

The MIDI Editor keeps the selected notes as indices into the edited clip's note list. Those indices went stale in three ways. Each one is handled here:

- **Clip switch.** When the editor moved to another clip, it updated the clip id and scroll, but kept the selection and any drag or rubber band in progress. Delete could then remove notes in the new clip. `MidiEditorState::switch_clip` now clears the selection, drag and band when the clip changes.
- **Session switch.** `session.new`, `session.open`, `session.close` and `session.revert` now reset the editor state. Otherwise a new session with the same clip id would keep the old selection.
- **Keyboard moves.** `midi.notes_move` re-sorts the notes, so after an arrow key moved a note past another one, the selection pointed at a different note. The command now also returns `indices`, the new positions of the moved notes, which works like `midi.note_edit` returning the edited note's new `index`. The arrow-key path sets the selection from it. The moved notes stay selected, so pressing the arrow again keeps nudging the same notes. Clearing the selection would have made every second press do nothing.

Drag-move already cleared the selection after `midi.notes_move`. That path is unchanged.

Tests:
- `midi_editor::tests::switching_clip_drops_selection_and_gestures`: a new clip clears the selection and gestures. The same clip keeps them.
- `tests::replacing_the_session_drops_the_midi_note_selection` (ui-egui `lib.rs`): `session.new` and `session.close` clear the MIDI selection.
- `cmd::midi::tests::notes_move_reports_where_the_moved_notes_went` (engine): a note moved past another one reports its new index.
- `pro_tools_keys::the_piano_roll_selection_follows_notes_the_arrows_move_past_others`: in the demo Keys clip, Shift+Up moves the lowest chord note an octave up, past the other two notes. The selection follows it for two presses. On main it kept pointing at index 0, which is now another note.

title: Reset clip effect EQ/compressor state on stop and seek (#442)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #442.

`MixEngine::reset` (called by playback on stop, locate and loop jumps) reset the strip inserts, the instrument and the delay-compensation lines, but not the cached Clip Effects chains in `Strip::clip_fx`. Replaying a clip after a stop or seek reused the EQ biquad history and the compressor's detector and lookahead delay from the old position, so the output differed from a fresh engine.

Change:
- `ClipFx::reset` resets the EQ and compressor when they exist, using the same `Plugin::reset` that the strip inserts already get.
- `MixEngine::reset` calls it for every cached clip chain on every strip.

Offline renders (`render_clips`) build a new `ClipFx` for each call, so they were not affected.

Test: `reset_clears_clip_effect_history` primes a DC clip through the clip compressor (5 ms lookahead), and separately through the clip EQ (high-pass on). It then resets, renders a later block, and compares that block with a fresh `MixEngine` rendering the same block. Both cases fail without the fix: the old lookahead samples and the settled high-pass state remain.

title: Create session backups exclusively and stop when backup numbers run out (#426)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #426.

`back_up` (crates/engine/src/io.rs) checked write access only on the `Backups` folder, picked the next number with `saturating_add(1)` and copied with `std::fs::copy`. When `Song backup 4294967295.scraft` already existed, the counter stuck at that number and the copy wrote through whatever was there, including a link to a file outside the automation write roots.

Each point of the issue's recommended remediation:

- **Validate the actual destination:** `check_write` now also runs on the backup file path itself, not only on the folder.
- **Reject counter exhaustion:** the next number uses `checked_add`; when it runs out, the backup is skipped with the same `log::warn!("no backup of …")` as the other failures in `back_up`, and the save goes on as before (a failed backup never failed a save).
- **Create exclusively without following existing entries:** the new `copy_new` helper opens the destination with `create_new(true)`, so an existing file or link (even a dangling one) makes the backup fail instead of being followed. A partly written copy is removed. This matches the `create_new` use a few lines below in the same file.

Ordinary saves are unchanged: numbering, the keep-the-newest-ten pruning and the warnings stay the same.

Tests (in `save_tests`):

- `backup_never_overwrites_an_existing_entry_when_numbers_run_out`: a `Song backup 4294967295.scraft` sentinel is left untouched by `back_up` (fails on main, which overwrote it), and `copy_new` refuses an existing destination.
- `backup_never_writes_through_a_link_to_an_outside_file` (Unix): the issue's scenario, a max-numbered backup link to an outside sentinel, plus a link at the next backup name; the outside file stays unchanged.
- The existing `saving_keeps_the_last_ten_versions_as_backups` still covers normal numbering and pruning.

title: fix(video): reject zero/invalid NAL length widths in length_prefixed_nals (#469)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #469.

## Summary

`length_prefixed_nals` in `crates/video/src/bitstream.rs` never validated its `length_size` argument. With a width of 0 and non-empty input, the cursor never advances — the prefix is 0 bytes and a zero length reads a 0-byte payload — so the loop spins indefinitely, appending empty NAL units until the process runs out of memory. Widths above 4 were also accepted even though an AVCC/HVCC record can only produce 1–4, and the cursor arithmetic was unchecked.

## Changes

- `crates/video/src/bitstream.rs` (+52/−8): reject any width outside `1..=4` up front with a new `BitError::InvalidLengthSize` variant. Width 3 stays valid: it is `lengthSizeMinusOne == 2`, produced by the crate's own AVCC/HVCC parsers.
- Same file: prefix and payload cursor arithmetic now uses `checked_add`, returning `BitError::Eof` on overflow, matching the existing truncation behaviour.
- Same file: two new tests — `length_prefixed_rejects_bad_length_size` (widths 0, 5 and `usize::MAX` return `InvalidLengthSize`) and `length_prefixed_widths` (1-, 2- and 3-byte prefixes split correctly; truncated prefix/payload return `Eof`; empty input yields no NALs). No behaviour change for valid inputs.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-video` — 95 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; doc-tests: 1 passed
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-video bitstream::` — 10 passed, 0 failed, including both new tests
- `cargo fmt -p soundcraft-video -- --check` — clean
- The full workspace test suite was not run; the change is confined to the `soundcraft-video` crate, whose tests pass as above.

title: Mix: the mouse wheel turns the fader or knob under the pointer
author: woodgrain816
body:
Part of #305 ("Lack of mouse intuitive controls"). Until now, faders and pan knobs could only be dragged. With this PR the mouse wheel over one turns it, as in Pro Tools, Cubase and Logic.

## Behaviour

title: Open a plugin when it's inserted (#486)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
Fixes #486

### What changed

Picking a plugin for an insert slot added it but opened nothing, so every new plugin took an extra click on its slot. As in other DAWs, the pick now opens it:

- A hosted plugin (CLAP, VST3, AU) opens its own editor.
- Otherwise its plugin window opens, as a click on the slot does: built-in plugins, no audio engine, or an editor that can't open here (CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor on macOS, #485; Audio Units, #501). The reason is shown in the status line.
- Empty and filled slots alike (replacing a plugin opens the new one), in the Mix window and the Edit window's Inserts column (same `insert_slot`).
- The instrument picker is unchanged.

How: the insert menu's three picks (search, built-in categories, CLAP/VST3/AU) go through `pick_insert`, which remembers the slot when `mix.insert` succeeds. `SoundApp::open_inserted` opens it on the next `logic` pass, right after `update_session`, once the audio engine has the instance and its editor. Only the menu opens it, so `mix.insert` from the CLI, MCP or control channel still opens nothing.

`docs/ui-parity.md`: a new row and a revision entry.

### How to test

1. Click an empty insert slot in the Mix window and pick a built-in plugin, e.g. EQ › EQ 7-Band. Make sure its window opens straight away.
2. Right-click a filled slot and pick another plugin. Make sure the new one opens.
3. Turn on the Edit window's Inserts column (Views) and pick a plugin there. Make sure it opens.
