title: feat(midi): implement hardware MIDI I/O, live auditioning, and recording
author: Goldwaterfung
body:
Resolves **Gap G-02 (MIDI Hardware Devices)**, providing full clean-room physical MIDI hardware I/O, low-latency live instrument auditioning, and sample-accurate take recording across macOS (CoreMIDI), Windows (WinMM), and Linux (ALSA).

1. Hardware Abstraction & Lock-Free SPSC Queuing (`crates/playback`)
- Integrated `midir` for cross-platform physical device discovery and input stream polling.
- Implemented `LiveMidiEvent` 16-byte zero-allocation POD message representation.
- Designed `MidiInputRing` (bounded lock-free SPSC ring with `Slot` padded to 64 bytes to eliminate cache-line false sharing).
- Implemented `MidiManager` supporting hot-plug rescanning, persistent port enabling via `session.edit.flags`, and dynamic stream synchronization without tearing down existing active connections.

2. Real-Time Audio Callback & Sub-Sample Timing (`crates/playback`, `crates/mix`)
- **Real-Time Safety:** Guaranteed zero heap allocations on the audio thread. Pre-allocated bounded arrays (`[Option<LiveMidiEvent>; 256]`) for block ingestion.
- **Clock Epoch Synchronization:** Hardware callback timestamps are normalized against monotonic host time to eliminate CoreMIDI boot-time epoch mismatches.
- **Clock Jitter Elimination:** `block_start_us` is derived mathematically on the audio thread via rendered sample counts (`rendered_samples * 1_000_000 / sample_rate`), eliminating non-deterministic `Instant::now()` system calls during steady-state playback.
- **Sub-Sample Accurate Offsetting:** Input events are timestamp-mapped to sample offsets `[0..block_len)` within the audio buffer.

3. Mixer Routing, Voice Tracking & Monitoring (`crates/mix`)
- **Low-Latency Monitoring PDC Bypass:** Monitored/record-armed tracks bypass alignment and extra delay lines (`st.align = 0`, `st.out_extra = 0`), ensuring zero latency for performers.
- **16-Channel Voice Tracking:** Implemented `HeldNotes` using a zero-allocation `[u64; 32]` bitset (2048 distinct (channel, pitch) states). Eliminates cro…

title: fix(playback): retry the next output config when a stream won't start (#440)
author: nanox333
body:
Fixes #440

### What changed

A stream that builds but fails `stream.play()` only logged a warning, and `Player::open` still returned it as operational, so the device was never retried and no fallback ran. Now a failed start is treated like a failed build: that stream is dropped and the next config is tried (the default buffer size after the chosen one), and only then the silent clock.

- `start_stream` returns `false` when `play()` fails.
- The attempt loop in `Player::open` is now `first_started`, which takes the build and start steps as parameters, so the fallback order can be tested without an audio device.
- The success path is unchanged: a stream that starts is used as before.

### Checks

- New tests in `soundcraft-playback`: a stream that won't start is reported as failed; the first config that starts wins and later ones aren't tried; a config that fails to build falls through; no startable config yields `None`, which leads to the silent clock.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback --lib`: 33 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Not run: the full `cargo xtask ci` gate and the wasm check. The silent-clock branch of `Player::open` is not run by a test; only the helper's `None` result is.

title: Plugin editor windows on Linux (VST3 and embedded CLAP, X11)
author: ayozetr
body:
## Summary

Third-party plugin GUIs now open on **Linux** (and the BSDs). Until now VST3 editors reported `VST3 editors are not hosted on this platform yet` there, and CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor were refused. This follows the Windows work in #315, same structure.

- **VST3** (`soundcraft-vst3-host`): an X11 implementation of the `window` module (`kPlatformTypeX11EmbedWindowID`). The view embeds into a top-level window on our own X11 connection (XWayland on Wayland desktops), sized from `getSize`, resized on `IPlugFrame::resizeView`, with fixed size hints. Closing it only hides it (`WM_DELETE_WINDOW`); the editor link's `idle` then detaches the view and destroys the window, as on macOS/Windows.
- **VST3 run loop**: X11 editors have no event loop of their own, so `PlugFrame` also implements `Linux::IRunLoop`. Plugins register their display connection's fd and their repaint timers; the editor link's `idle` (once per UI frame, which is every 30 ms while an editor is open) polls the fds without blocking and fires due timers. Without this, JUCE editors open but never repaint.
- **CLAP** (`soundcraft-clap-host`): embedded-only editors get the same X11 host window (`create(x11, false)` → `get_size` → `set_parent` → `show`, `request_resize` applied in `idle`). The host now offers `clap.timer-support` and `clap.posix-fd-support` on X11, kept per instance and serviced by the editor's `idle`; registrations are dropped when the instance goes. Floating X11 editors benefit from these too.
- Everything stays inside each crate's `ffi.rs` (`unsafe` only there, `// SAFETY:` on every block). New Linux/BSD-only dependencies: `x11rb` 0.13 (pure Rust, already in the lockfile through winit) and `libc` (zero-timeout `poll`). Callbacks never run with the run-loop lock held, so plugins can (un)register from inside them; one removed earlier in the same pass is skipped.

Docs: `plugin-parity.md` (editor rows), `gaps.md` (G-05 shrinks to the macOS work), `ROADMAP.md` (progress log…

title: MIDI Editor: zoom, ruler and playhead; Pencil drags, group trims, Alt-drag copies, chord velocities
author: Limestudio90
body:

title: Undo is for edits: solo, mute, record and view settings aren't undo steps (#492)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
Fixes #492

### What changed

Cmd+Z undid Solo, Mute, Record Enable, track height and view, group activation and insert bypass. Soloing a track and pressing Cmd+Z to undo the last edit took back the solo instead, and every solo, mute or record-arm press filled the history. As in Pro Tools, Logic and Ableton, undo is now for edits:

- The commands listed in #492 are `noundo`: `mix.solo`, `mix.mute`, `mix.solo_safe`, `mix.clear_solos`, `mix.clear_mutes`, `mix.record_arm`, `mix.input_monitor`, `track.set_record_to_input_only`, `track.height` (+ `_up`/`_down`), `track.view`, `track.hide`, `track.change_width`, `track.group_toggle`, `mix.automation_mode`, `mix.insert_bypass` and `track.bypass_*`.
- `track.pin` and `track.color` stay undoable, as in Pro Tools.
- They're still journaled, and the session is still marked modified when they change, since they're saved with it.

How: undo restores a whole-document snapshot, so marking them `noundo` alone would put the old solo, mute, height and so on back on the next Cmd+Z. Each history entry now also keeps the document right after its step (an `Arc`), and `Engine::keep_live_state` carries what changed since then over to the restored snapshot, next to `keep_edit_mode`. What the edit itself changed is still undone: undoing a track preset takes its mute back, and undoing Commit shows the original track again. Insert bypass carries over only where the slot still holds the same plugin, and a width change carries its panners with it.

`docs/architecture.md` says a `noundo` command that changes the document needs its fields carried over in `keep_live_state`. `docs/mcp.md` and the Undo/redo row in `docs/target-app-parity.md` are updated.

### Changed tests

These used one of the settings as an example undo step:

- `track_height`: the two height-drag tests checked that a drag is one undo step. They now check that it isn't an undo step at all. This is the one behavior change to an existing test worth a look.
- `edit_menu`, `merge_test…

title: fix(audio-io): preflight fixed CAF packet sizes and bound packet allocations
author: LabDennis
body:
CAF's fixed-bytes/variable-frames packet tables could reach the demuxer without a packet-byte preflight. Check these sizes before demuxing and share the same check with variable-size packets: no packet may exceed the input file's length or 16 MiB.

The small regression fixture was accepted by `probe` on unchanged main; it now fails before packet allocation. Tests cover fixed and variable packet budgets, valid fixed-size/variable-frame tables, empty tables, and existing PCM decoding. No large hostile allocation or OOM test was attempted. The bound is per compressed packet and against the whole input file; it does not claim to validate every packet against the declared data-chunk extent or replace aggregate decoded-audio limits.

Upstream main and open PRs were rechecked immediately before publication; no overlapping CAF fix was open.

title: fix(audio-io): poison stream encoders after a failed write so later calls cannot claim success (#464)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #464

## Summary

The stream encoders (`FileEncoder` for WAV, AIFF and FLAC) stayed usable after a write failed partway through a block. `write_all` can append a prefix of the block before reporting the error, but the WAV/AIFF writers only advance their frame counter after a fully successful write, and the FLAC writer clears the pending samples before writing the encoded frame. A caller that continued after such an error could call `finish` successfully and get back headers whose counts disagree with the bytes actually on the sink — or, for FLAC, a stream that silently lost a frame of audio.

Each writer now poisons itself on the first failed block/frame write: every later `write` and `finish` call fails with an encode error instead of completing an inconsistent file. Refusals that happen before anything is written (the format size limits checked by `check_room`) do not poison the encoder, and encoders that never see a failed write behave exactly as before.

## Changes

title: Bounce: a Dither option in the dialog and for stems (#522)

body:

Every 16- and 24-bit bounce was TPDF-dithered with no way to turn it off: the Bounce dialog never sent `dither` (so `file.bounce_mix` used its default, `true`), and `file.bounce_stems` hard-coded `dither: true`.

- **Bounce dialog:** a **Dither (TPDF)** checkbox under Normalize, **off by default** as the issue asks (Pro Tools behaviour: the master chain decides). It's disabled for 32-bit float, where there's nothing to dither, and the dialog then sends `dither: false`.
- **`file.bounce_stems`** takes `dither?: true`, like `file.bounce_mix`.
- The engine defaults stay `true`, so scripts and MCP callers that don't pass `dither` keep today's output.
- README: "with optional dither".

**User-visible:** a 16/24-bit bounce from the dialog is now undithered unless Dither is ticked.

`soundcraft-cli convert` always dithering is a separate issue (#548) and is not touched here.

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/bounce.rs`: `the_bounce_dialog_dithers_only_when_dither_is_ticked`. The dialog opens with Dither off; a 16-bit bounce without it is within ½ LSB of the 32-bit float bounce on every sample, and ticking Dither moves samples further. The test doesn't compile on `main` (no `dither` field).
- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: `stems_dither_only_when_asked`, the same check for `file.bounce_stems` with `dither: false` against the default. Fails on `main`.

title: cli: reject unknown options and missing option values
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #549

### The problem

`convert`, `run` and `script` read options with `arg_value`, which matches a flag exactly and takes the argument after it:

```rust
args.iter().position(|a| a == flag).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned()
```

A misspelling, an `--option=value` form, or an option with its value missing therefore all read as **absent**, and nothing inspects what is left over. The command ran without what was asked for and still exited 0.

Reproduced on `c0cb993`, the commit named in the issue, with a 0.1 s 48 kHz 16-bit tone:

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `convert … --rate 44100` | 44100 Hz | 44100 Hz (unchanged) |
| `convert … --rate` | exit 0, 48000 Hz | exit 1, `--rate needs a value` |
| `convert … --rate=44100` | exit 0, 48000 Hz | exit 0, 44100 Hz |
| `convert … --bitdepth 16` | exit 0, Int24 | exit 1, `unknown option --bitdepth` |
| `convert … --bit-depth=16` | exit 0, Int24 | exit 0, Int16 |
| `convert … --normalise` | exit 0, un-normalised | exit 1, `unknown option --normalise` |
| `convert … --bogus` | exit 0, file written | exit 1, `unknown option --bogus` |
| `run --cmd session.new --bounce` | exit 0, no file | exit 1, `--bounce needs a value` |
| `run … --bounces x.wav` | exit 0, no file | exit 1, `unknown option --bounces` |
| `run … --bounce=y.wav` | exit 0, no file | exit 0, `y.wav` written |

### The change

`check_options` takes the options a subcommand accepts, with whether each carries a value, and rejects an unknown option or a missing value. `arg_value` additionally reads `--option=value`, which the issue called a bonus and which makes the forms people evidently reach for do what they look like.

Applied to `convert`, `run` and `script`. `script` is included because it shares `--in`, `--demo`, `--save` and `--bounce` with `run` through `load_engine` and `finish`, so validating one and not the other would leave the same flags checked in one place and not the other.

`app` and `mcp` are left alone: both parse arg…

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `soundcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon alsa-lib vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: soundcraft`;
  - `conflicts: soundcraft, soundcraft-bin, soundcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.soundcraft`, not `soundcraft`.** The AUR already has `soundcraft`, `soundcraft-bin` and `soundcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.6.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `soundcraft-0.6.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.

title: convert: dither only when the output loses resolution (#548)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #548

`soundcraft-cli convert` passed `dither: true` for every conversion, so a same-depth or wider conversion still added ±1 LSB TPDF noise, and digital silence came out as noise.

## What changes

- `convert` now dithers only when it writes integer samples that cannot hold the source exactly:
  - the output has fewer bits than the source (24 to 16-bit),
  - the source is float or a lossy codec (or 32-bit integer, which is already rounded to f32 on decode),
  - `--rate` (to a different rate) or `--normalize` produced new sample values.
- 32-bit float output never dithers.
- A 16-bit file written as 16 or 24-bit, or anything written as 32f, is copied sample for sample, and digital silence stays silent.
- `--dither` and `--no-dither` override the automatic choice; both together are an error (exit 1). This follows the Dither option that #551 adds to Bounce (#522), which does not cover `convert`.
- Usage text and ROADMAP progress log updated.

User-visible: conversions that keep or widen the bit depth no longer change the samples (previously ~25% of samples moved by 1 LSB); conversions that reduce depth behave as before.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the flag parsing and the automatic decision (`auto_dither`).
- `apps/soundcraft-cli/tests/convert.rs` runs the real binary: silence and a 16-bit tone converted to 16, 24 (also the default) and 32f come back unchanged; `--dither` still dithers; a 24-bit source with sub-LSB detail is dithered to 16-bit by default and rounded with `--no-dither`. Both tests fail on main.

The wasm step was not run: Gentoo's Rust has no wasm32 std.

title: Lossless audio: keep timing and report damage instead of silently dropping frames (#550)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #550

A damaged FLAC decoded silently to shorter audio: the FLAC demuxer drops a frame whose checksum fails and resyncs on the next one (so the `DecodeError` branch in `symph.rs` never even saw it), all later audio moved one block earlier, and a truncated file just stopped. `convert` and `file.import_audio` reported success.

## What changes

- `soundcraft-audio-io`, lossless streams only (lossy codecs keep skipping bad packets as before):
  - a FLAC frame the demuxer dropped is found from the gap in the packet timestamps and filled with silence of the same length, never past the length the file declares;
  - a packet that fails to decode is likewise replaced by silence of its duration;
  - `AudioInfo` gains `damage: Option<String>` (serde default, skipped when `None`), describing corrupt frames, a demux error, or audio that ends before its declared length. `probe` leaves it `None` (it does not decode).
- `soundcraft-cli convert` refuses a damaged file: exit 1, `damaged audio, nothing written: …` on stderr, no output file.
- `file.import_audio` still imports it (the timing now holds), logs a warning and adds a `warning` field to that file's entry in the result.
- ROADMAP progress log.

User-visible: `convert` of a damaged or truncated lossless file now fails instead of writing shorter audio; importing one keeps later audio in place (silence where the frame was lost) and returns a warning. Intact files are unaffected.

- `crates/audio-io/tests/damage.rs`: an intact FLAC reports no damage; with one byte flipped mid-file, the decode is still 48000 frames, every sample is either the original at the same position or silence, and the damage is reported; a FLAC cut in half is reported as ending early; WAV/AIFF report none.

author: ProdByBuddha

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

SoundCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`, `alsa-lib`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `soundcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

title: A Pencil click on a MIDI clip selects it, so the MIDI Editor follows
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #562.

With the Pencil on a MIDI or instrument track, the Edit window's click handler only acted when the click missed a clip (to add a one-bar clip there), so a click on an existing clip did nothing: the selection stayed on the last drawn clip and the MIDI Editor kept showing it. title: Apply the punch range before placing a recorded take
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #431

## Cause
`place_recording` placed the whole take with `add_recording` first and trimmed to the punch range afterwards. Placing the full take cleared the existing material across the pre-roll and post-roll, and trimming could not bring it back.

## Fix
The punch range is now applied inside `add_recording_in`, before placement. The clip's start, length and source offset are cut to the punch range, so only the punched span is overwritten. - `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Recording without a punch range goes through the original placement path with the same start, length and source offset. `add_recording` keeps its signature.

title: Plugin scans in the background, cached between launches; Setup > Plug-in Folders
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Problem

Hovering **CLAP** or **VST3** in a Mix insert or instrument menu scanned the plugin folders on the UI thread. The app froze until every plugin file had loaded, and that happened again at every launch. On my machine it took 5.4 s for 17 VST3s, and 4.8 s of that was one plugin (Supertone Clear) loading its model.

## What changes

- **Scans no longer block the UI.** The VST3 and CLAP registries now scan without holding their lock. A separate lock still runs scans one at a time. While files load, the UI can read the cached list and plugin infos, and a plugin is created from the previous or cached list rather than waiting for the scan.

title: Fix stale sample read at the end of each mix block when device and session rates differ
author: DCubix
body:
## Problem

When the device sample rate differs from the session rate (for example a 44.1 kHz
device with a 48 kHz session), the output resampler in `AudioState::fill`
interpolates between `pending[c][i0]` and `pending[c][i0 + 1]`.

`pending` is `BLOCK` (512) samples long, but only the first `pending_len` samples
belong to the current block. When `i0 + 1 == pending_len`, the second sample is
leftover data from an earlier block. The result is one small discontinuity at the
end of every mix block. It is audible as crackling.

At equal rates the fractional part is 0, so the bug does not appear.
Lower buffer sizes make the mix block (`quantum`) smaller, so there are more block
edges per second and the crackling is louder.

## Change

At the block edge, use the last valid sample for the second interpolation point
instead of reading past `pending_len`.

This holds the last sample for the final fraction of a block. It is a deliberate
simplification, noted in a code comment. Carrying the first sample of the
next block would be exact, but needs the next block to be rendered first.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback`: passes.
- Tested on hardware with a 44.1 kHz device and a 48 kHz session. Before/after
  videos are attached below.
- No automated test covers the block edge.

### Before
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73110701-a994-469a-9a80-392c32c211f0

### After
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/695fb95a-c8cf-48c3-86ef-7605a7227402


## Related

- #490 fixes the input monitoring ring. It is independent of this change.

title: Saturate midi.notes_move tick and pitch arithmetic
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/midi.rs:129-130` (no existing issue): midi.notes_move overflows (panics) on huge `ticks` or `semitones`.

## Cause
`notes_move` added the unclamped `ticks` and `semitones` command params to a note's start and pitch with plain `+`. With `i64::MAX` this overflows. Debug builds panic, which `Engine::execute` reports as `EngineError::Internal`. Release builds wrap silently, so a huge positive `ticks` sent the note to the clip start.

## Fix
Both sums now use `saturating_add`. The existing `.max(0)` on the start and `.clamp(0, 127)` on the pitch are unchanged. A huge move now pushes the note to the far right, or pins the pitch at 127, without an error.

## Verified
- Regression test `notes_move_huge_params_do_not_overflow`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib notes_move_huge_params_do_not_overflow`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change the other midi commands or add a range limit on `ticks` or `semitones`.

title: Reject invalid send slot in automation.copy_to_send
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:697` (no existing issue): automation.copy_to_send silently writes to Send A when `send` is invalid.

## Cause
`copy_to_send` parsed `send` with `slot_of(...).unwrap_or(0)`. An out-of-range, unparseable or missing slot became slot 0. The command then copied volume automation into the Send A level lane and recorded an undo step.

## Fix
`copy_to_send` now returns a BadParams error when `send` is missing or not a valid slot (0..N or a..x). That matches the behaviour of `mix.send_remove` and `mix.insert`. Nothing is edited and no undo step is pushed on error.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The copy logic for valid slots is unchanged. `slot_of` and the other slot-taking commands are unchanged.

title: video: budget coded pixel geometry before decoding
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Fixes #427. The pixel budget was enforced only after a frame was decoded (`Movie`), while allocations are sized from the codec's coded geometry: a crafted ProRes frame header (16-bit width/height, up to 65535x65535 pixels) or an H.264 SPS (up to 1024x1024 macroblocks per axis) inside a container whose own dimensions pass the opening check could drive multi-gigabyte allocations, ending in an allocation-failure abort.

The shared `MAX_PIXELS` budget (8192x8192) now lives at the crate root and is checked on coded geometry before anything is allocated — in `prores::decode_frame_into` right after the frame header is parsed, and beside the existing per-dimension cap in `Sps::parse`; `Movie`'s post-decode checks stay as a backstop. Regression tests craft an over-budget ProRes header (refused with `picture too large` before the planes; 8192x8192 at the budget still proceeds) and an over-budget SPS via the existing test writer (refused; exactly-at-budget 8192x8192 still parses); both fail on the unpatched code. `cargo test -p soundcraft-video --lib` passes (96 passed, 0 failed).

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: session: reject duplicate ids and an exhausted id space on load
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Fixes #448. `Session::from_json` accepted documents with duplicate ids in a namespace and with saturated allocator state, so after loading, commands, selections and source associations could act on an arbitrary one of two objects sharing an id, and every further allocation returned `u64::MAX` again.

A new `Session::validate`, run after `sanitize`, rejects duplicate track/clip/source/video/bus/marker/group ids — the error names the namespace and the repeated id — and rejects an exhausted id space (`next_id` or any existing id at `u64::MAX`, which `sanitize` folds into `next_id`). Sessions written by SoundCraft itself never contain either, so only crafted or corrupted files are affected. Regression tests load a session with two tracks sharing an id and sessions with a maximal `next_id` / maximal existing id, asserting `SessionError::Invalid`; all fail without the new call (the sessions load `Ok`) and `cargo test -p soundcraft-model --lib` passes (37 passed, 0 failed).

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Round negative timecode and feet+frames positions symmetrically
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/timecode.rs:111` (no existing issue): Negative timecode and feet+frames positions parse one sample off (asymmetric rounding in FrameRate::samples_at_frame).

## Cause
`FrameRate::samples_at_frame` added `n/2` and then used truncating integer division. That rounds half up for positive frames, but for negative frames truncation toward zero rounds the other way. At 25 fps and 48 kHz, `-00:00:01:00` parsed to -47999 instead of -48000, so format→parse was not a round trip.

## Fix
`samples_at_frame` now rounds the magnitude of the frame count half away from zero and reapplies the sign. Negative frames therefore mirror positive ones. Timecode, Feet+Frames and `position_param` parsing all go through this function, so all three are fixed. Two regression tests were added: one in `timecode.rs` and one in `format.rs`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `timecode::tests::negative_timecode_rounds_symmetrically`, `format::tests::parse_round_trips_timecode_negative`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-time --lib -- negative_timecode_rounds_symmetrically parse_round_trips_timecode_negative`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`frames_at` (already floors with `div_euclid`), the other time formats, and the behaviour for non-negative frames are unchanged.

title: Fix Min:Secs showing 1 ms early at exact millisecond positions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/format.rs:46` (no existing issue): Min:Secs counter/ruler shows 1 ms too early at exact millisecond positions (44.1 kHz) because of float floor.

## Cause
`min_secs` computed `(seconds * 1000.0).floor()` in floating point. Exact millisecond positions, such as sample 88641 at 44.1 kHz, come out just below the integer, so floor shows one millisecond too little (`0:02.009` instead of `0:02.010`).

## Fix
`min_secs` now computes whole milliseconds in integer arithmetic, `|s| * 1000 / hz` in i128. The mins/secs/ms split is the same as before. The result saturates instead of overflowing.

author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Chinese session, track and clip names rendered as nothing in the Tracks panel because the font loader only had a Hangul fallback: a Chinese "主旋律Lead" showed "Lead" and a fully Chinese name showed no label at all. This adds a Simplified-Chinese fallback loaded from the operating system (PingFang/Heiti SC/Hiragino Sans GB/Songti on macOS, Microsoft YaHei/SimSun/SimHei on Windows, Noto Sans CJK SC or WenQuanYi via fontconfig on Linux) and appended to every font family, exactly like the existing Korean fallback, with no fonts redistributed. A regression test opens the real font definitions and asserts every family can draw Chinese text when the system has a Chinese font, and a companion test keeps the candidate list covering every desktop platform and the right Noto face index. `docs/localization-parity.md` is updated accordingly.

Fixes #267

title: packaging: sign macOS binaries with the plug-in-hosting entitlement (#153)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
With only the microphone entitlement, hardened runtime's library validation refused every third-party VST3/CLAP/AU binary signed by another team, so a release build scanned no plug-ins (the reported log line: "mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs"). This adds `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` to the macOS entitlements and signs the CLI with the same entitlements file, since the CLI hosts plug-ins in-process too. An xtask regression test fails if the entitlement is removed or if any of the three signed binaries stops using the entitlements file, so the packaging gate keeps it honest. The G-05 gap entry is shrunk accordingly.

Fixes #153

title: engine: refuse session bundles over the reader's limits (#433)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The bundle reader refuses bundles over 10 000 entries or 1 GiB because bundles are hostile input, but the writer had no matching caps, so saving a session with enough in-memory audio could deliver a file SoundCraft itself cannot reopen — and still mark the session clean. The writer now counts entries and encoded bytes as it assembles the bundle and refuses to deliver one over the reader's caps, before the delivery hook or `mark_clean` is reached. Regression tests pin the entry-count boundary with a real session of 10 000 sources, assert the caps match the reader's exactly (at the cap is fine, one over is refused), and keep the 0.03 s runtime so the suite stays cheap.

Fixes #433

title: ui: MIDI Real-Time Properties submits only the property that changed (#444)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The window's sliders always sent all four Real-Time Properties from the form's state, and the form was never initialised from the selected tracks, so nudging Velocity silently reset Transpose, Duration and Delay — and switching tracks carried the previous track's values over. The form now re-reads the target tracks' values whenever the target selection changes, and each frame submits only the property whose control actually moved, which is what the `event.midi_rtp` command is built for (it stores each key it is sent). The regression test drives the real window through egui_kittest: it sets Transpose 7 / Duration 50 on a track, opens the window, drags the Velocity slider, and asserts Velocity reached the engine while the other three properties are untouched — this fails on main with "editing Velocity reset Transpose: left: 0.0, right: 7.0".

Fixes #444

title: Autosave: give every session its own folder; keep the tests apart from coarse mtimes (#579)
author: switch87
body:
With the temp dir on tmpfs, `cargo xtask ci` fails on `main` in four autosave/recovery tests, not only the one in the issue. There are two causes:

**1. Two sessions could share one autosave folder (code fix).** `Autosave::create` named the folder `<name> <millis>-<pid>` and created it with `create_dir_all`, so two sessions started in the same millisecond got the *same* folder, and the second overwrote the first's unsaved work. On tmpfs the tests run fast enough to hit this every time (`recovering_keeps_the_unsaved_work_it_replaces`, `closing_the_session_or_quitting_drops_its_autosave`). `create` now makes the folder with `create_dir` and, when the name is taken, tries `-2`, `-3`, ... Nothing parses the folder name, so leftovers and recovery are unaffected.

**2. Coarse mtimes (test-only fix, as suggested in the issue).** `leftovers()` offers an autosave only when it is strictly newer than its session file. A save and the autosave right after it can share one mtime on tmpfs, so the tests that save and then autosave now move the saved file's mtime a second back (`unsaved_work_is_offered_once_its_session_closes`, `saved_audio_is_referenced_and_takes_are_copied_once`, and `an_exit_without_quit_offers_unsaved_changes_at_the_next_launch` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/recovery.rs`). The `>` comparison itself is unchanged.

New test: `sessions_started_together_get_folders_of_their_own` creates 20 autosaves back to back and checks they all get different folders (fails on `main`).

Testing (Gentoo, Linux 6.18, `/tmp` on tmpfs):
- Before: `recovery` 3 of 6 failing and the engine autosave test failing every run; all pass with `TMPDIR` on XFS.
- After: engine autosave tests 9/9 and `recovery` 6/6, repeated several times on tmpfs.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets and layers pass. The `wasm` step was not run: Gentoo's system Rust has no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` std.

title: Save a session bundle only if it opens again (#433)
author: vxMacDev
body:
Fixes #433.

`read_bundle` refuses a bundle with more than 10,000 entries or more than 1 GiB unpacked, but `session_bundle` wrote whatever the session held. In the browser, `save_session_bundle` then delivered the file and marked the session clean, so a long session (an hour of stereo 48 kHz float audio is about 1.4 GB) saved without complaint and couldn't be opened again.

- The two limits are now one `BundleLimits`, used by both sides.
- `session_bundle` counts each file and its bytes the way `read_bundle` does (stored entries, so the bytes are the unpacked size) and returns an error before going past either limit: "bundle: too large to save (a bundle holds at most 10000 files and 1024 MiB, or it can't be opened again)". `save_session_bundle` already returns before delivering or marking clean when `session_bundle` fails, so the session stays unsaved.

**Test:** `a_bundle_is_saved_only_if_it_opens_again` saves the demo session with limits set to exactly its file count and size, and checks that `read_bundle` opens it with those same limits. One file fewer or one byte less refuses the save. Turning the writer's check off makes it fail.

On Windows, the engine's tests don't compile on main: `windows_ignores_case_and_refuses_devices` in `file_access.rs` moves `upper` into `check` and then formats it. I patched that locally only to run the tests (not part of this PR). With that, all `soundcraft-engine` tests pass (229 unit tests plus the integration tests) and fmt is clean. Clippy flags nothing in `io.rs`; with `-D warnings` it stops on an existing Windows-only `unused_mut` at `autosave.rs:560` (the `mut` is only needed on Unix).

title: Reject invalid slot in mix.insert and mix.send
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:300` (no existing issue): mix.insert and mix.send silently use the first free slot when `slot` is out of range or invalid.

## Cause
`mix.insert` and `mix.send` read the optional `slot` with `slot_of`, which returns None for out-of-range or unparseable values (12, "k", "x1"). The code then fell back to the first free slot, so a bad slot looked the same as no slot and the command still reported success.

## Fix
A new `optional_slot` helper treats a missing or null `slot` as "first free slot". Any other value that does not parse now returns the same "`slot` must be 0..N or a..x" error that `track_slot` gives. Both commands use this helper, and the check runs before anything is changed (including before `mix.send` creates the bus).

## Verified
- Regression test `insert_and_send_reject_invalid_slot`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib insert_and_send_reject_invalid_slot`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`slot_of` and the commands that need a slot (`track_slot` users, `mix.insert_move`) are unchanged; they already reject invalid slots.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a floating window in SoundCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the window says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside SoundCraft and names this app's own world, so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent window or control names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.

title: Release held VST3 notes on reset instead of discarding them
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #441

## Cause
`Vst3Plugin::reset` cleared the pending note-event queue and the host's held-note array. That threw away the note-off events `all_notes_off` had just queued, which `Mixer::reset` calls right before `reset()`. The processor's voices kept sounding after stop/seek while the host believed no notes were held.

## Fix
`reset` now keeps pending note-off events, moves them to the start of the next block, and calls `all_notes_off` to queue releases for any keys still held before it clears the held-note array. Pending note-ons, pressure events and control events are still dropped.

## Verified
- Regression test `reset_after_all_notes_off_still_releases_held_voices`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-vst3-host --test fixture_e2e reset_after_all_notes_off_still_releases_held_voices`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The mixer's reset call order in `crates/mix` and the block-boundary scheduling discussed in #182.

title: Reject CLAP port layouts beyond host limits instead of truncating
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #435

## Cause
`Instance::audio_ports` clamped the advertised port count to 16 and each port's channel count to 64. `ClapPlugin::prepare` then built buffers from those reduced numbers and activated the plugin anyway, so a plugin that advertised a wider layout was processed with fewer ports or channels than it declared.

## Fix
`audio_ports` now returns an error when a plugin advertises more than 16 ports or more than 64 channels on a port. When that happens, `prepare` logs a warning, leaves the plugin inactive and clears its buffers, so `process` passes the audio through untouched and the plugin never runs. The test fixture gains three wide-layout plugins: one exactly at the limits, one with 17 ports and one with a 65-channel port. The plugin count expected from the fixture goes from 2 to 5 in the clap-host and engine tests.

## Verified
- Regression test `layouts_beyond_the_host_limits_are_rejected_not_truncated`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-clap-host --test fixture_e2e layouts_beyond_the_host_limits_are_rejected_not_truncated`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 16-port and 64-channel limits stay the same, and `Plugin::prepare` still returns `()`, so a rejected layout is reported through the log, not to the caller.

title: Add MP3 export / bounce support
author: Milkshak3s
body:
## Bounce Mix writes MP3

Adds MP3 output to Bounce Mix and Bounce Stems with a new pure-Rust MPEG-1 Layer III encoder in `soundcraft-audio-io`. It has no `unsafe`, no C dependencies and no GPL/LGPL code. This closes the MP3 half of G-21.

### What's new
- **Bounce commands:** `file.bounce_mix` and `file.bounce_stems` take `format: "mp3"` and an optional `bitrate` from 32 to 320 kbps. The default is 320.
- **Bounce Mix dialog:** MP3 is a Format option, and a Bitrate picker replaces Bit Depth when it's selected.
- **Surround:** a surround mix bounced to MP3 folds down to stereo automatically.
- **Sample rates:** sessions at rates MP3 can't hold are resampled to 44.1 or 48 kHz.
- **CLI:** `--bitrate` on `convert` and `run --bounce`.
- **MCP:** the `bounce_mix` tool lists `mp3` and `bitrate`.

### Encoder
- **Design:** constant bitrate, joint stereo, a bit reservoir, and scalefactor noise shaping against a simple masking estimate.
- **Quality:** about 55 dB SNR at 320 kbps and 44 dB at 128 kbps on a test signal.
- **Speed:** about 70–110× realtime in release builds.
- **Tables:** the ISO Huffman tables and window were generated from puremp3 (MIT OR CC0-1.0) and verified by decoding the output with symphonia.

### Known limitations
- **No gapless tag:** decoded files start with the usual MP3 delay of about 22 ms.
- **Long blocks only:** there's no full psychoacoustic model.
- **Still missing:** AAC export.

The parity docs, gaps (G-21) and roadmap are updated.

title: Clamp retrospective record start_ticks to stay within MAX_POSITION
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/event_more.rs:753` (no existing issue): event.retrospective_record overflows (panics) on huge start_ticks and places clips far past MAX_POSITION.

## Cause
`retro_record` set a floor of 0 on each note's tick but no upper limit. When `start_ticks` was `i64::MAX`, the eagerly evaluated `unwrap_or(first + 1)` overflowed and panicked. Large values that did not overflow (e.g. 1e15) placed the clip far past `MAX_POSITION`, where the timeline cannot reach it.

## Fix
Each note's tick is now capped so that a note of the longest allowed length still ends within `MAX_POSITION`. The fallback end tick uses `unwrap_or_else` with `saturating_add`, and the clip end in samples is also capped at `MAX_POSITION`.

## Verified
- Regression test `retro_record_huge_start_ticks_stay_in_range`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib retro_record_huge_start_ticks_stay_in_range`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `start` (sample position) path still goes through `position_param` as before. The new tick cap applies to it too, but in-range input behaves the same.

title: mcp: a batch past 1000 calls is refused before anything runs (#460)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #460

## Before
`batch` in `crates/automation/src/mcp.rs` iterated `calls.iter().take(1000)`. A list of more than 1000 calls ran its first 1000 and, if those succeeded, the tool result was a plain success listing 1000 results — nothing said the rest had not run. An agent sending a long edit list got a session with part of it applied and no error.

## Change
- `MAX_BATCH_CALLS = 1000` (public constant). A longer list is refused **before any call runs**: `isError: true` with `` `calls` has N entries; at most 1000 run in one batch, split it ``. Nothing is left half done; the caller splits the list.
- Exactly 1000 still runs in full; `keep_going` and the per-call results are unchanged.
- `docs/mcp.md` states the cap.

Refusing whole (rather than running 1000 and flagging the remainder) keeps the contract simple: a batch either ran or did not, which is what `keep_going`'s semantics already assume.

## Tests
`batch_over_the_cap_is_refused_before_anything_runs` (`crates/automation/tests/agent_tasks.rs`): 1001 `track.new` calls → `isError`, the message names 1001 and the cap, and `inspect_session` shows zero tracks; then exactly 1000 calls run and create 1000 tracks. Fails on `main` (1000 tracks appear and the result is a success).

`cargo test -p soundcraft-automation` (all suites), `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` green (Linux build host).

title: Bound playback publication and retire resources on the control thread
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Playback now admits one prepared session publication at a time and retains the latest waiting snapshot on the control owner. Stalled or disconnected retirement cannot discard a displaced snapshot or processor on the callback, and Stop/Locate/recording/input commands remain serviceable.

A control-created envelope carries displaced sessions, retired processors, replaced pending buffers and old sample-rate engines back through a bounded return channel. Shutdown stops the stream or joins the silent clock before reclaiming audio state, device scratch and shared meter storage on the control caller; late callback closure release sees an empty state slot.

title: Decode and probe zero-frame FLAC files written by our encoder
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs:41 (open/run, used by probe and decode for FLAC)` (no existing issue): Zero-frame FLAC written by our own encoder cannot be decoded or probed ("malformed audio: end of stream").

## Cause
An empty FLAC has a STREAMINFO block and no audio frames. Symphonia's FLAC reader looks for the first frame when it is constructed and hits end of stream, so `probe` and `decode` return `Malformed("end of stream")` for files our own encoder wrote.

## Fix
`open` in `symph.rs` now checks for a FLAC stream whose STREAMINFO declares 0 samples and has nothing after the metadata blocks. In that case `probe` and `decode` build the `AudioInfo` and an empty buffer from STREAMINFO and skip symphonia's reader. All other FLAC input still goes through symphonia, and the existing metadata checks run first.

## Verified
- Regression test `zero_frame_flac_round_trips_like_wav_and_aiff`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io --test roundtrip zero_frame`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Symphonia is unchanged. A FLAC that claims a non-zero sample count but holds no frames still returns an error. WAV and AIFF are unchanged.

title: Drop out-of-range tempo and meter events when sanitizing a session
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/tempo.rs:254` (no existing issue): Session with a meter change near i64::MAX loads, then Bars|Beats math overflows (panics in debug builds, wrong positions in release).

## Cause
`TempoMap::sanitize` only rejected tempo and meter events with negative ticks and set no upper bound. A session with a meter event near `i64::MAX` therefore loaded, and the bar arithmetic in `bar_start_tick` and `bar_beat_at_tick` (`(nt - cur_tick) + tpb - 1`) overflowed. In debug builds that panics when parsing, snapping or formatting Bars|Beats positions.

## Fix
`sanitize` now keeps only tempo and meter events whose tick lies in `0..=MAX_POSITION`, the same bound used for clips, notes and other positions. The first meter segment can no longer reach a tick that overflows. The first event is still guaranteed at tick 0.

## Verified
- Regression tests `sanitize_drops_events_beyond_the_position_range`, `a_meter_change_far_beyond_the_position_range_is_dropped_on_load`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-time --lib sanitize_drops_events_beyond_the_position_range && cargo test -p soundcraft-model --lib a_meter_change_far_beyond_the_position_range_is_dropped_on_load`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The bar arithmetic in `bar_start_tick` and `bar_beat_at_tick` is not changed to saturate. Events set through the API at ticks beyond `MAX_POSITION` are not validated. This fix only covers maps loaded from files, which go through `sanitize`.

title: Fix step_input extending a MIDI clip over the adjacent next clip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/event_more.rs:416-445` (no existing issue): event.step_input at the boundary of two adjacent MIDI clips extends the first clip over the second, creating overlapping clips.

## Cause
`event.step_input` chose its host clip with `contains(at) || end() == at`. At the boundary of two adjacent MIDI clips, `find` returned the earlier clip because it ends at `at`. The note was then placed outside that clip and the clip was grown into the next one, because `next_start` ignores a clip that starts exactly at `at`.

## Fix
Host selection now looks for a MIDI clip that contains the insertion point first. It falls back to a clip that merely ends at the insertion point only if none contains it. At a boundary, the note now goes into the clip that starts at `at`, and no clip is extended over its neighbour.

## Verified
- Regression test `step_input_at_clip_boundary_uses_next_clip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib step_input_at_clip_boundary_uses_next_clip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `next_start` limit on extension and the new-clip creation path are unchanged.

title: Keep key inputs consistent through Commit, routing changes, bus deletion and presets
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The built-in Compressor/Limiter and Expander/Gate can now take their key from a bus: kick to a bus, bass compressor keyed from it.

In Pro Tools you send the source to a bus, pick that bus in the plug-in's key input menu and turn on External Key; the dynamics then react to the bus instead of their own track. This PR does the same for our two built-in dynamics: a Key menu in the plug-in window (No Key Input or any session bus) and `mix.insert_key {track, slot, bus | null}`, plus an `ext_key` parameter, so it can be automated like any other. Picking a bus turns External Key on and "No Key Input" turns it off (happy to switch if you'd rather keep the two separate). Tracks keyed from a bus are rendered after the strips that fill the busses, in the same dependency order as the auxes. A bus that already carries the track's own signal (directly, through an aux or through another keyed track) is greyed out in the menu and refused by the command, since it would be a feedback loop; a later send or output that would close such a loop is refused too (I couldn't check what Pro Tools does in that case). Commit of a keyed track keeps the tracks feeding its key playing into the key bus, so a keyed gate doesn't commit silence. Deleting a bus clears the keys that read it, and a track preset leaves keys behind like the rest of the routing. The audio path stays realtime-safe: the key is a borrowed slice of the bus buffer, nothing is allocated or locked, and the ordering is only recomputed when the routing changes.

Left for follow-ups (#502 stays open): sidechain buses for third-party plugins (VST3, CLAP and AU hosts), a key input on the De-Esser, Key Listen, and delay compensation of the key path: with latent plugins in the session the key arrives late by the slowest track's insert latency, plus the slowest aux return's when an aux returns onto the key bus.

title: Import audio off the UI thread (#597)
author: 4waymedia
body:
Fixes #597.

Importing a large audio file froze the window: File ▸ Import ▸ Audio, drag-and-drop, Open With and a Workspace double-click all read, decoded, resampled and built peaks on the UI thread. A 10-minute 44.1 kHz stereo WAV into a 48 kHz session took ~28 s (dev build) with no redraws.

title: Fix GNOME/Wayland window controls
author: danielmigueltejedor
body:
## What and why

GNOME/Wayland does not provide server-side window decorations. These desktop builds enable eframe's Wayland backend with default features disabled, which leaves winit's Adwaita frame disabled as well. This can leave decorated windows without usable window controls.

Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita` specifically for Linux. Its minimize, maximize/restore and close icons are vector paths, so the close icon does not depend on a font glyph. X11 and compositors offering server-side decorations retain the window manager's frame.

Attribute the dependency's unmodified Cantarell fallback font and include its OFL text and sctk-adwaita's MIT notice in `NOTICE`. Ensure the existing package-document helper ships those notices. title: Resample through a polyphase bank: 5x faster rate-converting imports (#597)
author: 4waymedia
body:
Importing audio whose sample rate differs from the session's spent most of its time in `dsp::offline::resample`. Each output sample looked up and interpolated the windowed-sinc kernel once per tap, in f64. This came up in #597 ("it takes very long to import") and is the follow-up promised in #636.

## What changes

Only `crates/dsp/src/offline.rs`.

- `resample(ch, from, to)` reduces the rate change to `step / phases` (44.1 kHz → 48 kHz is 147 / 160). It precomputes the kernel weights once per phase in a `Polyphase` bank, then each output sample is one dot product over contiguous input.
- The weights are the ones the per-tap path computes. Taps beyond the kernel's half width weigh 0. Taps are summed in the same order, and at the signal's edges taps outside the signal are skipped as before. Cutoff and output length are unchanged.
- The bank is capped at 4 Mi weights (16 MiB). Rate pairs with no small common ratio (for example 44 100 → 96 001) fall back to the existing per-tap `resample_channel`, which is unchanged. `resample_ratio` (time stretch and pitch shift) is untouched.

## Results

10-minute stereo 24-bit WAV imported into a 48 kHz session with `soundcraft-cli`, dev build, same machine, warm file cache:

| File rate | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 44.1 kHz | 25.5 s | 4.6 s |
| 48 kHz (no resampling, control) | 0.9 s | 0.9 s |

The same speedup applies wherever `resample` runs: imports, opening sessions whose files are at another rate, the Sampler, and AudioSuite varispeed.

## Tests

- `dsp: offline::tests::polyphase_resample_matches_the_per_tap_kernel` compares the bank against `resample_channel` at 44.1↔48 k, 48↔96 k, 22.05→48 k, 8→44.1 k and 48→22.05 k. The largest difference is under 1e-5. It also covers a signal shorter than the kernel (edges only) and the fallback for a large ratio.
- The existing resampler quality tests (`dsp/tests/offline_meters.rs`) and the fuzz test pass unchanged.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp -p soundcraft-engine` passes, `car…

title: Read iXML field-recorder metadata from WAV/BWF/RF64 and show it in info
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Read iXML field-recorder metadata from WAV/BWF/RF64 files and show it in `soundcraft-cli info`, next to `bwf`.

Field recorders (Sound Devices, Zoom, Zaxcom...) write an `iXML` chunk alongside `bext`: an XML document with the project, scene, take, tape, notes, whether the take was circled, and a `TRACK_LIST` naming each channel of a polyphonic file. Pro Tools reads it when you import such a file. This PR reads those fields into a new `AudioInfo.ixml` (`IxmlInfo`: project, scene, take, tape, note, circled, and tracks with channel index, interleave index and name), the same way `bwf` is read, and `info` prints it. There's no XML crate in the workspace, so it's a small reader for just these elements: no DTDs, only the predefined entities and character references, chunks over 1 MiB skipped, nesting capped. An iXML chunk it can't read is dropped with a `log::warn!` and the file imports exactly as before. Using the channel names to name tracks on import (and conform) is left for a follow-up, so this one stays reviewable; `docs/gaps.md` G-17 and the parity row say so. `ixml` is boxed in `AudioInfo` because most files have none and the inline struct tripped `large_enum_variant` on `AiffParse`. Happy to switch to an unboxed field or a different shape if you prefer.

title: Shift controller events by Delay in track.write_midi_rtp
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/track_more.rs:370-392 (write_rtp); playback side: crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1526-1527` (no existing issue): track.write_midi_rtp ignores the Delay property for controller events, so the baked MIDI no longer matches playback.

## Cause
`write_rtp` applied the Delay real-time property only to `sequence.notes`, then deleted the `rtp.<id>.*` values. Playback in `schedule_notes` also delays controller events (CC, pitch bend, aftertouch, program), so after baking, notes moved but controllers stayed at their old ticks.

## Fix
`write_rtp` now adds `delay_ticks` to every controller event with `tick >= 0`, using the same `saturating_add(..).max(0)` as notes. It does this before re-sorting the sequence, so the baked MIDI matches playback.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtp_delay_shifts_controller_events`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib rtp_delay_shifts_controller_events`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Controller events before tick 0 (hidden by a start trim) are left as they are, because playback ignores them. Transpose of poly-pressure keys in `write_rtp` is unchanged.

title: Plugin-only editor changes mark the session modified
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #455.

Some changes made only inside a plugin's own editor never reached the document. A clean session stayed clean, so the autosave skipped them. Edits on a hosted instrument were dropped in `apply_editor_edits`: hosted instruments keep their parameters in their own state, so `mix.insert_param` can't take them. And `ClapEditor::idle` cleared the host's `state.mark_dirty` flag without telling anyone. `PluginEditor` now reports that flag through a new `state_changed`. Each frame, the UI reads the state of the plugins that changed, plus any instrument edited in its editor, and stores it in the session with `mix.insert_state`, the way `capture_plugin_states` already does before a save. The session turns modified, asks to be saved, and the one-second autosave writes the new state.

Three details keep this quiet:
- A state stored while a gesture is running (a knob drag, an automation pass) joins that gesture through `execute_merged`, so a drag stays one undo step even when the plugin marks itself dirty on every frame. This adds a small `Engine::merge_key` getter and leaves the merge semantics alone.
- `mix.insert_state` with the bytes already stored is a no-op: the session isn't cloned, the revision doesn't bump and no autosave is queued.
- A `mark_dirty` sent while the plugin loads or restores its state is dropped when the instance is created, so opening a session doesn't make it modified.

Only CLAP implements `state_changed`. VST3 and AU editors keep the default `false`, so a non-parameter state change in a VST3/AU insert still needs another edit (or a save) before it reaches the session. Edits on VST3/AU instruments are covered, through the instrument path. The state is read on every frame that has a change. Happy to switch to a throttled read if some plugins have heavy states.

title: Drag an insert to move it, Option-drag to copy it, across slots and tracks (#638)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Drag an insert to another slot, on the same track or another one, to move it; Option-drag to copy it.

In Pro Tools a plain drag moves a plug-in to the slot you drop it on and Option-drag copies it there with its settings, each as one undo step. This PR does the same in the Mix window and in the Edit window's Inserts view, which share `insert_slot`. The drop runs a new command, `mix.insert_transfer {track, slot, to_track, to_slot, copy}`, so a move or copy is one undo step for both tracks. `mix.insert_move` keeps swapping slots as it does now. Before the drop, the app stores each hosted plugin's live state on its insert (`capture_plugin_states`), so a CLAP or VST3 copy gets the current settings, not the ones from the last save. Dropping onto a used slot replaces the plugin there, as the issue asks. The insert's automation goes with it: moved on a move, duplicated on a copy, and the replaced plugin's lanes are dropped, since they're keyed by slot and would otherwise drive the new plugin. If the moved insert's lane was on show, the destination track now shows it and the source goes back to Volume. I couldn't check what Pro Tools does with automation across tracks, so happy to switch on both of these. An instrument insert (a MIDI track's synth) can only go on another MIDI track. A plugin editor that was open on a moved insert is reopened on its new slot on the next frame; that path has no test (it needs a real plug-in with an editor), so I'd appreciate a quick check with one you use.

One fix in playback was needed: the player kept a hosted plugin's instance whenever the slot held the same plugin id, so a copy dropped onto the same plugin, or Undo of one, kept playing the old instance, and the next autosave wrote its state over the copied one. The player now remembers every state each instance was created with or captured in, and creates a new instance when the slot gets a state from outside that set. title: Fix Split into Mono repeating the left channel
author: reoniazx
body:
Splitting a stereo or surround audio track into mono now preserves each source channel. Previously, all resulting mono tracks played channel zero of the original multichannel source, so the right and other surround channels were replaced by the first channel.

## Before and after

The added numeric regression uses a synthetic stereo source with a constant left channel of `0.2` and right channel of `0.7`. It splits the track, disables the original track, and renders the resulting mono tracks with their existing left/right pan positions.

| Check | Before this fix | After this fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rendered left output, sample 64 | `0.2` | `0.2` |
| Rendered right output, sample 64 | `0.2` — incorrectly repeats the left channel | `0.7` — preserves the right channel |
| Media referenced by the new mono clips | Original multichannel source; mono rendering always reads its channel zero | A mono source containing the corresponding original channel |
| Missing or zero-channel source audio | Split can succeed with unusable clips that render silently | Returns a command error and rolls back all tracks and sources created by the command |

The numeric regression was run against the upstream implementation and failed with `L=0.2, R=0.2`. With this fix it passes with `L=0.2, R=0.7`. The original track and multichannel source remain available.

## Implementation

- Extract the complete source channel into mono media, keeping clip source offsets, timeline positions, lengths, gain/envelopes, fades and stretch intact. Preserve the source's BWF time reference as well.
- Cache each extracted `(source, channel)` for the command so repeated clips and selected tracks share it. Reuse sources that are already mono, and retain the renderer's channel-wrapping behavior when a track is wider than its source.
- Register the extracted media through the existing source/import path, giving it mono waveform peaks, distinct save paths, and the existing save/reopen behavior. No session schema …

title: Fix master fader automation leaking across render-block boundaries
author: reoniazx
body:
Master fader volume automation could start changing the previous render block when a breakpoint belonged to the next block. This PR makes the master use the same first/last-sample endpoints as track faders, so a gain change starts at its own timeline position and a ramp reaches its requested final value.

## Before: automation leaked into the preceding block

For a block starting at `pos` with `frames` samples, the rendered samples occupy `[pos, pos + frames)`. The master nevertheless evaluated its second volume value at `pos + frames`, the first sample of the next block, and interpolated with a denominator of `frames`.

Track faders already evaluated their second value at `pos + frames - 1` and interpolated over `frames - 1` sample intervals. The different master behavior had two observable consequences:

- A sharp gain change at the next block's start pulled the preceding block toward that future value.
- A ramp whose target was the current block's last sample did not reach that target at the last rendered sample.

This happens in the shared `MixEngine` path used by realtime playback and offline rendering.

## Concrete before/after results

### A gain step must start at the next block

The regression fixture uses a synthesized constant signal of amplitude `0.5`, hard-panned left, a stereo master, and a nonzero render start of sample `37`. For a 512-sample block, the current block covers samples `37..548`; the next starts at `549`. The master's volume lane stays at `0 dB` through `548`, then changes to `-60 dB` at `549`.

The correct signal is `0.5` throughout the first block and `0.0005` from the first sample of the next block. Rounded output values are:

| Timeline sample | Position in block | Before | After / expected |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 37 | First sample | 0.500000 | 0.500000 |
| 293 | Relative sample 256 | 0.250250 | 0.500000 |
| 548 | Last sample before the breakpoint | 0.00147559 | 0.500000 |
| 549 | First sample at -60 dB | 0.000500 | 0.000500 |…

title: Fix stale aux and master latency after insert failures
author: reoniazx
body:
When an aux, routing-folder, or master insert produces NaN/infinity and is taken out of the signal path, subsequent blocks should compensate only for the inserts that still process audio. The latency pre-pass was continuing to count the failed insert, so reported delay and aux alignment could remain too long until the engine was reset.

## Root cause

`process_strip()` already skips inserts when `slot.failed` is set, and master insert processing does the same. However, `note_insert_latency()`—the pre-pass used to calculate aux/folder and master delay compensation before routing—only checked whether an insert was active or bypassed.

That let a plugin's audio processing stop while its reported latency continued to influence compensation. On aux/folder strips, this could add an alignment delay for a plugin that was no longer delaying any audio. On masters, the pre-pass could continue inflating the mix's reported total latency.

## Changes

- Add `slot.failed` to the early-exit condition in `note_insert_latency()`, matching the audio-processing eligibility checks. Already-failed plugins are skipped before parameter updates and latency queries.
- Extend the existing test-only NaN plugin wrapper to forward the wrapped plugin's `latency()`, allowing the failure fixture to exercise a real nonzero lookahead.
- Add `failed_inserts_stop_contributing_latency_until_reset`, which checks rendered audio and reported latency across audio, aux, folder, and master tracks.
- Record the fix under G-04 in `docs/gaps.md` and in `ROADMAP.md`, with review dates and revision history.

The production change adds one condition to the existing loop. It introduces no allocation, lock, new parameter, or session-format change.

## Before and after

The regression uses a 48 kHz stereo session with delay compensation enabled and two inserts on the tested strip:

1. A synthetic failing insert with a 5 ms / **240-sample** lookahead that writes NaN into the audio block.
2. A healthy compressor at rati…

title: Fix source offset when trimming the start of a stretched audio clip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/model/src/clip.rs:246 (Clip::trim_start_to, used by crates/engine/src/edit.rs:36 split_clip)` (no existing issue): Splitting or trimming the start of a stretched (vari-speed or conformed) audio clip plays the wrong part of the source.

## Cause
`Clip::trim_start_to` advanced an audio clip's source offset by the raw timeline delta. The mixer plays a stretched clip from `offset + rel / stretch`, so the right half after a split or start trim began at the wrong source sample whenever `stretch != 1.0`.

## Fix
For audio clips with a stretch other than 1.0, `trim_start_to` now advances the offset by `delta / stretch`, rounded to the nearest sample. An invalid stretch is treated as 1.0, as the mixer does. All callers (split, trim start, clear range and others) get the fix because they go through this method.

## Verified
- Regression test `trim_start_of_stretched_audio_advances_offset_by_source_time`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-model --lib trim_start_of_stretched_audio_advances_offset_by_source_time`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Video clips still advance their offset by the raw delta, because the mixer applies `stretch` only to audio. The behaviour for clips with stretch 1.0 is unchanged. MIDI re-anchoring is unchanged.

title: CLI: convert and run reject unknown options and options without values
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`convert` and `run` looked their options up with `arg_value(args, "--flag")` and never checked what was left over, so a misspelled option, an `--option=value` form, or a known option whose value was missing was treated as absent: the command ran, did something other than what was asked, and exited 0.

Both subcommands now parse their options instead of searching for them:

- an unknown option fails with `unknown convert option '--bogus'` (or `unknown run option ...`) and a non-zero exit;
- a known option without its value fails with `--rate needs a value`;
- `--opt=value` is accepted for every option that takes a value, and valueless flags keep working as before.

The parsing lives in `parse_convert_args` / `parse_run_args` so it is testable directly; the new tests cover the unknown-option, missing-value, `--normalise` (rejected) and `--rate=44100` (accepted) cases, and the whole `soundcraft-cli` suite passes (20 tests).

Fixes #549

title: Scroll Into View in the track name menu: the track goes to the top of the Edit window and the left of the Mix
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Right-click a track name and choose Scroll Into View: the track goes to the top of the Edit window and to the left of the Mix.

In Pro Tools, Scroll Into View is in the track name's right-click menu, in both the Edit and the Mix window (not in the Track menu: Track > Scroll to Track... is the dialog one). It scrolls both windows: the track goes to the top of the Edit window and becomes the leftmost Mix strip. This PR adds it to the same shared name menu, outside the `items` list. The window you're not looking at scrolls the next time it's shown. It uses the track you clicked, even when other tracks are selected, and leaves the selection alone. I couldn't find what Pro Tools does with several selected, so happy to switch to the first selected one. Near the end of the session the Edit window scrolls only as far as the wheel and the scroll bar can go (`scroll_by`), so the last tracks come up as far as possible rather than to the very top. A Mix strip whose track is inside a closed folder still scrolls the Mix, but the Edit window stays put and the folder stays closed. In the Mix, egui's `scroll_to_rect` stops one item spacing short of the edge, which left a sliver of the previous strip showing, so the target rect is shifted by that spacing.

It's a view action with no engine command, like Track Height in the same menu. If you'd like it reachable from agents and MCP, I can add one. `track.scroll_to` (Track > Scroll to Track..., Cmd+Alt+F) still only selects the track and doesn't scroll. Happy to make Scroll to Track scroll too, here or separately. Also left out: Ctrl+Shift-click in the Tracks list, which does the same in Pro Tools.

title: VST3: show the plugin's own text for identity-mapped parameters
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #599.

Many VST3 plugins (everything built with JUCE, and the SDK's default `Parameter`) leave `normalizedParamToPlain` as the identity and keep their real range only in `getParamStringByValue`. `param_info` builds the range from `normalizedParamToPlain(0/1)`, so those parameters get 0..1 while keeping their unit label, and the plugin window prints "0.4 dB". The plugin's own text was only used for choice labels.

This adds an optional `PluginEditor::value_text` (default `None`) and implements it on the VST3 editor handle, which already talks to the controller on the main thread; the generic plugin window uses it and falls back to `ParamInfo::format` otherwise. The call happens on the main thread only (`None` elsewhere, in the spirit of #434), and only for the identity case (a plain mapping with a 0..1 range): parameters with a real plain range keep today's formatting ("1.20 kHz"). Like JUCE's label and the SDK's `RangeParameter`, the units come separately from the text, so they are appended unless the text already ends with them.

Happy to use the plugin's text for every continuous parameter instead, as DAWs do. One limitation: a text that depends on other parameters (a time that switches to note values with sync) is asked of the controller, which may not have seen automated values yet while playback runs.

Validation:
- `editor_main_thread`: new fixture params "Level" (identity, text "−6.0", units "dB") and "Drive" (units already in the text); fails on main (`None` instead of `"−6.0 dB"`), passes here. Also checks that "Drive" is not doubled, that Gain and choices keep SoundCraft's format, and `None` once the plugin is gone
- `fixture_e2e identity_mapped_param_text_is_read_on_the_main_thread_only`: the 0..1 range, and `None` off the main thread on macOS/Windows
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-vst3-host --test editor_main_thread --test fixture_e2e`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-dsp -p soundcraft-vst3-host -p soundcraft-playback -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -…

title: Honour start or end given alone in markers.add
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/event.rs:300-305 (add_marker)` (no existing issue): markers.add ignores `start` when `end` is not given and drops the marker at the edit selection instead.

## Cause
`add_marker` only used `start` when `end` was also given, because its match had no arm for `start` alone or `end` alone. Those calls fell through to the default arm, which puts the marker at the edit selection start, or at the transport position if playing. The command still returned success.

## Fix
Added a match arm so a lone `start` or a lone `end` places a point marker at that position, for any marker kind. The `at` and `start`+`end` cases are unchanged. A regression test covers `start` only, `end` only, and `start`+`end`.

## Verified
- Regression test `markers_add_start_or_end_alone_is_used`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib markers_add_start_or_end_alone_is_used`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The default placement when none of `at`, `start` or `end` is given is unchanged, as are the `at` and `start`+`end` cases and the `markers.edit` command. A lone `start` or `end` now takes precedence over `kind: selection`, which previously ignored it.
