title: au-host: open Audio Unit editors (Cocoa views) on macOS (#501)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Audio Units open their own editor on macOS: **Open Plugin Editor** shows the unit's Cocoa view in a host window.

In Logic and other AU hosts, opening an Audio Unit shows the interface the unit declares (`kAudioUnitProperty_CocoaUI`) in a floating window titled with the plug-in's name. The window takes the view's size. Units without a view of their own get generic controls. This PR does the same. `editor()` returns a handle when the unit names a Cocoa view, and the existing button, the Mix window's slot menu and #530's open-on-insert then work as they already do for VST3. The view comes from the unit's `AUCocoaUIBase` factory and goes into an `NSWindow` set up like the VST3 one (floating, closable, not minimizable, out of the Dock). The window follows the view when the view changes its own size: AUNBandEQ and AUNetSend do that right after they appear. Edits made in the view reach the session through a parameter listener, the same way the generic sliders' edits do. The generic sliders tell the view with `AUParameterSet`, and that change is not reported back. Units without a view (AUReverb2, AUMatrixReverb, AUMIDISynth…) keep the generic sliders and the disabled button.

Lifetime rules:
- A view only ever lives inside its window. A view created outside one crashed the process after its unit was disposed (one of CoreAudioAUUI's timers messages a freed object), so the size probe also builds it in a hidden window.
- Views are torn down, and the autorelease pool drained, before the unit is disposed.
- If an instance were destroyed off the main thread with its editor open, the view, the window and the unit are leaked instead of crashing, as VST3 does. `close_editors` already prevents that case.
- An Objective-C exception thrown by a view aborts the process, like a C++ exception escaping a VST3. Catching it would need objc2's `exception` feature and a new package.

Left out:
- AUv3 view controllers (`requestViewController`). au-host doesn't load AUv3 extensions yet, and non…

title: Apply mix.volume once to each member of a targeted mix group
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:206-222 (volume, with set_grouped at 185)` (no existing issue): mix.volume delta_db is applied twice to every member of an active mix group when the whole group is targeted.

## Cause
`mix.volume` calls `set_grouped` for every target, and `set_grouped` also changes every sibling in an active mix group. When several members of one group are targets, each member was changed once for itself and again for every other target. A `delta_db` of -3 gave -6 dB, and an absolute `db` shifted the members' offsets.

## Fix
`volume` records the tracks already moved as group siblings of an earlier target and skips them. The group-expansion logic moved into a small `grouped_ids` helper that `set_grouped` also uses, so its behaviour is unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression tests `volume_delta_on_a_whole_group_applies_once`, `volume_absolute_on_a_whole_group_keeps_offsets`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib whole_group`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other callers of `set_grouped`, such as solo and the toggles, are not changed by this PR.

title: Reject unknown param in automation.clear instead of clearing all lanes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:516 (clear_lane)` (no existing issue): automation.clear with a misspelled or unknown `param` silently deletes every automation lane on the track.

## Cause
`clear_lane` parsed the optional `param` with `str_param(...).and_then(AutoParam::parse)`. A misspelled name became `None`, which is the same as no filter, so `automation.clear` deleted every lane on the targeted tracks and reported success.

## Fix
When `param` is given, `clear_lane` now resolves it through `lane_param`, as `automation.set_point` and `automation.write_range` do. An unknown name returns an `unknown automation param` error and nothing changes. When `param` is absent, the command still clears all lanes.

## Verified
- Regression test `clear_with_unknown_param_keeps_lanes`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib clear_with_unknown_param`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`lane_param` and the other automation commands are unchanged. `lane_param` defaults to volume when `param` is absent, so `clear_lane` doesn't call it in that case. A `param` value that isn't a string is still treated as absent.

title: Keep merging fader gestures once the undo history is full
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:368-381 (Engine::execute_merged, with push_undo at 280-291)` (no existing issue): Fader/knob drags stop collapsing into one undo step once the undo history is full.

## Cause
`Engine::execute_merged` only pops the step just pushed when `undo.len() == before_len + 1`. When the history is at `history_limit`, `push_undo` trims the oldest entry right away, so the length never grows and the pop never fires. Every tick of a fader drag, knob turn or automation pass then stays as its own undo step and pushes real edits out of the history.

## Fix
For a continuing tick with an existing undo entry, `execute_merged` now raises `history_limit` by one while it runs the command, so nothing is trimmed before the extra step is popped. It restores the limit afterwards, including when the command fails. A zero limit still keeps no history.

## Verified
- Regression tests `a_fader_gesture_is_one_undo_step_when_the_history_is_full`, `a_zero_history_limit_keeps_no_undo_entry_for_a_gesture`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test fader_merge_full_history`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`push_undo` and the trimming behaviour of `execute` are unchanged. The first tick of a gesture still creates a normal undo step.

title: Keep playlist sorted after delete_fades trims overlapping clips
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #697

## Cause
`delete_fades` sorts the playlist once, then trims each pair of overlapping neighbours back to their midpoint. If one clip overlaps several later clips, `trim_start_to` can push a clip's start past the start of the clip after it. Nothing sorts again after that loop, so the playlist is left unsorted ("playlist not sorted").

## Fix
`delete_fades` now sorts the playlist again after the trim loop. A unit test covers a clip that overlaps two later clips. The shrunk failing case, which fails on the unfixed code with the same `after edit.fades_delete` "playlist not sorted" error, is added to `random_edits.proptest-regressions`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `delete_fades_keeps_playlist_sorted_when_a_clip_overlaps_several`, `random_edits_keep_the_session_sane`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib delete_fades_keeps_playlist_sorted_when_a_clip_overlaps_several && cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test random_edits random_edits_keep_the_session_sane`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The seed in the issue (`782c51a1…f6b2c`) is shortened, so it can't be added to the regressions file. The shrunk seed added instead hits the same failure. The midpoint trimming logic itself is unchanged.

title: Reject missing or non-numeric values in mix.pan and mix.trim
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:237 (pan); same pattern at mix.rs:76 (mix.trim)` (no existing issue): mix.pan (and mix.trim) silently reset to centre/0 dB when the required `pan`/`db` parameter is missing or not a number.

## Cause
mix.pan and mix.trim read their required `pan` and `db` parameters with `f32_or(..., 0.0)`. That helper falls back to the default when the key is missing or not a number. A call like `mix.pan {tracks:["Kick"]}` or `{pan:"left"}` returned Ok and reset the track to centre (or trim to 0 dB).

## Fix
Both commands now read the parameter strictly. A missing, non-numeric or non-finite `pan`/`db` returns `BadParams` before any track is touched. Valid values are still clamped as before.

## Verified
- Regression tests `mix_pan_rejects_a_missing_or_non_numeric_pan_and_keeps_the_pan`, `mix_trim_rejects_a_missing_or_non_numeric_db_and_keeps_the_trim`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test mix_required_params`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `f32_or` helper and the optional `index` parameter of mix.pan are unchanged. Other commands that use `f32_or` for genuinely optional parameters are unchanged.

title: Saturate note tick addition in event.extract_chords
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/event_more.rs:579-580 (extract_chords)` (no existing issue): event.extract_chords panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' when a MIDI note has a huge start tick.

## Cause
`extract_chords` added the clip's base tick to `n.start` and `n.end()` with plain `+`. A note whose `start_ticks` is near `i64::MAX` in a clip that starts after sample 0 overflowed. Debug builds panicked, and release builds wrapped to a negative tick and silently skipped the note.

## Fix
Both additions in `extract_chords` now use `saturating_add`, as `Note::end()` already does. A huge note is clamped to the clip end and produces no chord, so the command returns `Ok`.

## Verified
- Regression test `extract_chords_survives_huge_note_start`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib extract_chords_survives_huge_note_start`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change `midi.note_add` or `midi.note_edit`, which still only clamp `start_ticks` to at least 0. I also did not change the other tick arithmetic in the command.

title: Apply the MP4 edit list so AAC imports drop encoder delay and padding (#707)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #707.

symphonia-format-isomp4 0.5.5 parses `edts`/`elst` but does not apply it, so `enable_gapless` has no effect for MP4: an AAC/M4A file decodes with the encoder delay (priming) at the start and the padding at the end. The issue's fixture came in as 49,152 frames with the click at 25,024 instead of 48,000 frames with the click at 24,000.

Changes:
- `mp4::edit_trim` reads the edit list of the first sound track (`moov/trak/edts/elst`, versions 0 and 1). It returns the frames to skip (`media_time`, in the media timescale from `mdhd`) and the frames to keep (`segment_duration`, in the movie timescale from `mvhd`), both rescaled to the decoded sample rate. It returns nothing when there is no edit list, more than one entry, an empty edit (`media_time` = -1), or a cut that keeps everything. In those cases the behaviour does not change.
- `symph::run` applies the trim to the decoded channels, and to the counted frames when `count_only` is set. `symph::probe` applies it to the header frame count. So `info`, `convert` and `file.import_audio` all report and produce the trimmed length.

Tests (in `mp4.rs`): a 1024-sample priming cut with a 48,000-frame segment; a 1000 Hz movie clock with a 44.1 kHz media clock and 2112-sample priming (the phone case from the issue); empty and multi-entry edit lists are ignored; the trim cuts every channel.

title: fix(audio-io): report AC-3/E-AC-3 as unsupported instead of malformed (#709)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #709.

AC-3 and E-AC-3 elementary streams have no format reader, so symphonia's probe (`Probe::next`) scans the whole file for a container marker and runs into the end of the data with an `UnexpectedEof` I/O error. `map_err` turned that into `AudioError::Malformed`, so the CLI printed `malformed audio: end of stream` for a file that is fine but simply not a format SoundCraft reads.

`open()` in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs` now maps that end-of-data probe error to `AudioError::Unsupported`, the same variant other formats we don't decode already get (e.g. Ogg Opus: `unsupported audio: core (codec):unsupported codec`):

- data starting with the AC-3/E-AC-3 sync word `0x0B77`: `unsupported audio: AC-3 and E-AC-3 are not supported`
- any other data no reader claims: `unsupported audio: no supported audio format found`

Other probe errors still go through `map_err`, and errors from a reader that did claim the file (truncated or damaged WAV, FLAC, MP4, ...) are still reported as malformed. `probe`, `decode` and so `info`, `convert` and `file.import_audio` all go through `open()`, so every entry path from the issue is covered.

Test: `ac3_is_unsupported_not_malformed` in `crates/audio-io/tests/malformed.rs` checks that an AC-3-style stream gives `Unsupported` mentioning AC-3 from both `decode` and `probe`, and that unrecognised data gives `Unsupported` without the AC-3 mention. Without the fix both come back as `Malformed`.

title: Keep the existing volume lane in automation.clip_gain_to_volume
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:676-681 (clip_gain_to_vol)` (no existing issue): automation.clip_gain_to_volume ignores the existing volume lane, so the level changes after conversion.

## Cause
`clip_gain_to_vol` wrote `fader + clip gain (+ envelope)` into the Volume lane. An existing Volume lane overrides the fader, so the clip's level became `fader + gain` instead of `lane + gain`. The conversion also replaced the lane points at the clip edges, which discarded the existing automation.

## Fix
The converted value is now the lane's value at that point plus the clip gain and the clip's gain envelope. The lane's own points inside the clip also carry the gain. The unchanged lane level is pinned just outside the clip's start and end so the neighbouring segments keep their shape. Without a lane, the fader value is still used.

## Verified
- Regression tests `clip_gain_to_volume_keeps_the_existing_lane`, `clip_gain_to_volume_leaves_audio_outside_the_clip_alone`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib clip_gain_to_volume`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`vol_to_clip_gain` and tracks without Volume automation are unchanged.

title: Fix mono device playback dropping right-channel audio
author: reoniazx
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

A mono audio device currently receives only the left channel of a stereo main mix. For example, `L = 0, R = 0.8` plays silence instead of the expected mono value `0.4`. Surround playback has the same problem after its ITU stereo fold-down: the right side is discarded.

Average both stereo sides at `0.5 * L + 0.5 * R` before device clipping. Surround mixes use that average after the existing ITU fold-down. Centered mono tracks retain their rendered level and pan law. The new mono average also contains non-finite results from opposing overflowed surround sides, so they cannot reach the device as NaN. The change adds no allocations or blocking operations to the callback.

## Before and after testing

The PR is based directly on upstream `main` at `f3a1948`. The same three new regression tests were run twice: first with the original output mapping, then with the fix restored.

```sh
cargo test -p soundcraft-playback mono_device -- --nocapture
```

**Before the fix:** exit status 101; **0 passed, 3 failed**.

```text

mono_device_preserves_centered_mono_level_and_includes_surround_right_channels ... FAILED
```

title: macOS: closing the window no longer crashes (#691)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Fixes #691

## Cause

When the window closes, or Quit SoundCraft sets `quit_requested` and `logic` sends `ViewportCommand::Close`, eframe drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still running. On a Mac with a Touch Bar, AppKit's Touch Bar code then raises an uncaught Objective-C exception (`-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]`) and the app crashes. This is storytold/craft-libs#3, the crash that `craft-quit` was added for.

## Change

- The close handling in `logic` moves into `close_window` in `apps/soundcraft/src/main.rs`, which ends with `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)`. When the window may close, it cancels the close and quits through `-[NSApplication terminate:]`. A close held for the Unsaved Changes prompt is left alone. On other platforms it does nothing.
- `on_exit` (autosave, preferences, player and plugin-host shutdown) still runs: `terminate:` reaches winit's `applicationWillTerminate:`, which runs eframe's exit handling and `on_exit` before AppKit ends the process.
- `craft-quit` is a workspace dependency pinned to the craft-libs rev that `craft-ui` already uses (`650b1c0`), with the `egui` feature in `apps/soundcraft`. `Cargo.lock` gains only `craft-quit`; its other dependencies were already locked.
- pdfcraft calls `on_close_request` the same way (storytold/pdfcraft#1533).
- A second commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

## Tests

Three new tests in `apps/soundcraft/src/main.rs`:

- `closing_a_saved_session_quits_through_the_platform_on_macos`
- `closing_with_unsaved_changes_asks_and_does_not_quit`
- `quit_from_the_menu_closes_the_window_then_quits_through_the_platform_on_macos`

On macOS the first and third fail without the `on_close_request` call.

On a MacBook Pro without a Touch Bar (macOS 27.0.1), a debug build started with `--demo --no-audio --control 0` exits with status 0 both after `app.quit` on the control channel and after a click on the close button. eframe logs "Closing of root viewport canceled with ViewportCom…

title: Bounce: report the levels of the clipped samples that are written (#717)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #717.

When a mix goes over full scale, every bounce encoder (WAV, AIFF, FLAC; float and integer) clamps each sample to [-1, 1] and writes NaN as 0 (`clamp_float` / `Quantizer::quantize` in `audio-io/src/pcm.rs`). `Bounce` measured `peak_db`, `lufs` and `true_peak_db` on the block *before* that clamp. So the `file.bounce_mix` result (and the "Bounced ... (peak ..., LUFS)" status in the app) could say +3.5 dBFS for a file that never goes above 0 dBFS.

**Fix**

In the writing pass, `Bounce::step` now clamps the block the same way the encoders do (NaN to 0, then clamp to [-1, 1]) before it meters and writes it. The written bytes do not change, because the encoders clamp first in the same way. The report now describes the file. Stem bounces (`bounce_stems`) use the same `Bounce`, so they get the fix too.

The normalize measuring pass is not changed. It still measures the unclamped peak, so normalizing a hot mix to -0.1 dBFS works like before. After that gain nothing goes over full scale, so the clamp does nothing in the writing pass.

**Tests**

`a_clipping_bounce_reports_the_levels_of_the_clipped_file` (in `crates/engine/tests/bounce.rs`) raises every clip of the demo session by +36 dB, checks that the rendered mix peaks above 1.0, bounces it to 32-bit float WAV, then decodes the file and checks that the reported peak, LUFS and true peak are the same as the values measured on the file (and that the peak is at most 0 dBFS). It uses the same checks as the existing `bounces_write_exactly_the_mix_and_report_its_levels`. Without the fix, the reported peak is above 0 dBFS and the test fails.

title: Audio import: check Matroska element sizes before symphonia allocates them
author: PierrunoYT
body:
symphonia's Matroska reader (`symphonia-format-mkv` 0.5.5) allocates whatever an element, a laced frame or a Vorbis codec header claims before reading it (`read_boxed_slice_exact` → `vec![0; len]`). It checks a child against its parent, but never against the file. Formats are detected by magic, so a crafted file under any extension (even `.wav`) reaches it. `audio-io` already pre-checks CAF, MP4, FLAC and RIFF for exactly this reason (`symph::open`), but Matroska had no check.

Reproduced on `main` (c1bf044, release build): `probe` on this 30-byte file
```
1A 45 DF A3 01 00 FF FF FF FF FF FF   EBML header, size 2^48-1
42 82 01 00 80 00 00 00 00 00         DocType, size 2^47
6D 61 74 72 6F 73 6B 61               "matroska"
```
prints `memory allocation of 140737488355328 bytes failed` and the process aborts. Neither `symph::guarded`'s nor `Engine::execute`'s `catch_unwind` can catch an allocation failure. This is reachable from File › Import Audio, drag and drop, sampler load and clip-group import. Because `session.open` decodes every source, a session referencing such a file aborts on every open.

**Fix:** a new `audio-io/src/mkv.rs` walks the elements before symphonia's reader is created, the way symphonia reads them:
- master elements are descended, unknown sizes run to the parent's end, and the resync after an unreadable ID is followed;
- a leaf larger than the bytes left in the file is refused;
- so is a SimpleBlock/Block whose Xiph- or EBML-laced frame sizes exceed the block, or `A_VORBIS` codec private data whose header packets exceed it;
- a zero first size byte, which symphonia reads as a size near 2^63, is refused for leaves;
- nesting deeper than 32 is refused;
- a file merely cut short inside a header is left to symphonia, which stops before allocating.

The error is `Malformed("Matroska … is larger than the file")`, matching the CAF, MP4 and FLAC checks.

**Tests:** `matroska_sizes_beyond_the_file_are_errors_not_aborts` in `tests/malformed.rs`.
- A well-…

title: H.264: build only the frame_num gap frames that stay references (#429)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Fixes #429.

When a slice's `frame_num` jumps, `Dpb::fill_frame_num_gap` inserted a "non-existing" frame for every missing frame number. For each one, `make_frame` in `start_picture` built a full picture: a crop-copy of the last decoded frame, or a grey plane set, plus `Frame::from_planes`. With `log2_max_frame_num = 16`, a single slice header could trigger up to 65,535 frame-sized allocations and copies. On native that ties up the only `video-decode` worker for a very long time at large picture sizes; on web it ties up the UI thread.

**Why skipping is safe.** The sliding window (8.2.5.3) keeps at most `max_num_ref_frames` references and always drops the short-term frame with the smallest `FrameNumWrap` first. Gap frames are the newest short-term frames. So of a gap longer than `max_num_ref_frames`, only the last `max_num_ref_frames` frames can still be in the DPB when the gap ends. Every earlier one is built only to be evicted.

**Fix.** `fill_frame_num_gap` now calls `poc_state` for every missing frame number, so POC derivation is unchanged. It runs the sliding window and `make_frame`, and pushes an entry, only for the last `max_num_ref_frames` of them. That is at most 16 pictures per gap instead of up to 65,535. The decoder side (`start_picture`) is untouched.

**Tests** (new `dpb::tests`):
- `skipping_unseen_gap_frames_leaves_the_dpb_as_building_them_would` compares the DPB after `fill_frame_num_gap` with a naive implementation of 8.2.5.2 that builds every frame. It starts from a DPB holding a long-term reference, a short-term reference waiting for output, and another short-term reference. It runs seven gaps: long, short, shorter than the window, a window of 1, wrapping past `MaxFrameNum`, and so on. Both DPBs end up the same (frame numbers, marks, output flags, non-existing flags).
- `a_frame_num_gap_builds_only_the_frames_that_stay_references`: a 65,534-number gap (10 → 9 with `MaxFrameNum` 65536, wrapping) calls `poc_state` 65,534 times but builds exactly 4 …

title: Mix: keep clip effects gain and send-level lanes within their ranges
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Two gain paths took whatever number a session file or a command supplied, and `db_to_gain` only stops at +200 dB (about ×10¹⁰).

- **Clip Effects gain.** `clip.effects_set` stores any finite value, and `ClipFx::configure` applied `clip_fx.<id>.gain` as given (`self.gain_db = v`). The window's slider is -36…+24 dB, but a session file or an MCP/control call can say `500`.
- **Send-level automation.** `AutomationLane::set_point` clamps to `AutoParam::range()` (-144…+12 dB for sends), but lanes loaded from a file only went through `retain(|p| p.value.is_finite())` in `Session::sanitize`, and `send_level` returned the lane value raw. Volume is protected by `v0.min(12.0)`; sends weren't.

Either way, an audible clip or send becomes a full-scale clipped signal through the speakers or headphones as soon as playback reaches it. A shared session is enough to trigger it.

**Changes:**
- `ClipFx::configure` clamps gain to `MIN_DB..=+24 dB` (`CLIP_FX_MAX_GAIN_DB`) and treats a non-finite value as 0 dB.
- `Session::sanitize` clamps each loaded automation point to `param.range()`, as `set_point` already does for points written in the app. Plugin lanes have the full `f32` range, so they are unchanged; plugins clamp their own parameters.
- `send_level` caps the lane value at +12 dB, as volume does.

**Tests:**
- `mix::tests::clip_effects_gain_and_send_level_lanes_stay_in_range` covers clip gain 500 (rendered exactly as +24 dB), a NaN gain (rendered as 0 dB), and a send-level lane point of 300 inserted directly (rendered the same as +12 dB). Without the fix the first assertion sees a sample of `3539729000`.
- `model::session::tests::sanitize_repairs` now also checks that send-level points of 300 and -1e9 come back as 12 and -144.

title: MIDI import: refuse files with more tempo changes than performances have
author: PierrunoYT
body:
`import_midi_bytes` caps meter changes at `MAX_MIDI_METERS` (10,000), because placing each meter walks the ones before it. Tempo events had no cap: every `FF 51` in a file went into `session.tempo`.

`TempoMap::tick_to_samples_f` / `samples_to_ticks_f` walk every tempo event on each call. The mix engine calls them per note (`schedule_notes`), per click, and per automation and grid lookup, many times per audio block, on the audio thread during playback. A ~7 MB SMF made of a million `01 FF 51 03 0F 42 40` events (all valid, 60 bpm) imports cleanly today. Every conversion then becomes a million-step loop: audio-callback overruns and UI stalls in any session that imported it. The map is also cloned into every undo snapshot.

**Change:** `MAX_MIDI_TEMPOS = 10_000`, checked next to the meter cap and before anything is touched. It returns `MIDI file: more than 10000 tempo changes`. For scale, a tempo change on every beat at 120 bpm is 1,200 events for ten minutes.

**Test:** `io::name_tests::midi_with_more_tempo_changes_than_performances_have_is_refused`.
- A file with 10,001 tempo changes is refused, and the session is left untouched: one tempo, no tracks.
- A file with exactly 10,000 imports with all 10,000.

`cargo test --no-fail-fast -p soundcraft-engine` passes locally on Windows except the pre-existing Windows-only `saved_audio_is_trusted_only_in_the_folder_it_was_saved_in` (path separator in the test, fixed in #749). `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: Player: drop plugin instances on the UI thread before closing the stream (quit hung with Jup-8000 V)
author: derekmwright
body:
## What

Quitting SoundCraft with a hosted instrument loaded could hang with the window frozen. Seen on Windows 11 with Arturia's Jup-8000 V (VST3) once the plug-in was actually running (a preset loaded, notes played): close the window, the window stops repainting, the process stays.

**Cause.** `on_exit` drops the `Player`, which closes the cpal stream, which joins the audio thread. The callback owns the `MixEngine`, so on its way out the audio thread dropped every plug-in instance, and `Instance::drop` (`setActive(false)`, `terminate`) ran on the audio thread. Jup-8000 V's `terminate` waits for the UI thread. The UI thread was the one waiting in the join. Minidump of the hung process:

- main thread: `eframe … save_and_destroy` → `on_exit` → player drop → `cpal::host::wasapi::stream` drop → `std::thread::Thread::join`
- audio thread: `Vst3Plugin` drop glue → `soundcraft_vst3_host::ffi::Instance::drop` → `Jup-8000 V.vst3` → `NtWaitForSingleObject`

`vst3-host`'s own comment on `Instance` already notes that VST3 expects `setActive` and the controller calls on the UI thread and that they "may then happen on the audio thread". This is the case where that matters.

**Fix.** `Player` gets a `Drop`: it sends a new `Cmd::Drain`, the callback answers with every instance it holds (`MixEngine::drain_plugins`, which already existed for the sample-rate change), the instances are dropped on the UI thread, and only then does the stream close. Bounded at 1.5 s so a device that has stopped calling cannot hang the quit; in that case the instances go down with the stream as before.

No change for the built-in engine path, wasm (no `Drop` there), or sessions without third-party plug-ins (the drain returns an empty list).

## Testing

- New: `playback` `drain_hands_every_instance_back_instead_of_dropping_it_on_the_audio_thread`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback` (30), `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` on `playback`, `xtask layers`.

title: Keep MP3 length and timing when a packet fails to decode
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #710

## Cause
symphonia 0.5.5 rejects valid MP3 frames whose last granule has no bits ("invalid main_data offset"). `run` in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs` then skipped these packets without putting anything in their place, so the imported audio came in shorter and everything after a dropped frame started early.

## Fix
When a packet fails to decode, `run` now adds its length (`packet.dur` minus trims, capped at `MAX_PACKET_FRAMES`) to a pending count of lost frames. Once the channel count is known, that count goes into the frame total and is written as silence in the packet's place, both for decode and for probe's counting path. Lost frames stay pending until they are written, so leading failures are kept too.

## Verified
- Regression test `mp3_frames_with_an_empty_last_granule_keep_their_length`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io --test mp3_empty_granule`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The symphonia MP3 decoder is unchanged, so these frames are not decoded. The whole frame, in every channel, is replaced by silence. That keeps the length and the timing of the following audio, but any sound the frame carries is lost. In the reported fixture the left channel's noise is lost, so the output is not the real audio of those frames.

title: Bounce the whole session when CLI --bounce has no range
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #745

## Cause
When neither --start nor --end was given, the CLI's `--bounce` called `file.bounce_mix` with no range, so it used the edit selection left behind by the script's commands. Command params read a bare number as samples, so `edit.select {"start":0,"end":19.2}` selects 19 samples, and the bounce came out as a 0.0004 s file at -144 LUFS.

## Fix
If neither --start nor --end is given, `finish()` in soundcraft-cli now passes start 0 and end = the session's content end, so the bounce covers the whole session. The usage text now says this and lists --start/--end for `script`.

## Verified
- Regression test `script_bounce_without_range_covers_the_session`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-cli --test cli script_bounce_without_range_covers_the_session`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`file.bounce_mix` still falls back to the edit selection when it is called with no range from the app, MCP or control channel. A bare number in command params still means samples. If only one of --start/--end is given, the behaviour is the same as before.

title: Mix tests: never load real plug-ins (cargo test hangs on machines with plug-ins installed)
author: derekmwright
body:
## What

`cargo test -p soundcraft-mix` cannot finish on a developer machine that has real VST3 or CLAP plug-ins
installed. The test `stored_state_comes_first_then_session_params` ends with an offline `render_range` over a
session that holds a `vst3:...` insert. With external instances off, `make()` calls `create_instance`, and
`create_plugin` falls through to the real hosts. Those hosts scan the system plug-in folders and load every
installed plug-in in-process. Some plug-ins (Native Instruments) never unload, so the test binary hangs and
cannot be killed. On Windows 11 the hung processes held Analog Lab V and Battery 4 open. CI has no plug-ins
installed, so CI stays green and only contributors see the hang. It happened four times in one day.

The fix is a `#[cfg(test)]` guard at the top of `create_plugin`. Third-party ids (`is_third_party`) return
`None` under test, with a comment giving the reason. The rule is stated in the `tests` module doc: tests adopt
fakes under `clap:test.*` ids via `MixEngine::adopt` and never call the real hosts. The test keeps its final
check, that an uncreatable third-party plug-in is absent and the signal passes through. That is what it
already asserted.

The guard is compiled only under `cfg(test)` of the mix crate. Production code is unchanged.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-mix --lib` completes with no `--skip`. It runs 39 tests on this branch. Before
  this change the run hung after the first ~40 s.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `xtask layers` are clean.
- Negative check: without the guard, the same command ran for over 10 minutes, with the test binary stuck in
  the plug-in unload.

title: Hosted plug-ins: run the engine for them while stopped, suspend each by its own status and tail (Guitar Rig 7 / Helix Native editors froze)
author: derekmwright
body:
## What

While the transport is stopped, the mix engine runs only when a track is armed, input monitoring is on, or
a live note is sounding. That is a global switch. It saves idle CPU, but a hosted plug-in gets no `process`
calls while the switch is off, and some plug-ins depend on those calls:

- Guitar Rig 7 and Line 6 Helix Native: an effect on an idle audio track opens its editor and never finishes
  loading. The GUI ignores clicks until transport runs. The stall is inside the plug-in: the editor window
  answers, so input reaches it.

This PR does not change the switch. It makes each hosted effect report what it needs, and the mixer uses
that to skip the effect when it has nothing to do. The formats already carry the signals:

- CLAP: `clap_process_status` after each block (`CONTINUE`, `CONTINUE_IF_NOT_QUIET`, `TAIL`, `SLEEP`).
- VST3: the host sets `silenceFlags` on each input bus; the plug-in reports its tail with `getTailSamples()`
  (`kInfiniteTail` means keep calling).

Suspension is per plug-in. A hosted effect is skipped only when its own status and tail allow it, and it
resumes on the first non-silent input block.

**What each crate does**

- `soundcraft_dsp`: adds `ProcessStatus { Continue, ContinueIfNotQuiet, Tail, Sleep }`, and two methods on
  `Plugin`: `process_status()` and `set_input_silent(bool)`.
- `clap-host`: returns the status from the last `process` call. Inputs known to be silent are marked with
  `constant_mask`.
- `vst3-host`: sets `silenceFlags` from `set_input_silent`. Derives `Tail` from a finite tail and `Continue`
  from `kInfiniteTail`.
- `soundcraft-mix`: keeps, per hosted insert slot, how long its input has been silent. `run_insert` skips
  `process` by these rules:
  - `Sleep` and `ContinueIfNotQuiet`: skip while the input is silent.
  - `Tail`: process for `tail_samples()` after the input goes silent, then skip.
  - `Continue`: never skip.
  - A non-silent input resumes processing at once.
  - Silence means every sample is exac…

title: Notes are always released: clip-end note-off on a block boundary, reset keeps releases (#441), All MIDI Notes Off wired, end-of-selection stop releases
author: derekmwright
body:
## What

A note from a MIDI clip could hold forever, with no way to silence it. Four separate defects produced it, and
they were found together:

- (a) `schedule_notes` clamps a note's off to `clip.end()`, but it skipped the clip for any block starting at
  or after that end. An off landing exactly on a block boundary was never sent. At 48 kHz and 120 BPM a bar is
  750 blocks of 128 samples, so a clip ending on a bar line hit this every time.
- (b) `MixEngine::reset` calls `all_notes_off()` and then `reset()`. In both hosts, `reset()` cleared the queue
  that held the just-queued note-offs, so Stop released nothing. This is the mechanism behind #441, the upstream
  audit issue that described it on 2026-10-13 and was closed on 2026-10-18. This PR addresses it.
- (c) `event.all_notes_off` ("All MIDI Notes Off", Event menu, Cmd+Shift+.) existed, but its UI handler was an
  empty arm.
- (d) Reaching the playback end point (`AudioState::render_next`, `pos >= end`) stopped playback without the
  `mix.reset()` that Stop performs. The last note of a selected clip always hung, because a selected clip plays
  its selection and stops at the end.

Commits, one fix each:

- The clip is let through when `clip.end() == pos`, so the clip-end off is sent.
- `reset()` in both hosts converts held keys to queued offs and keeps the queued offs. The decision is a pure
  function, `keep_releases_on_reset`.
- `Cmd::AllNotesOff`, `Player::all_notes_off` and `MixEngine::all_notes_off` are wired to the menu command.
- The end-point branch calls `mix.reset()`.

## Testing

- `a_note_off_on_the_clip_end_block_boundary_is_sent` (`mix`).
- `reset_keeps_the_releases_it_owes` (`vst3-host` and `clap-host`).
- `all_notes_off_releases_every_held_note_without_resetting` (`mix`).
- `all_notes_off_reaches_the_instrument` (`playback`).
- `reaching_the_end_releases_held_notes` (`playback`).

title: Pause the output stream while the input stream is opened or closed (cpal ASIO deadlock on arming or loading an armed session)
author: derekmwright
body:
## What

Loading a session with armed tracks on ASIO froze the app. The setup was Windows 11, a Focusrite USB ASIO
device, 48 kHz and 128 samples.

A minidump shows the main thread in `asio_sys::Driver::create_streams`, reached from cpal's
`prepare_input_stream`, `Device::get_or_create_input_stream`, `record::Recorder::open_with` and the UI. A second
thread is in `Mutex::lock_contended` inside cpal's ASIO callback. In cpal 0.16.0 (`host/asio/stream.rs`),
`get_or_create_input_stream` holds the `asio_streams` mutex while the driver recreates its buffers. That stops a
running driver with `ASIOStop`. `ASIOStop` waits for the driver's callback thread, and that thread is inside
cpal's output callback waiting for the same mutex. The comment there reads "0% chance of lock contention, the
host only locks when recreating streams". The deadlock happens whenever a callback is in flight while the input
is created or destroyed. At 128 samples that is nearly always.

The fix is in SoundCraft:

- `Player::with_output_paused` pauses the output stream. cpal's `pause` only flips a flag that the callbacks
  check before they take the lock.
- It waits two buffer periods (`reconfigure_settle`: 512 frames when the buffer size is unknown, clamped to
  5 to 50 ms).
- It runs the open or close, then resumes the output.
- The UI opens and closes the recorder inside this helper. Quit closes the input before dropping the output.

The pause applies to every backend. On WASAPI, pause and play is a stop and restart with no side effects. The
stall watchdog needs 2 seconds, so the pause does not trigger it.

This is a host-side workaround. The root cause is in cpal, and a cpal issue is not yet filed.

## Testing

- `with_output_paused_runs_once_and_returns_on_the_silent_clock`.
- `reconfigure_settle_is_two_buffers_clamped`.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo xtask layers` are clean. Test counts on the branch: playback 31 (including the two new tests).

The d…

title: Keep unity-gain clips unchanged when coalescing clip gain to volume
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit_more.rs:825-845 (coalesce_clip_gain_to_volume)` (no existing issue): Coalesce Clip Gain to Volume raises the level of unity-gain clips that sit before a boosted clip.

## Cause
`coalesce_clip_gain_to_volume` built the volume-lane breakpoints only from clips with non-zero gain or a gain envelope. `AutomationLane::value_at` holds the first and last point values outside the breakpoints, so unity-gain clips before the first or after the last boosted clip played at the boosted clip's level.

## Fix
Breakpoints are now added at the start and end of every audio clip, including unity-gain ones. The gain lookup also covers every audio clip, so each unity clip is anchored at its own level. Clips are still only coalesced on tracks that have at least one boosted clip.

## Verified
- Regression test `coalesce_clip_gain_keeps_unity_clips_unchanged`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib coalesce_clip_gain_keeps_unity_clips_unchanged`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`clip_gain_to_vol` in `mix.rs`, which ignores the existing volume lane, is a separate function and is unchanged.

title: Heal separations left by a cut, not only splits
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #772

## Cause
`heal` only merged neighbouring clips that touched exactly (`prev.end() == c.start`) and whose source offsets ran on directly (`oa + prev.length == ob`). After a cut, the two pieces have a gap between them on the timeline and in the source, so Heal Separation never rejoined them.

## Fix
`heal` now treats two neighbours as a separation when the second starts at or after the first one's end, the gap lies within the selection, and the timeline gap equals the source-offset gap. The merged clip runs from the first clip's start to the second clip's end. The new test `edit::tests::heal_rejoins_cut_separation` covers a cut, a selection that doesn't span the gap, shuffled pieces, pieces that were moved apart, and overlapping neighbours whose offsets line up. Overlapping neighbours are rejected by the `c.start >= prev.end()` check.

## Verified
- Regression test `edit::tests::heal_rejoins_cut_separation`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib edit::tests::heal_rejoins_cut_separation`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `edit.heal` command handler and its enable logic are unchanged. They already call `ops::heal` for each track.

title: Localization: packed zh-hans catalogs, language preference and web Han font
author: wayward-L
body:
# Localization: packed zh-hans catalogs, language preference and web Han font

SoundCraft ships Simplified Chinese through the same lightweight, build-time-packed catalog pipeline as our sibling craft apps: English source strings are the keys, one UTF-8 TSV per language, and a small runtime lookup (`t/tr/tr_ctx/tr_id/trn/fmt`) with English fallback.

## Catalog pipeline

- `crates/ui-egui/build.rs` packs every `src/i18n/*.tsv` at compile time into `OUT_DIR/i18n/`: one shared, deduplicated key table (`keys.deflate`) plus a per-catalog marker stream (`<code>.tsv.deflate`, `\x01` next-key / `\x02` relative index / `\x03` escaped literal line), Deflate-best compressed. The runtime embeds it with `include_bytes!`, inflates with a 16 MiB cap, validates offsets, and falls back to English on bad data — never panics.
- Catalog format is unchanged (`context<TAB>source<TAB>translation`, `@plural`, comments pass through the packer); the shipped catalog has no `@id` rows. Language codes are lowercase BCP 47 (`zh-hans`), matching the stored preference value; previously saved `zh-Hans` values still resolve.
- The shipped catalog has **1,139 entries** (1,123 plain, 9 `@plural`, 7 automation-context) covering every menu-tree label and path segment, every UI and engine command label, and every literal UI string (`t("…")` plus the tooltip arguments of `icon_button`/`text_toggle`) — enforced by tests.
- `tl!` was removed; `t()` is the literal API.

## Language preference

- `interface.language` is an engine preference (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`): default `auto`, validated as non-empty, at most 16 characters of ASCII letters/digits/`-`; `prefs.get` / `prefs.set` / `prefs.reset` are commands (query specs, not part of the document or undo), with all-or-nothing `prefs.set`.
- Native: `<settings>/preferences.json`, lenient bounded load (64 KiB), atomic temp+rename write on revision change and exit, one-time migration of a legacy `ui.language` from `ui.json`, `SOUNDCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` / `po…

title: Fix empty SMF export re-importing as one phantom empty track
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/midi/src/smf.rs:207` (no existing issue): Empty SMF export re-imports as one phantom empty track.

## Cause
write_smf always wrote a conductor track, and read_smf only folded a leading conductor track into the global lists when the file had more than one track. A file with zero content tracks came back with one empty track, whether the Smf was fully empty or held only tempos, meters, key signatures or markers.

## Fix
write_smf now omits the conductor track when the Smf has no global data and no content tracks. read_smf now also folds a lone, unnamed, note-less and controller-less track into the globals when it carried tempo, meter, marker or key-signature data. A conductor-only Smf therefore reads back with 0 tracks and keeps its global data. The regression test covers an empty Smf, a conductor-only Smf with one tempo, and a single empty content track.

title: fix(ui): bare "=" key nudges the selected clip right, matching "-"
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
Fixes #736.

## Cause

`edit.nudge`'s registered shortcut is `"Plus/Minus"`, matched in `shortcuts.rs` as `Key::Plus | Key::Minus`. On a real keyboard, `Key::Minus` is what a bare, unshifted "-" press sends — so nudge-left just works. But `Key::Plus` is only ever sent by a dedicated key that doesn't need Shift (a numpad `+`); typing "+" on the main row always needs Shift, and Shift+=/- is already a separate, intentional shortcut (steps the Grid value, `shortcuts.rs:125`). So nudge-right was unreachable on any keyboard without a numpad, while nudge-left worked fine — exactly the asymmetry in the report.

## Fix

Add `Key::Equals` (the bare key the "+"/"=" symbol sits on) to the nudge match arm, the same way `Key::Minus` already works. Also added `!m.alt`, since `Alt+=` is the separate, already-registered `window.event_list` shortcut (`Alt+'`/`Alt+6`/`Alt+7` siblings) that this change would otherwise shadow — caught by the existing `window_keys_open_their_windows` test failing once I added `Equals` to the arm.

## Verified

- Reproduced live first: built the app, ran a demo session with `--control`, selected a clip, and sent synthetic key events over the control channel. Plain `-` moved the clip; plain `=` and Shift+`=` both did nothing — confirmed the exact bug before writing any fix.
- New test `bare_plus_and_minus_nudge_the_selected_clip_in_edit` (`tests/shortcuts.rs`): isolated and run alone against the pre-fix code — fails at the same point the live test did (`left: 395077, right: 443077`). Passes after the fix.
- Added `Key::Plus` and `Alt+Equals` coverage to the same test, since those are the two existing behaviors most likely to regress from this change (a numpad `+` must still nudge; `Alt+=` must still open the MIDI Event List, not nudge).

title: Preserve finite headroom in Float32 WAV and AIFF-C encoding
author: mattburlage
body:
Float32 WAV and AIFF-C encoding clipped finite samples to ±1.0. For example, -2.0 and 1.25 became -1.0 and 1.0, so later gain reduction could not recover the peaks. Preserve finite Float32 samples in both `encode()` and `FileEncoder`, while keeping integer PCM clipping and the existing NaN/infinity handling.

Regression tests check stored bytes and decoded values across both formats and encoder APIs, including dither settings, signed zero, subnormals, maximum finite values, and buffer boundaries. A generated signal above full scale checks `file.bounce_mix` without inserts or normalization, then with normalization enabled; file samples and reported peak, LUFS and true peak must agree. Update the progress records and add the contributor's chosen display name.

Validation on macOS with Rust 1.97.1:

- The new whole-file, streaming, and bounce headroom tests failed on the original code, then passed with this fix.
- All 27 focused encoder and bounce tests passed.
- `cargo +1.97.1 xtask ci` passed: formatting, Clippy, 1,149 tests, assets, layers, and WASM. One existing video performance test is ignored.
- Code review found no issues.

Related to #717. The unconditional Float32 clamp proposed in #734 conflicts with this fix; the new bounce test detects that loss of headroom.

Fixes #791.

title: macOS: sign the app and CLI with the plug-in-hosting entitlement (#153)
author: resname
body:
## Problem

Reported from a macOS run (SoundCraft 0.8.0, Apple silicon): every third-party plug-in fails to load and the plug-in scan finds none of them. The log is one long wall of these, one per vendored plug-in (Vital, Kontakt, Kilohearts, Melda, Waves, nih-plugs …):

```
WARN [main] soundcraft_vst3_host::registry: cannot load VST3 plugin /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Kontakt 8.vst3:
dlopen(...): tried: '...' (code signature in <4E9CEA88-…> '...' not valid for use in process:
mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs)
```

## Root cause

`packaging/macos/package.sh` signs the app with hardened runtime (`--options runtime`) plus `entitlements.plist`, which granted only `com.apple.security.device.audio-input`. With the hardened runtime, **library validation is on by default**: the mapping process only accepts code signed by the same Team ID (or a platform binary). A plug-in host is signed with one Team ID while vendors sign their plug-ins with theirs — so every third-party CLAP/VST3/AU bundle is rejected at `dlopen`, exactly as the log shows. This is tracked as #153 (user reports: #153, closed #149 "vst on mac").

Hosting third-party, vendor-signed plug-ins *is* the product, so a DAW host must accept them: the standard fix (Logic, Ableton, Reaper, …) is the `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` entitlement.

## Changes

- `packaging/macos/entitlements.plist`: add `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` with the reason, and correct the header comment (the host does map third-party plug-in code).
- `packaging/macos/package.sh`: sign `soundcraft-cli` with the same entitlements — the CLI hosts plug-ins in-process through `engine`/`mix`, and it was signed with hardened runtime and *no* entitlements, so it has the same failure.
- `xtask/src/main.rs`: regression test asserting the entitlement exists and that the app executable, the app bundle and the CLI are all signed with it.
- Progress docs per convention: `gaps.md` (…

title: fix(ui): open the plugin's own editor, not the generic panel, on insert
author: NDIO-AI
body:
## Problem

Inserting a plugin that has a native editor also opened SoundCraft's generic parameter panel, leaving a ghost panel behind the plugin's own window. Two paths caused it:

- **On insert**, the generic panel was pushed before the player had created the instance, so `has_editor` was still false.
- **On click**, an occupied insert always opened the generic panel, even when the plugin had a native editor.

## Fix

- `Player::plugin_ready(track, slot)` exposes whether the side thread has prepared (or refused) the slot's instance, so the UI can tell “this plugin has no native editor” from “the instance is still being created”.
- `open_inserted` keeps its pending request until the instance is ready, then opens the native editor instead of falling back to the generic panel during the race.
- A shared `open_plugin()` opens the native editor when the slot has one and the generic window otherwise. Insert clicks, instrument clicks and open-on-insert all use it.
- The insert menu now has explicit **Open/Close Plugin Editor** and **Edit Parameters…** entries, so the generic panel is still available when wanted.

## Scope

UI/playback only; no host or packaging changes. Verified with the current VST3 host (TrackPlug 7) and the AU host from #687 (bx_tonebox, RX 11 De-hum): the native window opens with no generic panel behind it, and `plugin_windows` has no entry for those slots.

No entitlement change: #793 already covers that. This makes AU editors open correctly once #687 lands.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --test open_on_insert --test plugin_window` — all pass (built-in inserts still open their generic window, which is the correct behavior for plugins without a native editor).
- Manual checks on macOS with the plugins listed above.

title: Import external-WAV AAF as editable session data (pure Rust)
author: vhhr7
body:
Addresses #40: an AAF handoff from a picture editor can't be opened in SoundCraft as editable tracks.

## What it does

**File → Import → Session Data...** analyzes an AAF, lists its audio tracks and imports the ones you select as new tracks, with one clip per edit. Each clip keeps its offset into the complete source file, so handles stay available for trimming. Tracks are not consolidated. The import is one undo step. Save collects the full sources into the session's Audio Files folder.

Supported subset:
- One CompositionMob whose timeline slots hold SourceClip/Filler sequences.
- Clips resolved through MasterMobs to SourceMobs with a WAVEDescriptor and one external file locator.
- Mono or interleaved stereo PCM WAV.
- Composition timecode and frame rate, including 24000/1001 and drop-frame.

Gain, fades, transitions, selectors, nested sequences, embedded essence, split channels, mixed sample rates and non-local locators fail with an explicit message. A montage that is silently wrong is worse than a refusal.

## How

- `crates/interchange` (new, layer 3; no filesystem, process or UI access):
  - `build_session(Plan)` turns a versioned rational-time plan into a `Session`. Edit endpoints are rounded to samples independently, so adjacent edits share boundaries without drift.
  - `aaf::read_aaf` reads the AAF object model directly from structured storage: properties streams, strong-reference vectors and sets, and dictionary weak references. Media access goes through a `MediaResolver` trait.
- `crates/engine` adds two commands:
  - `file.preview_aaf`: read-only analysis.
  - `file.import_aaf`: undoable insertion.

  The engine's resolver opens only files named exactly in the media folder the user chose. It checks `file_access` and reads WAV headers without loading sample data. The import probes and decodes the media again before it touches the session.

title: Let a soloed VCA solo its members and implicit solo follow aux chains
author: lucasegen
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Two solo cases silence the session instead of letting the soloed audio through.

1. **Soloing a VCA master mutes everything.** The VCA's own `solo` flag counted as "something is soloed", but nothing passed it on to its members. Every track, members included, was solo-muted. A VCA's mute already mutes its members; its solo now solos them, as on the incumbent's VCA masters. A VCA with no members mutes nothing.
2. **Implicit solo stops after one bus.** `receives_solo` only looked at tracks writing directly onto an aux's input bus. With `track → bus 1 → aux 1 → bus 2 → aux 2 → main`, soloing the track kept aux 1 audible but muted aux 2, so the soloed signal never reached the main mix. The same happens through sends, for example a reverb return that feeds a further aux.

## Change

- `solo_reach` computes, once per block, which tracks the solo lets through.
  - It starts from the soloed tracks: their own solo, or the solo of their VCA.
  - It then adds every active aux or folder track whose input bus they feed, hop after hop. Only those strips read their input bus. An audio track whose input is a bus plays its own clips, so it is not added: the solo mutes it like any other track that is not soloed, `solo_safe` still exempts it, and it passes no solo on to the auxes after it.
  - It walks in processing order (producers first), so a chain usually takes one pass. A pass that marks nothing ends the walk, so routing loops terminate.
  - Inactive tracks pass no solo on.
- It fills a `Vec<bool>` kept on `MixEngine`, cleared and refilled each block, so there is no allocation in steady state. With nothing soloed it returns after one scan.
- `process_strip` takes `solo_muted` instead of `any_solo`. `solo_safe` still exempts a track.
- `soundcraft_mix::solo_muted_tracks(session)` exposes the same rule for displays, for every track in one pass. The Edit window calls it once per frame and hands each track header its own value.

title: Mix: realtime headroom on large sessions (strips stay on the audio thread, clips by index)
author: mrrobbiec
body:
Three changes to realtime rendering that matter on large sessions. Found on a real one: an edited drum mix with 42 tracks, 63,424 clips and four VST3 drum instruments, at 48 kHz / 128 samples through ASIO (Audient iD14). It glitched constantly; with these changes (and #805 for the UI side) it plays cleanly.

## 1. Strips stay on the audio thread unless a block is heavy

`MixEngine::render` handed every block's strips to the global rayon pool, and the calling thread blocked until they were done. From the audio callback, `par_iter_mut` goes through `in_worker_cold`, so a profile of the render loop spent ~65% of its samples in rayon's `LockLatch::wait_and_reset`. The time-critical callback waited every block for workers of ordinary priority to wake up, and queued behind anything else using the global pool (ProRes decode uses it).

Realtime renders now process strips serially and time each one. Only while the strips' cost peaks above 50% of the block's duration (back below 25%, with a peak that halves over ~0.5 s) are they shared. Then the audio thread claims strips from the same atomic counter as the workers, heaviest first, so it only waits for strips a worker has already started. The pool is the mix engine's own, created by `MixEngine::new` and never on the audio thread. Offline renders always share their strips, as before. `crates/mix/src/schedule.rs` has the details.

## 2. Each block's clips come from an index

Each audio and MIDI track walked all of its clips every block to find the few under it: 165 µs per block on this session, pulling ~13.7 MB (63k × 216-byte `Clip`) through the caches ahead of the plugins. `ClipIndex` keeps, per track, the clip starts and the running maximum of their ends, so two binary searches bound the candidates. Playback builds it on the UI thread with each snapshot and sends both together (returned with the old session, so it is freed off the audio thread); `RangeRender` builds one for bounces.

The index only narrows the search. Candid…

title: VST3: cache scans on disk and scan without freezing the UI
author: mrrobbiec
body:
Every launch loaded every VST3 binary just to list its classes. That takes seconds with a large plugin folder, and runs every plugin's static initialisers whether it's used or not. The scan also ran inside a single UI frame the first time the VST3 menu opened, freezing the window.

## What changes

- **A scan cache on disk.** The app sets `vst3-cache.json` in its config folder (`set_cache_file`; not when `SOUNDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` is set). It stores each bundle's classes, or why it wouldn't load, keyed by path plus its binary's size and modification time. An unchanged bundle is listed without loading it. A bundle that failed isn't retried until its binary changes; Rescan reloads everything and rewrites the cache. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and a missing, corrupt, oversized (> 16 MiB) or other-version file is ignored.
- **A scan that doesn't block the UI.** `scan_step(budget)` lists cached bundles for the cost of a file stat and loads at most one uncached bundle per call. The Mix window's VST3 menu and plugin search call it once per frame with a 30 ms budget and show "Scanning VST3 plugins… n of m". `scan()` and `rescan()` still scan to completion. The scan stays on the main thread on purpose: modules adopt the thread that loads them (JUCE ties its message thread to it), and their editors must open there.
- **A folder added mid-scan joins it.** Before, `add_search_dir` filled an empty list with just that folder's plugins. With an incremental scan that would end it early, with the standard folders' plugins missing and the job never cleared, so the Scan button didn't come back. The folder now joins the running scan. Outside a scan it behaves as before.

- `cache`: round trip; junk, missing and other-version files read as empty; the stamp follows the binary.

title: Playback: one ASIO host and one device value per driver
author: mrrobbiec
body:
Two ways the ASIO backend could go silent once both input and output were in use, both because cpal's ASIO objects carry driver state:

1. **A second host reloads the driver.** asio-sys remembers the loaded driver per `Host`. Every device lookup made a fresh `cpal::host_from_id(Asio)`, which loaded and initialised the driver again under the streams already running on it, and unloaded it again when its last device dropped, silencing them. ASIO now gets one host for the whole process (`OnceLock`), handed out as `HostRef::Shared`. Other hosts are still made per call (`HostRef::Owned`).
2. **A second device value rebuilds the buffers.** An ASIO driver has one set of buffers for input and output together, and cpal keeps the record of that set in the `Device` value. Opening input from a different `Device` value of the same driver recreated the buffers for input only, leaving the output stream writing into buffers the driver had disposed. Device lookups on ASIO now return one shared value per driver name, so cpal creates both sides together.

Non-ASIO systems are unaffected: `device()` returns what it found unchanged.

## Notes

- The shared device values live for the process, one per driver name. That fits ASIO, which loads one driver at a time anyway, but it means the value isn't refreshed if a driver is re-registered while the app runs.
- Tested on Windows with an Audient iD14 (Audient USB Audio ASIO Driver, 48 kHz, 128 samples): a 42-track session with four VST3 instruments plays cleanly, and input with output at once (the case in point 2) works: guitar tracks recorded through the iD14 inputs while the session played back. `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -D warnings` is clean with and without `--features asio`, and `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback --features asio` passes all 36 tests. There's no automated test, since it needs an ASIO driver.

title: Playback: input monitoring drops a backlog instead of keeping it as latency
author: mrrobbiec
body:
Input monitoring could carry up to half a second of extra latency for as long as a stream ran. `InputRing` is the FIFO between the input callback and the output callback. Whatever sits in it is heard that much later, and the input and output streams start at different moments and their clocks drift. Nothing ever drained that skew, so it stayed as monitoring latency, up to the ring's 0.5 s cap.

## What changes

`pop_into` now drops the oldest frames beyond what is needed: one input callback (the size of the last push, recorded lock-free) plus this read, plus 32 frames of slack. It only trims once the backlog exceeds that allowance by at least the allowance itself or 128 frames, whichever is more, so ordinary callback jitter never trims. Both sides still only `try_lock`, and nothing allocates.

## Tests

- `monitor_backlog_is_dropped`: 200 callbacks queued before one read; what's heard comes from the newest callbacks, and at most one callback plus one read stays queued.
- `monitor_jitter_is_not_trimmed`: two callbacks queued before one read are played in full, oldest first.
- The existing ring tests (rate conversion, decimation, underrun, NaN) still pass. `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback` passes all 38 tests.

title: Fade deletion: preserve unfaded overlaps and restore playlist ordering
author: jackcanon
body:

Trimming can also move a clip start beyond a later clip after the playlist's only sort. This draft remembers selected adjacent pairs with opposing fades, preserves ordinary overlaps and unrelated crossfades, and sorts again after trimming.

This draft overlaps both and adds the distinction between actual opposing fades and plain selected overlaps. Their existing work should keep its credit. If those land first, I can rebase this to the remaining predicate and tests; please do not merge overlapping fixes independently without reconciling them.

title: Fix normalize producing inf samples for subnormal peaks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/dsp/src/offline.rs:62-79` (no existing issue): dsp::offline::normalize turns near-silent (subnormal-peak) audio into ±inf samples.

## Cause
`normalize` computed `target / p` in f32. When the peak `p` is subnormal, the quotient is larger than `f32::MAX` and becomes inf. Every sample was then multiplied by inf, in both the per-channel and joint branches.

## Fix
A new helper, `scale_to`, keeps the f32 gain whenever it is finite, so results for normal peaks are bit-identical to before. When the f32 gain would overflow, it computes the gain and the scaling in f64 and rounds back to f32, so a subnormal peak reaches the target level. The regression test `normalize_subnormal_peak_stays_finite` (crates/dsp/tests/offline_normalize.rs) fails without this change and passes with it. `normalize_silent_and_normal_channels` guards that silent channels stay zero and that normal channels still reach the target.

## Verified
- Regression tests `normalize_subnormal_peak_stays_finite`, `normalize_silent_and_normal_channels`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp --test offline_normalize`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The streaming bounce normalization in `crates/engine/src/io.rs` computes its own f32 gain (`db_to_gain(-0.1) / self.peak`). It can overflow the same way for a subnormal peak. I did not change it.

title: Resolve same-pitch overlapping notes when writing SMF
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/midi/src/smf.rs:486-493` (no existing issue): SMF export/import changes note lengths when same-pitch notes overlap.

## Cause
write_smf emitted an independent note-on/note-off pair for every note. When same-pitch, same-channel notes overlapped, the events interleaved. read_smf pairs offs with ons first-in first-out, so the notes swapped their ends and re-imported with different lengths.

## Fix
write_smf now trims a note that is still sounding when the next same-pitch, same-channel note starts, so its off comes before the next on. When several same-pitch notes start on the same tick, only the longest is written and the others are dropped, because the reader cannot tell them apart. The regression test `smf::tests::same_pitch_overlaps_do_not_swap_ends` covers a nested overlap (0 with length 1000 and 100 with length 200), a same-start overlap (2000 with lengths 500 and 900), and a non-overlapping note at 1000 that must keep its length.

## Verified
- Regression test `smf::tests::same_pitch_overlaps_do_not_swap_ends`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-midi same_pitch_overlaps_do_not_swap_ends`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
read_smf still pairs note-offs first-in first-out. Notes that do not overlap on the same pitch and channel are written exactly as before.

title: UI: CJK font fallback from the system fonts (#141)
author: midasdf
body:
## What was wrong

CJK text has no face in the UI font stack: the only non-Latin fallback was the system Hangul face
(`HANGUL` in `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`), so Japanese and Chinese session, track, clip and
marker names drew as missing-glyph boxes. This addresses the CJK part of #141, following the
maintainer's direction there: probe system fonts at runtime per script instead of bundling ~45 MB
of font files into every binary and the wasm build.

## The fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs` gains the same runtime fallback the Hangul path already used, for
two more scripts, in a fixed order:

1. **Japanese first** (kana and Japanese Han forms): `/System/Library/Fonts/ヒラギノ角ゴシック W3.ttc`
   and AquaKana on macOS; Yu Gothic / Meiryo / MS Gothic on Windows; Noto Sans CJK JP (face 0) and
   Noto Sans JP on Linux/BSD; `fc-match "sans-serif:lang=ja"` first on Linux/BSD.
2. **Chinese second**, for the characters the Japanese face lacks (页, 选, 删) and for Chinese names
   in general: PingFang / Hiragino Sans GB / STHeiti on macOS; YaHei / SimSun on Windows; Noto Sans
   CJK SC (face 2) and Noto Sans SC on Linux/BSD; `fc-match "sans-serif:lang=zh-cn"` first there.
3. **Korean last**: the existing `HANGUL` list, unchanged.

The faces are read from the platform's font paths (or `fc-match`) at startup, only OpenType/TrueType
files up to 64 MB are used, and nothing is redistributed. Every UI family gets them in that order
after the base fonts, so shared Han ideographs keep Japanese glyph forms while kana, Chinese and
Hangul all draw. `SOUNDCRAFT_NO_SYSTEM_FONTS` still disables system font loading entirely.

## Scope

Done here: Japanese, Simplified Chinese (shared/Traditional Han characters are covered through the
Chinese face's GB18030 coverage) and the unchanged Korean path.

Still open on #141 (not in this PR): a Traditional-Chinese-specific face selection, IME testing,
Devanagari/Arabic/Thai fallback and complex-script shaping/RTL layout. SoundCraft has no interface
language se…

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

body:
Lets a same-origin page that frames SoundCraft in an `<iframe>` open files in it and receive what it saves, like the GridCraft and WordCraft web bridges. With `?host=parent` and a same-origin parent:

title: Reset fades at cut edges in copy_range
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/edit.rs:157-174` (no existing issue): copy_range keeps fades of the original clip on a piece copied from its middle.

## Cause
`copy_range` trims each clip to the range with `trim_start_to` and `trim_end_to`, which only shorten an existing fade to fit the clip. So a piece copied from the middle of a clip kept the original clip's full fade-in and fade-out, while `split_clip` (used by cut and clear) resets the fade at each new edge.

## Fix
When `copy_range` trims a clip's start, it now resets `fade_in`, and when it trims the end, it resets `fade_out`, the same way `split_clip` does. A fade is kept only on an edge the range did not cut. A regression test covers copies from the middle, from the start, from the end and of the whole clip.

## Verified
- Regression test `edit::tests::copy_range_resets_fades_at_cut_edges`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib copy_range_resets_fades_at_cut_edges`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`trim_start_to`/`trim_end_to` still only clamp fades, because other callers rely on them keeping fades when a clip edge is trimmed.

title: Autosave: the autosave folders are owner-only on Unix
author: oracola91
body:
## What and why

Autosaves are unsaved sessions. `Autosave::create` made the autosave root and each session's folder with `create_dir_all`, and `Autosave::write` did the same for the `Audio Files` folder of audio that exists only in memory (`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs`). A session never saved also records its takes into `<autosave root>/<name>/Audio Files`, which the recorder makes (`TakeWriter::create`). On Unix all of these got the default mode (usually `0o755`) and the files in them the default file mode, so other accounts on the same machine could read the sessions and play the recordings, unless a folder above blocks them. That is common on Linux, where home folders are often readable by other accounts.

This adds `autosave::create_folder`, which creates folders with mode `0o700` on Unix (`DirBuilder` with `DirBuilderExt::mode`). The autosaver uses it for the root, the session folders and their `Audio Files`. `arm_recorder` uses it for the folder a never-saved session's takes go into (`<name>/Audio Files`), before the recorder makes anything in it. Takes of a saved session still go next to the session file, unchanged. A folder that already exists keeps its mode, for example an autosave root an earlier version made; the folders made inside it are still owner-only. Windows and the web build are unchanged.

PdfCraft and VectorCraft made the same change for their recovery folders (storytold/pdfcraft#3320, storytold/vectorcraft#3406).

#594 and #810 change the same line in `Autosave::create` to make a separate folder for each session. Whichever of them lands first, I'll rebase this onto it so the folder they create is owner-only too.

Not changed: folders an earlier version left keep their mode.

## How it was tested

- New unit test `the_autosaver_makes_owner_only_folders` in `crates/engine/src/autosave.rs` (Unix only). A new autosave root, the session's folder and its `Audio Files` are `0o700`. An existing root keeps `0o755`, and the session folder made inside …

title: Place Seconds and Frames grid lines at exact multiples of the step
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/grid.rs:127-128,158-161` (no existing issue): Seconds and Frames grids round the step to whole samples, so grid lines drift away from real seconds and frame starts.

## Cause
For Seconds and Frames grids, `line_at_or_before` and `next_line` used `step_samples`, which rounds the step to a whole number of samples (44 instead of 44.1, 1602 instead of 1601.6). Lines were then placed at `k * rounded_step`, so the rounding error grew with every line: 1.000 s at 44.1 kHz snapped to 44088, and 29.97 fps frame starts drifted by a whole frame after about 4000 frames.

## Fix
Absolute grids now compute line `k` directly: `round(k * exact_step)` for Seconds, `FrameRate::samples_at_frame(k * frames)` for Frames, and `k * n` for Samples. The line index is found by flooring and then corrected by one if rounding put it on the wrong side. `next_line` for these grids returns line `k + 1`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `grid::tests::seconds_grid_lines_land_on_whole_seconds`, `grid::tests::frame_grid_lines_land_on_frame_starts`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-time --lib grid_lines_land`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`step_samples` still returns the rounded step, because nudge and the UI's grid-density checks use it. The Bars|Beats (Note) grid code is unchanged.

title: Import Session from a Pro Tools export (File > Import > Import Session...)
author: rcappuccio
body:
Adds the Pro Tools AAF importer: `soundcraft-cli import-aaf`, the `file.import_aaf` command, and **File > Import > Import Session...** in the GUI.

**Stacked on #852**: until that merges, this diff also shows its commits. Only the last commits (`02ef450..`) are new here.


**Tested only on exports generated by Pro Tools 12.5.** If you have a later version of Pro Tools that can export AAF and the TXT session report, please try the importer on your sessions, or contact me and share sessions exported from other Pro Tools versions so I can test them.

title: Edit: keep stacked clips sorted when deleting fades
author: wayward-L
body:
# Edit: keep stacked clips sorted when deleting fades

`cargo test` (proptest `random_edits_keep_the_session_sane`) failed on `edit.fades_delete`: after `edit.duplicate_extend` and `edit.move_clips` (which clamps every clip's start to 0), three clips in one playlist share start 0. `delete_fades` assumed every overlapping adjacent pair is a crossfade and trimmed both edges to the pair's midpoint; that pushed a clip's start past the next clip's start and left the playlist unsorted.

## Fix

- Only treat a pair as a crossfade when the shapes really overlap (`a_start < b_start && a_end > b_start && a_end < b_end`); stacked/nested neighbours from a clamped move are left alone.
- Sort again after trimming, because a midpoint can land past a third clip's start.

## Tests

- Unit regression `delete_fades_keeps_stacked_neighbours_in_order` (3 clips at start 0, lengths 4000/3/15000) in `crates/engine/src/edit.rs`.
- Committed proptest seed `crates/engine/tests/random_edits.proptest-regressions`.
- The proptest plus `PROPTEST_CASES=400`/`1200` runs and `cargo xtask ci` are green.

The `move_clips` per-clip clamp (which can collapse a multi-clip selection onto 0) is intentionally unchanged; this PR only makes fades deletion safe for the result.

Split out of #783.

# Tooling: deterministic local pre-PR code review

title: Fix automation_id overflow and bad ids for high send/plugin slots
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/ui-egui/src/edit_window.rs:2474-2477` (no existing issue): automation_id panics with integer overflow for automation views with a high slot (e.g. send_255_level).

## Cause
`automation_id` computed `(b'a' + i) as char` with unchecked `u8` addition. For slot or send index 156 or more it overflows and panics in debug builds. For 26 to 155 it produces a non-letter character that `AutoParam::parse` can't read back.

A new `slot_id` helper emits a letter for slots 0..=25 and the decimal number for higher slots. `automation_id` uses it for sends and plugin slots. `AutoParam::parse` already accepts numeric slots, so every id now round-trips.
