title: Save Session: a bare file name is checked as the working directory against the write root
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #869.

A bare session name like `t.scraft` has an empty parent, and `write_session` passes that empty folder to `io::make_dir`, which runs the write-root check on it. `file_access::resolve` refuses an empty path, so with `--automation-*-root` the save fails with "path is empty", while `./t.scraft` (parent `.`) works and without roots the check is skipped. `make_dir` now checks an empty folder as `.`: docs/mcp.md says a path is made absolute against the server's working directory, so a bare name is the same file as `./t.scraft` and still has to be inside the write root. Creating the folder is unchanged (`create_dir_all("")` is a no-op). The fix sits in `make_dir` rather than at the call in `write_session`, so the other callers that can get an empty folder (`save_session_copy`, and #371's session-copy code, which uses the same `parent().unwrap_or("")` shape) get it too; it's the same empty-parent-means-`.` rule `sync_dir` already uses in io.rs, and that #612 and #876 apply in their own paths (bounce publication, AAF media folder). Neither of those touches the save path, so this doesn't overlap them.

Validation:
- `a_bare_save_session_name_lands_in_the_working_directory_inside_the_roots` (apps/soundcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs): runs the real `soundcraft-cli mcp` in a working directory that is both roots, with the steps from the issue. title: Deps: fix the workspace build after the dependency bump
author: wayward-L
body:
## Why main does not build

#767 bumped 11 dependencies but changed only the five manifests, so `upstream/main` no longer compiles on Linux either — not just the FreeBSD job. Three independent breaks:

1. **symphonia 0.5.5 → 0.6.1** — the probe module, `CodecParameters` and the decoded-buffer API moved; `soundcraft-audio-io` fails with 24 errors.
2. **cpal 0.16 → 0.18** — `SampleRate` is a plain `u32` now, the per-stream error types are unified into `cpal::Error`, the stream builders take `StreamConfig` by value, device names moved to `Device::description()`, and `StreamTrait` gained required `buffer_size`/`now` methods; `soundcraft-playback` fails with 52 errors.

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release

author: justinjohn0306
body:

title: fix(model): saturate the arithmetic in trim_start_to / trim_end_to (#907)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #907.

> **Depends on #959.** `main` does not compile right now (#767 bumped symphonia and cpal past breaking API changes). #959 restores a building tree; this branch is rebased onto it and contains only the `clip.rs` change.

**Cause.** `Samples` is `i64`, and `crates/model/src/clip.rs`'s two public trim methods did plain subtraction:

```rust
let new_start = new_start.min(self.end() - 1);   // end() - 1
let delta = new_start - self.start;               // extreme new_start vs extreme start
self.length -= delta;                            // -=
let new_end = new_end.max(self.start + 1);       // start + 1
self.length = new_end - self.start;               // extreme new_end vs extreme start
```

Command callers clamp to `MAX_POSITION` before calling, so nothing in the app trips this today. But the methods are `pub`, and a clip read from a hostile file can hold any `i64` before `sanitize` runs. An extreme `new_start` against an extreme `start` wraps in release and panics in debug.

**Fix.** Each site becomes a saturating operation followed by the same clamp `sanitize` already applies — so the result is bit-identical for every input a command can produce:

```rust
let new_start = new_start.clamp(-MAX_POSITION, MAX_POSITION).min(self.end().saturating_sub(1));
let delta = new_start.saturating_sub(self.start);
self.length = self.length.saturating_sub(delta).clamp(1, MAX_POSITION);
```

**Test.** `trims_saturate_on_extreme_arguments` sweeps `i64::MIN`/`MAX`, `±2 * MAX_POSITION` and the edges, in both directions, asserting positions stay within `±MAX_POSITION` and lengths within `1..=MAX_POSITION`. Verified against the unfixed arithmetic: it fails with `attempt to subtract with overflow`.

**Build.** `cargo test -p soundcraft-model` → 41 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-model --lib --no-deps --tests` clean.

title: fix(engine): number backups off the run the app writes, and refuse a linked Backups/ (#917)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #917.

> **Depends on #959.** `main` does not compile right now (#767 bumped symphonia and cpal past breaking API changes). #959 restores a building tree; this branch is on top of it and contains only the `io.rs` change.

**Cause.** `back_up` took the next number from `max().checked_add(1)` and pruned every `n` with `n + 10 <= next`. In a shared project folder:

- a planted `Song backup 4294967295.scraft` made `checked_add` overflow, so every save logged *"numbers are exhausted"* and wrote nothing — backups off, silently and permanently;
- a planted `Song backup 4294967285.scraft` made every save prune the real backups, because pruning kept the ten *highest* numbers.

`75eb152`'s `create_new` guard only protects the final component; a symlinked `Backups/` is still followed by `create_dir_all`, the copy and every prune.

**Fix.** Three parts:

- **Numbering** walks up from 1 while the name is taken, bounded by `BACKUP_RUN_LIMIT`. A planted high number is outside the run, so it neither exhausts numbering nor shifts pruning; a planted number *inside* the run still occupies its slot and can't displace a real backup.
- **Pruning** walks `range(..next).rev().skip(BACKUPS_KEPT - 1)`, so it only considers numbers below `next` and keeps the newest ten of the run.
- **A symlinked `Backups/`** is refused outright via `symlink_metadata`, so the copy and the prunes can never escape through it.

`BACKUPS_KEPT` and `BACKUP_RUN_LIMIT` are now named constants — the keep-count was a bare `10` inside the prune predicate.

**Tests.** Three cases, each verified to fail against the old logic:

- `a_planted_high_backup_number_does_not_turn_backups_off` — the `u32::MAX` scenario from the audit.
- `a_planted_number_inside_the_run_does_not_prune_the_real_backups` — a planted in-run name must not shift numbering or displace a real backup.
- `backup_never_writes_through_a_link_to_an_outside_file` — updated: its second half assumed backup 1 was still free, which the fix now occupies, so …

title: Let the Edit window's I/O column set volume and pan
author: lucasegen
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

The "vol" and "pan" readouts in the Edit window's I/O column were painted text: the volume and pan of a track could be read there but not changed. #724 asks for volume and pan next to the track in the track window.

Closes #724.

## Change

The two readouts become buttons. Nothing is added to the header: an untouched column looks as before, and a readout paints something more only when it is hovered, focused or open.

- **Volume.** A click opens a vertical fader (the Mix window's widget) over a readout that takes a typed dB value.
- **Pan.** A click opens a slider, or an L and an R slider on a stereo track.
- **Alt-click** resets without opening a popup. Volume goes to 0 dB. Pan puts every panner back to what a new track has: centre on mono, hard left and right on stereo.
- **A VCA, or a track on a multichannel output, keeps a text-only pan**, as in the Mix window.

Everything goes through `mix.volume` and `mix.pan`:
- A drag, a typed value or a reset is one undo step (`execute_merged`; the fader and the sliders use the Mix window's keys).
- The fader sets `Gesture::Fader`, so Touch and Latch automation write it.

To share code, `editable_readout`, `parse_db` and `parse_pan` become `pub(crate)`, and the Mix window's "is this track surround-panned" test becomes `surround_panned`, used by both windows.

## Testing

New tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/edit_window_headers.rs`:

Two gaps in how the Edit window shows the selection:

1. The ruler marked a range with two small triangles at the top of the ruler area, and marked nothing for an insertion point.
2. The blinking edit cursor was hidden during playback.

On the incumbent, with Link Timeline and Edit Selection on, the arrows in the ruler and the edit cursor in the tracks are the same selection shown twice: an insertion point is one arrow and the cursor, a range is an arrow at each end (guide p. 889). The cursor also stays on screen while the playhead moves; the guide defines each cursor (p. 728) but does not say outright that both are drawn together, which comes from press articles. SoundCraft already draws both from `edit.selection`; it just did not show them like that.

## Change

Two commits.

**Mark the selection in the main ruler with a split arrow.**
- The insertion point is one arrow pointing down at the ruler: a shaft over a head, tip on the foot of the row. A selection cuts it in two along its vertical axis. The left half sits on the start (cut edge on the start, wing to the left), the right half on the end (cut edge on the end, wing to the right). With no selection the halves join into the whole arrow on the insertion point.
- Both halves come from one definition (`arrow_half`), mirrored, so they always fit together. Each is filled, with a thin dark outline, and as tall as its ruler row.
- They sit in the main timebase ruler (the one that carries the main-counter marker; the top ruler if that one is hidden), in blue, or in red while any track is record-armed.
- They replace the two small accent triangles, which appeared only for a range.
- The left wing reaches 10 px out of its cut edge. At position 0, where a new session puts the insertion point, that is outside the timeline, so the clip is widened by 10 px for the ruler row only (never over the track headers). A start scrolled out of view keeps the plain clip.

title: Edit window: butted clips share one seam, and the clip name is a small pill
author: lucasegen
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Two things set the Edit window apart from the incumbent, one at every cut and one on every clip:

1. **A cut is drawn twice.** Two clips that meet exactly (the later one starts where the earlier ends) each draw their own outline, so the cut is two dark lines side by side, with a round corner on each side of it. The incumbent draws a single thin line between them, as thick as a clip's own outline, with square corners.
2. **The clip name is a full-width bar.** A coloured band across the top of the clip holds the name, the rating stars and the lock. It takes a strip of the clip's height from the waveform, the fades and the gain line. The incumbent keeps the clip body uniform and puts the name in a small rounded pill at the top-left corner.

After this PR:

- **Butted clips share one 1 pt dark seam with square corners.** The later clip draws the line and the earlier one drops its right edge. Gaps, overlaps (crossfades, layers) and lone clips look as they did. Selection only recolours the body, so a selected clip keeps its full outline.
- **The name is a pill** at the clip's top-left, one point inside the outline: half-transparent black, white bold text, as wide as the text plus padding.
  - A short clip caps the pill and cuts the text cleanly, with no ellipsis. A clip too narrow to show anything useful shows no pill.

title: Crossfades: store the cut, draw a zone, and select, slide, trim and delete it
author: lucasegen
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

A crossfade is two clips that overlap, the earlier one fading out and the later one fading in for exactly as long as they overlap (`fade_out.len == overlap == fade_in.len`). SoundCraft did not record where the two clips are *cut*, and the Edit window had no gesture for the pair as a whole. Today:

1. **The cut is forgotten.** The middle of the overlap stands in for it, so a crossfade made off-centre comes back centred as soon as anything needs the splice (Delete Fades, for one).
2. **Create Fades over a crossfade stacks fades on it.** With A = [0, 1100) and B = [900, 2000), creating fades over [500, 1500) leaves both fades 600 samples long across a 200-sample overlap.
3. **Delete Fades trims every overlapping pair on the track back to its midpoint**, including pairs outside the selected range (#449, see notes).
4. **A crossfade cannot be handled as one thing.** A click selects one of its clips. Its two fades have their own handles, and changing one alone breaks the equality above. Delete and Backspace do nothing. Clear and Cut on a clip of the pair act on its whole range, so they also cut into the partner.

After this PR:

- The cut is stored. Create Fades over a crossfade replaces it, longer or shorter, around the same cut. Delete Fades goes back to the cut, and only on the crossfades the range touches.
- In the Edit window a crossfade is a translucent zone over its cut. The two clips are butted at the cut, each drawn on its own side, and no line marks it. A click selects the crossfade and nothing else. Dragging the zone slides the cut and leaves the audio where it is. Pulling an edge with the Trim tool lengthens or shortens it from that side, the cut fixed. Delete or Backspace removes it.
- Selecting a clip of a crossfade selects what shows of it, up to or from the cut. Clear, Cut and Copy on it remove or copy the clips whole and rejoin the partner at the cut.

author: lucasegen
body:

Before this PR:

1. **Edit > Fades > Create (Cmd+F) opens a plain list of shapes.** The chosen shape goes to every fade the selection makes, so a crossfade cannot get a different shape on each side. title: Follow the desktop light/dark setting for the System theme on Linux (#951)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #951.

On Linux, eframe/winit never reports a system theme, so `ctx.system_theme()` is always `None` and **System** always ended up Dark.

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/appearance.rs`. When egui reports no theme, `theme::wants_light` now uses the desktop's own setting. On every other platform, and whenever egui does report a theme, nothing changes.
- On Linux a worker thread reads the XDG Settings portal's `org.freedesktop.appearance` / `color-scheme` value (1 = dark, 2 = light, 0 = no preference). It then follows the `SettingChanged` signal and asks for a repaint only when the value changes. It subscribes before the first read, so a change during startup is not lost, and nothing is polled. If there is no session bus or no portal, or the call times out (2 s), the value stays unknown and System falls back to Dark as before.
- Values nested in more than one variant (some portals send them that way) are unwrapped.
- This follows the same approach as CADCraft's `desktop_theme.rs`, LightCraft's `appearance.rs` and the `craft-platform` appearance module.
- Adds `zbus = "5"` as a Linux-only dependency. zbus 5.19.0 is already in the lock file through AccessKit/AT-SPI, so `Cargo.lock` only gains the dependency edge and no new packages.
- Unit builds never query the real desktop, so the existing theme tests stay deterministic on a machine set to light mode.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` now describes the Linux portal fallback, including for offscreen `ui_shot` renders.

Tests:
- `appearance::tests::desktop_setting_is_used_only_when_egui_reports_nothing`: the desktop value is used only when egui reports nothing, and the desktop is not asked when egui has an answer.
- `appearance::tests::portal_color_scheme_codes` (Linux only): maps the portal codes 0/1/2 and unknown values.

title: MCP: --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root may each be given more than once
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #874.

`--automation-read-root` and `--automation-write-root` can now each be given more than once, the same way VectorCraft takes them since storytold/vectorcraft#3546 (and FigCraft too), so one client config works across the suite. `AutomationRoots` keeps a list of folders per kind, and a path passes only if it lies inside one of the roots of its kind. The resolution is unchanged from #309: links followed, `..` resolved, whole folder names compared. So two sibling roots don't make their parent a root, and a link or `..` that leaves one root is refused unless it lands inside another root of the same kind. A folder given twice counts once. The refusal message stays `outside the read root X` with one root and becomes `outside the read roots X, Y` with several. The startup line now reads `files confined: read A, B; write C`.

The flag parser keeps the guarantees it had: a missing operand, an empty value or a `-folder` operand is still an error, and every folder must exist. The only thing that changes is the "given twice" error, which was there so a mistyped repeat couldn't silently replace a root. Now a repeat adds a folder and never drops one. `mcp_automation_root_flags_are_checked_up_front` used to expect "given twice", so those two lines now check that a missing folder or a missing operand in the second flag still stops the server. `read_root()`/`write_root()` are replaced by `describe()`, and `soundcraft-cli` was their only caller. docs/mcp.md is updated.

title: Require replace: true for file.export_session_text to overwrite

title: Don't register a source for a take that a punch range misses
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #920

## Cause
`add_recording_in` called `add_source` before working out which passes the punch range keeps. When the punch missed every pass, no clip was placed and no undo step was pushed, but the source stayed in the pool and was saved with the session.

## Fix
The take is resampled to the session rate first, so its length is known. The kept range of every pass is then computed, and `add_source` runs only if at least one pass keeps a clip. The clips are then placed from those precomputed ranges. Regression test: `io::record_tests::a_punch_that_misses_the_take_leaves_the_session_alone` (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib a_punch_that_misses`). CI is run by the pipeline.

## Verified
- Regression test `io::record_tests::a_punch_that_misses_the_take_leaves_the_session_alone`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib a_punch_that_misses`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`add_source` is unchanged. Placement, playlist creation for later passes and the undo push behave as before. The take is now resampled to the session rate before `add_source` is called, so the registered source holds session-rate audio. It is still marked unsaved when the take was resampled.

title: Guard all playback output paths against NaN from interpolation overflow
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #918

## Cause
The output interpolation `a + (b - a) * fr` overflows to infinity when two adjacent finite samples are near ±3.4e38. With `fr = 0` that gives `inf * 0 = NaN`, and `f32::clamp` passes NaN through. Only the mono-device path mapped non-finite values to 0.0, so the stereo, folded and direct output paths could send NaN to the device.

## Fix
Interpolation is now `a * (1.0 - fr) + b * fr`, which cannot overflow for finite inputs. Every output write now goes through one `out_sample` helper that clamps to [-1, 1] and maps any non-finite value to 0.0.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::interpolation_overflow_between_huge_samples_never_reaches_the_device`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-playback interpolation_overflow`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Nothing else in the mixing path changed, and `contain_failure` is unchanged.

title: Restore all engine side-effect state when a command panics
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #908

## Cause
When a command panicked, `Engine::execute` rolled back only `doc`, `revision` and `dirty`. Anything the command had already changed in `clipboard`, `messages`, `transport_requests` or `last_selection` stayed behind, so the rollback was partial.

`execute` now snapshots `clipboard`, `messages`, `transport_requests` and `last_selection` before running the command. It restores them in the panic arm along with the document. A test-only probe command and a regression test cover this.

## Verified
- Regression test `panic_tests::a_panicking_command_restores_side_effect_state`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine panic_tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `Err` return path is unchanged. Commands that fail normally can still leave messages or other side effects, as before. `execute_view` and `execute_merged` are also unchanged.

title: Fix quadratic WAV parsing with many empty data chunks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #893

## Cause
`wav::parse` called `only_chunks_follow` for every zero-size `data` chunk, although only the first `data` chunk is used. Each call walked the rest of the file, and the walk had no limit, so parse time grew quadratically with the number of empty chunks.

## Fix
The `empty` check now runs only for the first `data` chunk, so the file gets one linear walk. `only_chunks_follow` also stops at 100,000 chunks and returns `false` beyond that, which matches the cap in the main chunk loop. Regression test `wav::tests::many_empty_data_chunks_parse_in_linear_time` covers the reported case (`cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io --lib many_empty_data_chunks_parse_in_linear_time`).

## Verified
- Regression test `wav::tests::many_empty_data_chunks_parse_in_linear_time`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io --lib many_empty_data_chunks_parse_in_linear_time`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change the #466 behaviour for a single empty `data` chunk followed by metadata. A finished file with an empty first `data` chunk and fewer than 100,000 chunks after it behaves as before. With more chunks than that, the walk now returns `false`, so the first `data` chunk is treated as a recording and the metadata after it is read as audio. This follows from the cap and is a deliberate trade-off. I also left the main loop's 100,000-chunk cap as it was. I added no separate test for the #466 case, so the existing tests cover it.

title: Keep delay-line storage when the compensated latency changes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #889

## Cause
`DelayLine::set` replaced its buffers with fresh zeroed vectors whenever the delay length changed. It is called on every block, so automating a reported latency such as the compressor lookahead caused allocations of up to 2^20 × channels samples inside the audio callback. It also wiped the audio the line was holding, which caused a dropout.

## Fix
The rings now only grow, and the new ring keeps the old contents in order. A write position plus a read offset of `len` samples gives the delay, so changing the delay inside the ring's current capacity only moves the read offset, with no allocation and no zeroing. A regression test checks that the buffer pointers stay the same and that held samples still come out after a latency change.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::delay_line_change_keeps_buffers_and_history`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-mix --lib delay_line_change_keeps_buffers_and_history`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Lines are still allocated when they first grow, sized to the next power of two (capped at MAX_LATENCY + 1). They are not pre-sized to the maximum latency in `sync`, so growing past the current size can still allocate once. Only the delay line was changed; the latency reporting in the compressor and the per-block `set` callers were left as they were.

title: Bound Print Score and MusicXML output size (fixes #921)
author: sbacaro
body:
Fixes #921

## Problem
`MAX_MEASURES` limited the number of measures but not:
- items per measure (up to 1,024 sixteenths),
- pitches per chord (up to 128),
- total output bytes.

A hostile session with a 10M-note session produced a ~20 GB SVG `String` and aborted the process (the ledger-line loop emits ~2 KB of SVG per note against ~40 B of JSON in the session). `write_score` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) had no guard.

## Fix
- `fill` now caps items per measure (`MAX_ITEMS_PER_MEASURE` = 128) and pitches per chord (`MAX_PITCHES_PER_CHORD` = 16), so `layout` cannot build a pathological document in the first place.
- `svg()` and `musicxml()` now return `Result<String, String>` and check a 256 MiB byte budget (`MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`) incrementally — after each measure — so the output cannot grow without bound and the process never aborts.
- `write_score` surfaces the error to the caller as bad params.

## Tests
- `output_is_bounded_by_byte_budget`: a dense score stays under the budget.
- `oversize_score_is_refused_not_aborted`: many dense parts return `score too large` instead of aborting — for both SVG and MusicXML.

All engine tests pass (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine`, 261 tests) and `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * MusicXML and SVG exports are limited to 256 MiB. Exports that exceed the limit return an error instead of producing oversized output.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Export-generation errors are reported before output is written.
  * Score generation limits each part to 100,000 notes, each chord to 16 pitches, and each measure to 128 items.
  * Pitches beyond the chord limit no longer extend the onset duration, and discarded measure duration is restored as rests where possible.

title: Video: clamp H.264 IDCT inputs and temporal-direct mvs to the spec ranges (#928)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #928

Note: PR #957 ("Prevent H.264 skip-run bounds overflow") is a different H.264 fix — it covers
the CAVLC skip-run bound (#897), not this. No overlap with these files.

## What was wrong
Crafted H.264 streams could panic the decoder in debug / overflow-checks builds (and decode
wrapped garbage in release) in two places:

1. **Inverse transforms** (`crates/video/src/h264/transform.rs`). `scale4`/`scale8` and the DC
   dequantisations deliberately wrap (`wrapping_mul`, see the existing
   `huge_levels_dequantise_without_overflow_panics` test: huge levels must not panic *there*),
   so the coefficients reaching `idct4_add` (plain `+`/`-` in the row/column butterflies,
   ~lines 101-124 on main) and `idct8_1d` (used by `idct8_add`, ~lines 141-158) can be any
   i32 — the first butterfly addition of `i32::MAX` inputs panics with "attempt to add with
   overflow".
2. **Temporal direct motion vectors** (`crates/video/src/h264/slicedec.rs:606-608` on main).
   `m0[0] - mv_col[0]` / `m0[1] - mv_col[1]` subtract two i16 motion vectors; with extreme
   co-located mvs (stored mvs wrap by design: parsed `mvd` is truncated with `as i16` and the
   mvp add is `wrapping_add`) the subtraction overflows and panics.

## Root cause
The decoder's hostile-input convention (never-crash standard) is wrap-or-clamp arithmetic on
input-derived numbers; the dequantisation and mvd paths follow it, but the IDCT butterflies
and the temporal-direct MV subtraction use plain arithmetic on those (unbounded) values. The
spec leaves the output *unspecified* in exactly these situations — ITU-T H.264 8.5.12.1
(likewise 8.5.13.1 for 8x8): the inverse-transform output is unspecified when a dequantised
value r falls outside −2^15 to 2^15 − 1; and motion vectors are always within −2^15 to
2^15 − 1, so values beyond that only arise from non-conforming/crafted streams.

## What changed
- `transform.rs`: new `r_clamp` helper; `idct4_add` and `idct8_add` clamp their
  transform-domain input (`d`) to −2…

title: Bound the command journal (fixes #926)
author: sbacaro
body:
Fixes #926

## Problem
`Engine::execute` pushed every journaled command into a `Vec` that was never trimmed (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:339-341`). Large params (`clips`/`indices` arrays, junk fields from MCP or the control channel) were kept for the life of the process.

## Fix
- Store the journal as a `VecDeque` ring buffer capped at `MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRIES` = 10,000 entries (oldest are dropped).
- Cap a single entry's params at `MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRY_BYTES` = 64 KiB (serialized): a larger value is replaced by a `{"__truncated__": true}` marker before journaling.

## Tests
- `journal_is_bounded_to_max_entries`: pushing 10,500 entries keeps exactly 10,000.
- `oversized_params_are_truncated_in_the_journal`: a 256 KiB param is journaled as the truncation marker, not kept whole.

All engine tests pass (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine`, 261 tests) and `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Command history is limited to the 10,000 most recent entries; older entries are removed as new ones are added.
  * Command parameters are recorded up to 64 KiB. Parameters that exceed this limit or cannot be serialized are represented by a truncation marker, while smaller parameters are preserved.

title: Bound offline render commands: dedupe tracks and a total sample budget (fixes #896)
author: sbacaro
body:
Fixes #896

## Problem
AudioSuite-style commands looped over tracks/clips and kept every result as a new pool source, which undo snapshots also hold. Each render was capped per-track (`render_limit`), but:
- `tracks_param` did not remove duplicates — listing the same track id eight times rendered it eight times;
- `audiosuite.process`'s signal_generator branch checked only per track, so many distinct tracks could exceed memory in one command (one call listing the same id eight times over ~3 h kept ~16 GiB and aborted).

## Fix
- **`tracks_param`** (`cmd/mod.rs`) now dedupes track ids with a `HashSet`.
- **`generate()`** (`cmd/audiosuite.rs`) subtracts `frames * channels` from a `MAX_RENDER_SAMPLES` budget across all tracks and refuses with `too much audio to generate in one command` before allocating anything.

## Tests
- `duplicate_track_ids_generate_once_not_per_listing`: the same track eight times generates one clip.
- `generate_refuses_a_total_budget_across_tracks`: two distinct tracks over the total budget are refused.

All engine tests pass (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine`, 261 tests) and `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The long-term per-session pool byte budget (the same direction as #882) is left out of scope, as noted in the issue.

  * Audio generation now checks the combined sample limit across tracks and reports an error when the limit would be exceeded.

title: WAV: decide an empty data chunk's emptiness once, not per chunk
author: sbacaro
body:
## Problem

Fixes #893. `only_chunks_follow` walks from a given offset to the end of the file. The main WAV chunk loop called it for **every** zero-size `data` chunk, although only the first data chunk is ever used. Since an empty chunk advances the parse position by only 8 bytes, the cost is quadratic in the number of chunks (and unbounded in trailing `junk` chunks).

Measured on this machine (`--release`): a 4 MB file with 100k empty `data` + 400k `junk` chunks took **37 s** in `probe` before this fix — freezing imports, session opens and MCP commands. The audit measured 88 s for a similar case.

## Change

- `wav::parse` now decides the first data chunk's emptiness once (`data.is_none() && …`), instead of re-testing every empty data chunk.
- `only_chunks_follow` is bounded at 100,000 chunks (the same cap as the main loop), returning `false` beyond that.

## Validation

- New regression test `many_empty_data_chunks_parse_in_linear_time` fails on the old code after 37 s (`parse took 37.4s`) and passes in ~0.03 s with the fix.
- The existing #466 tests (empty data + metadata, unfinished recording, data-with-audio) still pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, doctest, assets, layers — all pass. The wasm gate fails on this machine for any code (Homebrew Rust toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target and no rustup is installed); the same failure occurs on the base commit, so it is environmental.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved WAV parsing for files with very large numbers of empty chunks. Chunk inspection is now bounded, and qualifying files with an empty first audio chunk are recognized as containing zero audio frames. This avoids prolonged parsing on these inputs while preserving accurate reporting of empty audio.

title: Add a loading progress modal for native audio imports
author: reoniazx
body:
Importing audio from the native Import Audio dialog, Workspace or external file drops now shows a responsive loading modal while a background worker reads, decodes, converts the sample rate and builds waveforms. Previously, these operations ran synchronously on the UI thread and could make the app appear frozen.

- Show the current filename, file count and processing stage with one cumulative progress bar for the whole batch. Smooth stage transitions without resetting between files; display 100% only after successful placement.

- Group multiple dropped audio files into one batch and guard session replacement, quitting and conflicting jobs while import is active.
- Update the roadmap, UI parity notes and G-19 without changing readiness estimates.

CLI/control imports retain their synchronous result contract. Browser byte imports remain synchronous. Reading, resampling and waveform construction finish their current stage before cancellation is observed; decoding checks cancellation per PCM block or codec packet. title: Render strips serially on the audio thread instead of using rayon
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #886

## Cause
`run_strips` dispatched work to rayon's global pool whenever there were at least 4 strips, including when called from the cpal audio callback. That thread is not a rayon worker, so it blocks on a latch until the shared pool, which also runs bounces, freeze and previews, finishes the work, causing dropouts.

## Fix
`run_strips` now takes the parallel path only when the caller is not the audio thread. The audio thread processes its strips serially on its own thread. Pool workers are always marked as not the audio thread.

## Verified
- Regression test `audio_thread_tests::the_audio_thread_never_hands_strips_to_the_rayon_pool`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-mix the_audio_thread_never_hands_strips_to_the_rayon_pool`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add a dedicated realtime pool, so offline rendering keeps using the global rayon pool. The wasm `run_strips` and the H.264 decoder's pool are unchanged.

title: Tracks: clip track and group names to their rows in the side lists (fixes #990)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #990 ("[Bug Report] [SoundCraft] Graphic bug mix window — track names goes beyond the edge").

## What was wrong

In the Tracks and Groups side panel (visible in the mix window layout), a long track or group name
painted past its row and across the panel's edge — the screenshot shows
`24H2026_27_JANVIER audi…` running over the lists' scrollbar gutter and the panel divider.

Measured on a headless render at 1600×1000: the row ends at x = 166 and the 10 px scrollbar gutter at
x = 176, but the name's paint was only clipped at x = 176 — every name longer than the row bled across
the gutter and over the panel's border line. The CLIPS list in the same file already clips its row
text to the row; the Tracks and Groups rows predate that.

## Root cause and fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, `tracks_and_groups()`: the track name and group name were painted with
plain `ui.painter().text(...)`, whose clip reaches to the scroll area's full strip (row + scrollbar
gutter) instead of the row. Fix: paint both through `ui.painter().with_clip_rect(r)` — the same idiom
`clip_list()` uses two functions below. Two-line change; no behavioural surface beyond the clipping
(hit targets, drag-to-reorder, visibility dots, colors and AccessKit labels unchanged).

## Tests

New `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/side_lists_text.rs`: rename a track to a 39-character name and create a
44-character group, then inspect the painted shapes via `harness.output()` (the geometry pattern
`mix_strip_layout.rs` uses) and assert the name's paint `clip_rect.right()` stays within its row's
right edge (`get_by_label(name).rect()`). Shapes from the edit window's track header (the same name in
its own clipped column) are excluded by an intersects-the-row filter.

- `a_long_track_name_stays_inside_its_row` — fails on main (paint clipped at 176, row ends at 166).
- `a_long_group_name_stays_inside_its_row` — fails on main, same numbers.

title: Add a built-in Ring Modulator plugin
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The built-in plugins have no ring modulator (`docs/plugin-parity.md`, Modulation row), and AudioSuite › Modulation › Sci-Fi runs the Flanger. Avid's D-Fi page describes Sci-Fi as "analog synth-type ring modulation, frequency modulation, and variable frequency resonators" with "positive/negative resonance, and modulation control by LFO, envelope follower, sample-and-hold": https://web.archive.org/web/20250918091748/https://www.avid.com/plugins/d-fi

This adds Ring Modulator (`ring_mod`), an original plugin in the Modulation category that also runs offline as AudioSuite. The page gives no parameter names or ranges, so they are SoundCraft's own.

- **Effect:** Ring multiplies the input by a sine carrier at Frequency. Frequency Mod reads the input through a delay that the carrier swings by ±1 ms. Resonator + and Resonator - feed the output back after one period of Frequency, with a positive or a negative sign, and scale it by `1 - resonance` so the peak gain at resonance is unity.
- **Modulation:** Mod Source picks an LFO, an envelope follower (5 ms attack, 100 ms release) or sample and hold at Mod Rate. At 100 % Mod Depth the frequency moves up to two octaves either way; the envelope moves it up only.
- **Parameters:** Effect, Frequency (20 Hz to 5 kHz), Resonance (0 to 95 %), Mod Source, Mod Rate (0.05 to 20 Hz), Mod Depth, Mix.
- `tail_samples` covers the resonators' feedback until it falls by 60 dB at the lowest modulated frequency.
- AudioSuite › Modulation › Sci-Fi opens it instead of the Flanger.
- `docs/plugin-parity.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and the README plugin list name it. The parity doc's Total row now reads 25 processors + 3 instruments, the count of the built-in registry (it said 26 + 2), and its Instruments row lists `sampler` and no longer lists the Sampler as missing.

title: Add a built-in Auto Pan plugin
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The built-in plugins have no auto-pan (`docs/plugin-parity.md`, Modulation row). The AutoPan chapter of Avid's Audio Plug-Ins Guide describes the controls: Output (-24 dB to +12 dB), Width and Manual, an LFO or envelope panning source, the Path, a Rate in BPM with Link To Tempo and a Duration from a 16th note to 4 bars, Single, Beat Clock, Envelope and Manual LFO triggers, and the envelope's Threshold, Attack and Release: https://web.archive.org/web/20260809112153/https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/PT/Audio_Plug-Ins_Guide_2023.9.pdf (Chapter 60).

This adds Auto Pan (`auto_pan`), an original plugin in the Modulation category that also runs offline as AudioSuite.

- **Panning:** the mono sum of the first two channels goes to left and right with constant-power gains, so a signal that is the same on both channels keeps its level at the center. - **LFO:** Sine, Triangle, Square, Saw Up, Saw Down, Half Sine and 4 Step Triangle. One cycle takes the Duration at Rate (BPM), or at the session tempo with Link to Tempo; a bar follows the time signature.

Beat Clock restarts the LFO at the start of every Duration on the transport and runs it at Rate in between. Note and beat Durations count from the song position, and bar Durations count from the bar line; the guide says the Duration "determines how often the Beat Clock signal triggers" AutoPan. title: AudioSuite: Vari-Fi slows a clip down to a stop or speeds it up from one
author: dotCooCoo
body:
AudioSuite ▸ Pitch Shift ▸ Vari-Fi resamples the clip at a constant speed (`docs/plugin-parity.md` lists "varispeed effect" as a gap). The Vari-Fi chapter of Avid's Audio Plug-Ins Guide describes a speed ramp: Slow Down and Speed Up, "similar to a tape recorder or record turntable" slowing down to or speeding up from "a complete stop"; Fit To, which processes two thirds of the selection so the result keeps its length; Extend, which renders 150 % of the selection from the same start; and Fades On or Off: https://web.archive.org/web/20260809112153/https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/PT/Audio_Plug-Ins_Guide_2023.9.pdf (Chapter 29).

This changes what the Vari-Fi menu item does: it now opens the speed ramp instead of the constant-speed Speed slider. The `varispeed` process stays available to `audiosuite.process`.

- **`offline::vari_fi`:** reads the audio with the speed at `1 - u²` for Slow Down and `1 - (1 - u)²` for Speed Up, where `u` runs from 0 to 1 over the result. Both curves average 2/3 of normal speed, which gives the guide's two thirds and 150 %. Fit To plays the first two thirds for Speed Up and the last two thirds for Slow Down, as the guide's Extend section implies. With fades, the gain follows the speed. At either end of the input, the interpolation reads the first or last sample, so the level holds at the stop with Fades Off.
- **`audiosuite.process`:** the new `vari_fi` process takes `change` (0 Slow Down, 1 Speed Up), `selection` (0 Fit To, 1 Extend) and `fades` (1 On, 0 Off). A clip whose result would not fit in one offline render is refused, as the other AudioSuite processes refuse it.
- **AudioSuite window:** Change, Selection and Fades rows of radio buttons. The defaults are Slow Down, Fit To and Fades On.
- `docs/plugin-parity.md` and `ROADMAP.md` describe it.

The guide does not give the speed curve, the fade shape or the defaults; those are SoundCraft's own.

title: Add a built-in Subharmonic plugin
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The built-in plugins have no subharmonic synthesizer (`docs/plugin-parity.md`, Harmonic row). Chapter 54 of Avid's Audio Plug-Ins Guide 2023.9 (pages 343 to 353) describes one that "synthesizes low-frequencies based on the harmonic content of the source audio signal", with its controls and their ranges: https://web.archive.org/web/20260809112153/https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/PT/Audio_Plug-Ins_Guide_2023.9.pdf

This adds Subharmonic (`subharmonic`), an original plugin in the Harmonic category that also runs offline as AudioSuite. The controls and ranges follow the guide's mono and stereo version. The synthesis method, what each Drive character changes, that a band solo also mutes the dry signal, that -120 dB turns a band off, the linear Mix taper and the defaults are SoundCraft's own; the guide does not describe them.

- **Bands:** Range picks a lower and an upper band frequency (120-180, 80-120, 60-90 or 40-60 Hz). Each band band-passes the input at its frequency and multiplies it by a flip-flop that changes sign on every rising zero crossing, which moves the band an octave down at a level that follows the band. The direct band is the input low-passed at the upper band frequency.
- **Gains and solos:** Lower, Upper and Direct Gain run from -120 to +24 dB (-120 dB is off), each with a solo. A soloed band plays alone and mutes the dry signal.
- **Drive:** -18 to +18 dB into a saturation stage with six characters: Clean I (tanh), Clean II (a softer curve), Resonant I and II (tanh, with Q 2 and 4 on the low-pass after each divider), Distort I (asymmetric, DC removed) and Distort II (hard clip at full scale).
- **Filters:** HP and LP Freq (5 to 1000 Hz) and Q (0.1 to 5) shape the summed bands after Drive.
- **Mix:** below 50 % the dry signal stays at full level and the wet level falls; above 50 % the wet signal stays at full level and the dry level falls. Wet Solo mutes the dry signal. Input and Output run from -18 to +18 dB.

title: Add an Android app shell

body:
This adds `apps/soundcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus the platform seams the desktop shell normally supplies. The engine, the UI, the theme and the command table are untouched.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — builds as `libmain.so`, loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.

The picker cannot answer inside the frame that asks: the hook starts a worker, returns `None`, and the picked file is copied into `<filesDir>/import/` and opened over the app's own control channel. `pick_save` answers with a scratch path in `export/` and publishes the finished file to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination. `pick_folder` stays `None`.

title: Meters: Peak Hold and Clip Indication can be set to 3 Seconds, Infinite or None
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Meters hold a peak for a fixed 2 s and keep a clip light on until Track › Clear All Clip Indicators (`feed_meter` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`), and neither can be changed. The Pro Tools Reference Guide's Metering preferences ("Peak/Clip Section", pages 122 and 123) give Peak Hold and Clip Indication three options each: 3 Seconds, Infinite ("until you click them to clear them") and None. Page 228 says Track › Clear All Clip Indicators clears all meters: https://web.archive.org/web/20210805202452/https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/PT/Pro_Tools_Reference_Guide_2020.12.pdf

- The guide places both under Setup › Preferences › Metering; until a Preferences window exists, SoundCraft shows them as radio buttons in its own Setup › Metering… window (`window.metering`).
- `ui.peak_hold` and `ui.clip_indication` take `{"mode": "three_seconds" | "infinite" | "none"}` and return the current mode without one. Both are saved with the UI preferences.
- The defaults are 3 Seconds for Peak Hold (it was 2 s) and Infinite for Clip Indication (as before). With None, the clip light is lit only for the meter update in which the clip happened. The guide does not give defaults, so these are SoundCraft's own.
- Track › Clear All Clip Indicators also clears the held peaks.
- The 3 Seconds timers use the frame time. The old hold timer added up each update's step. That step is capped at 0.25 s, and after playback stops each frame applies it twice, so the timer did not follow the clock.
- Each channel has its own hold timer, which restarts only when the level reaches a held value above zero. The old timer was shared by both channels and restarted on any level equal to the held one, so a silent or steady channel kept the other channel's peak held for as long as it played.

title: Reject out-of-range timecode fields so Min:Secs strings fall through
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/timecode.rs:189-211 (Timecode::parse), reached via crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:275-287 (position_param_raw)` (no existing issue): Min:Secs position strings are misread as Timecode when the main counter is Timecode.

## Cause
Timecode position parsing accepted any non-negative number for minutes, seconds and frames. With the Timecode main counter, the Min:Secs string "0:12.500" was read as 00:00:12:500, so it never fell through to the Min:Secs parser.

## Fix
In `parse_position`, the Timecode branch now returns a parse error when minutes or seconds are 60 or more, or frames are at or above the session frame rate. Out-of-range strings then fall through to the other formats, so "0:12.500" is read as Min:Secs.

## Verified
- Regression test `min_secs_with_timecode_counter::min_secs_string_is_not_misread_as_timecode_when_the_counter_is_timecode`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test it min_secs_string_is_not_misread_as_timecode`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Timecode::parse` is unchanged, because it has no frame rate and the range check needs one. Hours are still unbounded. A string whose fields happen to be in range, such as "0:12.5", is still read as timecode under the Timecode counter.

title: track.delete: keep a folder's input bus when surviving tracks route through it
author: CloudCorpRecords
body:
Fixes #914

### The problem

`track.delete` treats whatever bus a folder takes as its input as the folder's own summing bus (`owned_folder_bus` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/track.rs`) and removes it, repairing every route to it: surviving tracks lose the bus as an input (set to none), as an output (rerouted), and as a send target (the send is cleared).

But a folder does not always own its input bus. `track.input`, or a session file, can point a folder at any bus: the demo session's shared Verb bus, say, which an aux takes as its input and several tracks send to. Deleting such a folder removed the Verb bus and wiped every reverb send in the session.

### The fix

When collecting the busses a delete would remove, skip any bus that a surviving track still routes through: as its input, as a send target, or as its output from outside the deleted folder's own subtree. Members' outputs are the one exception, because the delete already reroutes those to the parent folder's bus, and they are what makes a genuinely owned folder bus removable. Members of the deleted folder are still promoted and rerouted exactly as before; only the bus, and the routes of tracks outside the folder, are now preserved.

### Tests

New regression test `deleting_a_folder_keeps_a_bus_other_tracks_still_use` in `cmd/track.rs`: in the demo session, point a new folder's input at the Verb bus with `track.input`, delete the folder, and assert the bus, the aux's input and the Snare's send all survive. On main before the fix it fails with "a bus other tracks route through must survive"; with the fix it passes. The existing `tracks_can_move_between_nested_folders_and_leave` still covers the owned case: a deleted folder's own bus is removed.

Run here: `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine` (282 lib tests and 73 integration tests, all passing), `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clean).

title: Keep bounced stems from overwriting each other on name collisions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/io.rs:658 (bounce_stems_with)` (no existing issue): Bounce Stems overwrites a stem when two track names sanitize to the same file name.

## Cause
bounce_stems_with builds each stem path from the sanitized track name and never checks whether that path was already used. Names like `Kick?` and `Kick*` both become `Kick_`, and names like `Kick` and `kick` point to the same file on case-insensitive file systems. The later bounce overwrote the earlier one, and both paths were still reported.

## Fix
bounce_stems_with now records each written path, lowercased, and adds `-2`, `-3` and so on to the file name until the path is unused, the same way export_clips does. Only the paths actually written are reported. Added regression tests for names that sanitize to the same string and for names that differ only in case.

## Verified
- Regression tests `bounce::stems_of_tracks_with_colliding_file_names_do_not_overwrite_each_other`, `bounce::stems_of_tracks_whose_names_differ_only_in_case_do_not_overwrite_each_other`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test it stems_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
sanitize_name and export_clips are unchanged. The check only looks at paths written during the current call, not at files already in the target directory.

title: Plugin hosts: blocklist, paths-only scans and targeted rescans (CLAP, VST3)
author: forwardaudio
body:
## Why
Scanning, and creating any one CLAP or VST3 plugin, loads every binary in the standard
plugin folders on each launch. Copy-protected plugins (iLok and the like) then pop licence
dialogs, and a test harness that drives `soundcraft-cli` pays for — and risks crashes from —
plugins it never uses. We hit this running SoundCraft headlessly as a cross-platform
test host for our own plugins.

## What
- `SOUNDCRAFT_PLUGIN_PATHS_ONLY=1`: scan only `VST3_PATH` / `CLAP_PATH`.
- `SOUNDCRAFT_PLUGIN_BLOCKLIST` + `engine.plugin_blocklist {set, add, remove}`: bundles,
  folders or bare bundle names that are never loaded (component-wise, case-insensitive,
  links resolved on either side). Blocked plugins leave the cached lists at once.
- `rescan: [path, …]` on `engine.vst3_plugins` / `engine.clap_plugins`: reload only those
  bundles. Before any full scan their plugins can be inserted without loading anything
  else, and a rescanned bundle wins over an installed one with the same id.
- Safety: rescan targets must be absolute and inside the search path (a rescan never loads
  what a full scan wouldn't), and inside the read roots under `--automation-read-root`.
- Audio Units are unaffected (listed by the system without loading binaries).

## Tests and docs
- `scan_control` (own process per host, against the CLAP and VST3 fixtures) + engine
  command tests; `cargo xtask ci` passes (with `SOUNDCRAFT_PLUGIN_PATHS_ONLY=1` locally).
- `control-protocol.md` (Choosing which plugins load), `plugin-parity.md`, `gaps.md`
  (G-13: Plug-In Manager UI, saved blocklist and on-disk scan cache remain).

Open to reshaping the command surface (e.g. one `engine.plugin_rescan` for both formats)
or sharing the path helpers between the two hosts if you prefer.

title: Offline renders: fixed, cycled or seeded random block sizes for plugin testing
author: forwardaudio
body:
Offline bounces always ran in 1024-sample blocks, so hosted plugins never saw odd or
changing block sizes — where many plugin bugs hide. `file.bounce_mix` and
`file.bounce_stems` now take an optional `block`: a size (1–16384), a list that is
cycled, or `{"random": {min, max, seed?}}`, seeded so a failing run can be repeated.
Plugins are prepared for the largest size. The default is unchanged (1024), and realtime
playback is unaffected (blocks of at most 512).

Sizes asked for are capped at ten million blocks per job (or as many as the default would
take, if more; normalizing counts twice, stems once per track), so tiny blocks can't keep
the engine busy for hours; default-size bounces are never refused. On a session without
automation, comparing a default bounce with an odd-size bounce shows block-size bugs in a
plugin; docs/control-protocol.md has an example and explains why automated sessions differ
per block size.

We use this to test our own plugins (VST3 and CLAP) headlessly: two effects stay
bit-identical down to 1-sample blocks.

Tests: block-size sequences, averages and validation; a probe plugin receives exactly the
requested sizes, unsplit, never above what it was prepared for; `bounce_mix` (both
normalize passes) and stems render in the sizes asked for; renders through a latent plugin
match a fixed-size render sample for sample; the cap, and that default sizes are exempt.
`cargo xtask ci` passes locally.

title: Playback: render each device callback in one block (up to 8192 frames)
author: forwardaudio
body:
Playback mixed in blocks of at most 512 frames whatever the device buffer, so with a 1024,
2048 or 4096-frame buffer plugins saw each callback split into 512-frame pieces and were
prepared for 512. Plugins whose processing depends on their block size (FFT or lookahead
sizes, CPU per callback) behaved differently than in other hosts.

Each Player now sizes its block when it opens: the device buffer × the session/device rate
ratio, between 512 and 8192. The mix engine, its buffers and the third-party plugins Side
prepares all use that size; a buffer change already reopens the stream, so plugins are
prepared again off the audio thread. The Playback Engine window shows the block.

Automation is read once per block (volume/trim/VCA at the block ends, sends and plugin
parameters at its start), so a session with any automation lane keeps 512-frame blocks —
larger ones would coarsen automation from ~10 ms to as much as 170 ms. Reading automation
on a timeline grid (as pan already is) would lift that limit; happy to follow up with that
separately. Callbacks larger than the block (ALSA rounding, varispeed) are still split, and
WASAPI shared mode calls back at its own period whatever buffer is chosen.

No new allocation on the audio thread; buffers are sized at open. Memory per strip grows
with the block (about 200 KB per stereo track at 8192).

Tests: block sizing over buffers, rates and limits; a probe plugin sees a 2048-frame callback
as one block (four 512-frame blocks before, and with automation). Docs: hardware-parity,
architecture, gaps (G-01), roadmap. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally.

title: VST3/CLAP hosts: resizable plugin editor windows negotiated with the plugin
author: forwardaudio
body:
Plugin editors whose view can resize now get a resizable host window, and user resizes follow the plugin's constraints.

- **VST3 (macOS, Windows):** after `attached()`, if `IPlugView::canResize()`, the window gets a resize handle. Drags ask `checkSizeConstraint`; finished resizes snap to it and call `onSize`. The macOS zoom button respects the constraints.

Alt+Shift-dragging the fader of a selected track in the Mix window now moves every selected track's fader by the same amount, for #865.

Avid's Pro Tools Shortcuts Guide (2023.6, Global Keyboard Shortcuts) lists Option+Shift (Alt+Shift) as the modifier that changes a parameter on all selected channel strips, while a plain move touches one track; the Reference Guide describes grouped faders as moving relative to each other and keeping their offsets when one of them reaches the end of its travel. Touch/Latch automation writes still follow only the fader under the mouse. If you'd rather have a plain drag move the selection, as the issue describes for other DAWs, happy to switch.

libc++     std::__thread_specific_ptr<std::__thread_struct>::__thread_specific_ptr()
libc++     std::__thread_local_data()
WaveShell1-VST3  std::__thread_proxy<… wvWavesV17_1_42::ServerClient::WCBIClientWithWLSThread …>
```

`pthread_key_create` fails with `EAGAIN`: the process has run out of thread-specific data keys (`PTHREAD_KEYS_MAX`, 512 on macOS). The Waves shell is the first library in the process to start a `std::thread` through the system libc++, which needs one more key, and the resulting `std::system_error` escapes the thread and aborts.

The keys are used up by the scan. `Bundle::load` keeps every scanned binary loaded for the life of the process, and each one's static initialisers (plus `bundleEntry` / `clap_entry.init`) keep whatever keys they took. I measured this outside SoundCraft with a small C harness that does what the scan does (`dlopen`, `bundleEntry` + `GetPluginFactory`, `clap_entry->init`) for every installed bundle: free keys went from **510 → 144** after the scan alone, before any plugin was instantiated. Each instance and editor takes more (a Waves instance takes ~15), so a normal session hits zero.

The same in-process scan also took down the unmodified 0.12.1 build during a scan on this machine: a heap corruption in HIToolbox, with ~470 plugin images mapped. Any plugin that crashes or hangs while loading takes the whole app down.

## Fix

The desktop app scans CLAP and VST3 bundles **out of process**, like most DAWs:

- `soundcraft-vst3-host` / `soundcraft-clap-host` get an `isolate` module (safe code, no new `unsafe`). When a scanner executable is set (`set_scanner`), `scan_paths` runs each bundle in a short-lived child (`<exe> --scan-vst3-bundle <path>` /…

title: Mixer: a click on an insert opens the plugin's own editor
author: forwardaudio
body:
As in other DAWs, clicking a hosted (CLAP/VST3) insert or instrument opens the plugin's own editor. Built-in plugins, Audio Units and slots without an audio engine open SoundCraft's parameter window. For hosted inserts, the parameter window moves to the slot menu (Edit Parameters…), next to Open/Close Plugin Editor.

- `window.plugin {track, slot, view?, value?}` gives the same behaviour as a command (CLI/control/MCP): `view:"editor"|"parameters"`, `value:false` closes, and it replies `{track, slot, view, value}`. `window.hide_floating` also closes hosted editors; `window.close` keeps upstream behaviour.

Their Open Plugin Editor is greyed out with the reason, and a click opens the parameter window with no error.
- `Player::set_editor` (doc-hidden) lets UI tests put a fake editor in a slot; happy to switch to a `test-support` feature if you prefer.

title: Strip Silence: Rename sets the names of the clips it leaves
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Builds on #1040, which adds the Extract and Separate buttons; until #1040 merges, this diff also shows its commits.

On `main`, Strip Silence leaves every clip it cuts with the name of the clip it came from, and the Strip Silence window has no Rename button. The reference guide's "Auto-Naming for Strip Silence" section (Pro Tools Reference Guide 2020.12, Chapter 41, page 926) describes the button: it "opens the Rename Selected Clips dialog, which determines how clips are named when stripping silence", with Name, Number, Zeros and Suffix fields and a Clear button, and the dialog "remembers your previous settings". Its example, SFX, 23, 1 zero and .Reel1, gives SFX023.Reel1 to SFX026.Reel1. The guide: https://web.archive.org/web/20210805202452/https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/PT/Pro_Tools_Reference_Guide_2020.12.pdf

title: Meters: keep every block's peak until the UI takes it
author: forwardaudio
body:
The audio thread overwrote the shared meter snapshot every block (~94 blocks/s at 512 frames, 48 kHz) while the UI read it 20–60 times a second, so the meters only ever showed the latest block and short transients were under-read (at 60 Hz and 512 frames, about a third of the blocks were never seen).

- Blocks are now folded together (max per channel peak and gain reduction; plugin failures keep the latest count) until the UI takes them with `Player::take_meters`, which starts a new period. Blocks rendered while the UI holds the lock wait in an audio-side accumulator instead of being lost; the audio thread still only `try_lock`s.
- Stop, start and locate zero the meters in place instead of clearing the maps, so playing again no longer re-allocates every track's entry on the audio thread. The UI works out which tracks a session update deleted and tells the audio thread, which drops just those entries.
- The Mix window and the Renderer read the one snapshot the app takes per poll, so a period's peaks aren't split between readers.

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` green. New playback tests: a one-block spike among quiet blocks reaches the UI; a spike rendered while the UI holds the meters arrives on the next read; stopping zeroes meters in place and deleted tracks are pruned; gain reduction keeps its maximum until taken.

This is the first of a small meter series: #1047 (ballistics and peak readout) builds on it, #1046 (pre-fader metering) is independent, #1049 (meter types) builds on both.

title: Mix: make Pre-Fader Metering meter before the fader
author: forwardaudio
body:
Options › Pre-Fader Metering was stored with the session, but every track meter still read post-fader.

With it on, track meters now read the pre-fader tap (after the inserts, before fader and VCA) that pre-fader sends already use. The strip keeps that copy whenever the option is on, and it goes through the same delay compensation as the post-fader signal, so the meter stays in step with what is heard. Mute doesn't silence the pre-fader tap (mute automation does, as for pre-fader sends). Master faders keep metering what they send out.

Known limits, documented in `docs/control-protocol.md` and `docs/ui-parity.md`: an aux input's pre-fader tap isn't delay-compensated (as its pre-fader sends already aren't), and turning the option on sizes each strip's pre-fader buffer and delay line in the audio callback that receives the change, as other document edits do.

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` green. Mix tests: pre-fader metering reads before the fader and stays in step with delay compensation; master faders keep metering post-fader with the option on.

title: Meters: true peak, RMS, VU and K-System meter types
author: forwardaudio
body:
**Depends on #1047 and #1046**; only the last two commits are new here (plus the merge of the two). Draft until they land.

Track and main meters can measure sample peak, true peak (dBTP), RMS, VU or K-12/14/20 (`options.meter_type`, saved with the session; chosen from a meter's right-click menu, which also offers "next type").

- `soundcraft_dsp::meter::MeterBank` measures one block of a strip per call: every channel's sample peak plus the selected type only; no allocation once the channel count is stable.
  - True peak: the 4× polyphase filter of ITU-R BS.1770-4 Annex 2 the loudness meter already used (now shared), on a doubled history buffer.
  - RMS: 300 ms exponential average (full-scale sine reads −3 dB). VU: average-responding, critically damped, 99 % of a step in 300 ms. K-12/14/20: 600 ms RMS, sine-referenced (AES17).
- Each type has its own scale: dBFS, VU (0 VU = −18 dBFS) or K units with K-System colours. Peak types keep the display release; averaging types bring their own ballistics.
- Changing the type resets holds, clip lights and readouts; each reading carries the type it was measured as, so blocks of the old type are dropped rather than shown on the new scale.
- Clip lights and readouts follow the highest sample peak of any channel, or on a true-peak meter the highest true peak, so inter-sample overs light them too. The main meter reuses the last master fader's measurement instead of oversampling the mix twice.
- Offline renders (bounces, stems) turn metering off entirely (`set_metering(false)`); plugin failures are still recorded.

title: AU host: Audio Unit editor views on macOS
author: forwardaudio
body:
**Depends on #1038 and the CLAP-on-macOS PR #1048**; only the last three commits are new here. Draft until those land.

Audio Units get editors on macOS.

- **Editor view:** the unit's own Cocoa view via `kAudioUnitProperty_CocoaUI` (the `AUCocoaUIBase` factory in its bundle, by class name or principal class, checked for `uiViewForAudioUnit:withSize:`), or CoreAudioKit's `AUGenericView` when it has none, in a floating transient NSWindow sized to the view. The window follows the view's frame changes, is user-resizable only when the view resizes with its superview, and counts as closed only when the user closes it.
- **Parameter sync:** an `AUEventListener` on the main run loop watches value changes and gesture ends and queues `(id, value)` (latest per parameter, bounded), drained by `PluginEditor::idle`. Host-side `set_param` goes through `AUParameterSet` with our listener as sender, so the view updates without an echo.
- **Lifetime:** teardown removes and releases the view in an autorelease pool, closes the window, disposes the listener, all before the unit is disposed. Dropped off the main thread with the editor open, the unit and view are leaked rather than torn down on the wrong thread. Objective-C exceptions are not caught.
- **Channel layout:** `configure()` now also sets `kAudioUnitProperty_AudioChannelLayout` (Mono/Stereo tag matching the accepted format) on the buses before `AudioUnitInitialize`, so units that display their bus layout no longer show a placeholder. Units that refuse the property still initialize.

Closes #501.

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` green. A `harness = false` main-thread test opens Apple's AUDelay (own view) and AUSampleDelay (generic view), checks view class and window size, moves a generic-view slider and receives the edit from idle, sets a parameter without echo, hides, closes via the window button, reopens and drops with the editor open. title: Plugin hosts: editors stay open while the app is inactive or minimized
author: forwardaudio
body:
**Depends on #1038** (resizable editors); only the last four commits are new here. Draft until #1038 lands.

Plugin editor windows closed themselves when SoundCraft lost focus or was minimized: the editor links took "window not visible" to mean "the user closed it".

- **macOS:** host windows use `hidesOnDeactivate`, so ⌘-Tab to another app ordered every VST3 editor out and the link tore it down within a frame (the slot stayed lit, the editor was gone). The window delegate now records the user's close (`windowWillClose:`; the host's own close clears the delegate first), and the link checks that instead of `isVisible`.
- **Windows:** VST3 and embedded-CLAP host windows are owned by the app window, and Windows hides owned windows while their owner is minimized, so minimizing SoundCraft closed every editor. `WM_CLOSE` (which only hides the window) now sets a closed flag kept in the window's Rust-side state (`GWLP_USERDATA`, next to the sizer), so marking a close can't fail; raising the window clears it.
- `HostWindow::is_visible` is renamed `is_open`, since it now means "not closed by the user".

Testing: `cargo xtask ci` green on macOS. The macOS main-thread editor test orders the fixture's window out (stays open), closes it by its button (closed) and reopens it; it fails against the old `isVisible` check. Each host gets a `#[cfg(windows)]` unit test (hidden stays open, `WM_CLOSE` closes, `raise` reopens); it is type-checked and clippy-clean for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` but has **not run on Windows**: I have no Windows machine, and the CI gate runs on Ubuntu only. If someone can run `cargo test -p soundcraft-vst3-host -p soundcraft-clap-host` on Windows (it needs a desktop session and briefly shows a window), that would cover it. Linux only check/clippy (it keeps the stub window module).

title: Scale trim_clip file bounds by clip stretch
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/edit.rs:756-758,770 (trim_clip, file closure)` (no existing issue): Trim tool lets a stretched clip run past the end of its audio file.

## Cause
`trim_clip` bounded trimming to the file with `start - offset .. start - offset + material_len`. That treats source samples as timeline samples and ignores `clip.stretch`. The mixer plays a clip from `offset + rel / stretch`, so the bound was wrong for any stretched clip.

## Fix
In the `file` closure of `trim_clip`, the source offset and the material length are now multiplied by the clip's stretch before they are used as timeline distances. A clip with stretch 0.5 over a 10,000-frame file now clamps its end to 5000. A clip with stretch 2.0 can extend to 20,000.

## Verified
- Regression test `edit::tests::trim_clip_bounds_stretched_clip_to_its_file`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib trim_clip_bounds_stretched_clip_to_its_file`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`create_fades` handle calculation still uses unscaled source lengths. I did not change it, because it is outside this bug.

title: Strip XML-forbidden characters from MusicXML/SVG score export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/score.rs:216-218 (xml_escape), used by musicxml() and svg()` (no existing issue): MusicXML/SVG score export writes control characters from track names, which makes invalid XML.

## Cause
`xml_escape` only replaced `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`. Control characters and other code points XML 1.0 forbids, such as U+0001 and U+FFFE, passed through unchanged from track names, the title and the composer. Strict MusicXML and SVG parsers reject the resulting files.

## Fix
`xml_escape` now drops every character outside the XML 1.0 `Char` production before applying the existing escapes. A regression test checks both the MusicXML and SVG output.

## Verified
- Regression test `score::tests::exports_drop_characters_xml_forbids`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib exports_drop_characters_xml_forbids`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change how names are stored or validated, and I did not change the escaping of `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`. Forbidden characters are dropped, not replaced with a placeholder.

title: Keep clip spacing when moving a group left past the session start
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/edit.rs:486-489 (move_clips), reached via edit.move_clips in crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:935` (no existing issue): Moving several clips left past the session start squeezes them together.

## Cause
move_clips clamped each clip's new start to 0 separately. When a group moved left by more than the earliest clip's start, that clip stopped at 0 while the later clips kept the full shift, so the spacing inside the group shrank.

move_clips now limits the shift once, to the negative of the earliest moving clip's start, and applies that same shift to every clip. The group stops at 0 together and keeps its spacing.

shuffle_clips and ripple_spans already keep the group's spacing, so I left them alone.

title: Playback: audio callback load and dropout meter (System Usage, ui.audio_load)
author: sanderdewijs
body:
## What

A load and dropout meter for the audio callback.

- Each device callback is timed against how long its buffer lasts. **Window ▸ System Usage** shows:
  - the average and peak load over the last half second, with a bar;
  - the heaviest callback;
  - the number of *late* callbacks: callbacks whose render took longer than the buffer lasts, so the device ran dry (a dropout).
  - A Reset button starts the worst load and the count again.
- `ui.audio_load {reset?}` returns the same for agents: `measured`, `average`, `peak`, `worst`, `late`, `callbacks`, `buffer_ms`. The MCP reaches it through `execute` with `--connect`.
- System Usage now counts instruments as plugin instances. It used to count inserts only, so a session with 28 inserts and 14 instruments showed 28.

## How

`crates/playback/src/load.rs`: the audio thread is the only writer. It keeps a local half-second window and publishes through atomics, so there are no locks and no allocation in the callback. The UI asks for a reset with a flag, and the audio thread clears the counters at its next callback. cpal doesn't pass on the device's own overload notices, so late callbacks are counted here instead. On the web (wasm32), `Instant` isn't available and the meter reports `measured: false`.

## Why

Glitches during realtime playback were hard to tell apart: plug-in behaviour, scheduling jitter, or plain CPU shortage. Without a number, every fix was a guess. On a real 19-track session the meter immediately separated two causes:
1. A plug-in in trial mode: 9 late callbacks, up to 276%. After activation: 0.
2. A remaining isolated 97% spike on a ~13% average, which is the jitter #886 describes.

It also gives #886, #1006 and #804 a before/after measure on the same session.

## Tests

- `load.rs` unit tests: per-window averaging and peaks, late counting, worst, reset, and hostile timings (NaN, infinite, zero and negative durations are ignored).
- `ui-egui` integration test: `ui.audio_load` without an audio engin…

Part 2 of #1065: a read-only query that lists the parameters of the plugin in an insert slot or a track's instrument. Built-in, CLAP, VST3 and Audio Units all work the same way.

mix.plugin_params {track?, slot: 0..9 | a..j | "instrument", filter?, offset?: 0, limit?: 200 (1..1000)}

- `steps` and `values` for toggles and choices. `value` is the numeric index.

Without an editor (Audio Units, or headless/MCP), there was no way to find out which parameter ids a hosted plug-in has. Checked against `auval -v` for Ample Guitar SC: all 222 ids and names match.

title: Playback: strips render on the audio thread itself; count underruns and late callbacks
author: forwardaudio
body:
Playback dropped out under CPU load: the realtime callback handed strips to rayon's global pool whenever a session had four or more, then waited for them. The pool's workers run at normal priority, so with the machine busy the callback, a realtime thread, waited on starved workers (priority inversion). Waiting there also breaks AGENTS.md's "the callback never blocks". The global pool is also shared with bounces and video decoding, so offline work could delay callbacks too.

Two commits:

1. **Strips render on the audio thread itself.** `run_strips` keeps rayon for offline renders (bounces, `render_range`) and renders strips one after the other when it runs on the thread `mark_audio_thread` marked. `as_audio_thread`, which marked pool workers while they rendered for the audio thread, is no longer needed and removed.
2. **The player counts how it keeps up.** cpal 0.18 reports underruns as `ErrorKind::Xrun`; they were only logged. `Player::health()` returns the device callbacks, device-reported xruns, callbacks that overran their buffer period, and the worst callback load; `Player::take_health()` reads and counts afresh (each counter swapped for zero, so nothing falls between). Relaxed atomics plus one `Instant::now()` per callback, no locks or allocation; nothing on wasm32. The control method `audio.health` (`{reset?: bool}`) reports them with the device's rate and buffer; documented in docs/control-protocol.md and known to `soundcraft-cli app`. Input (recording) streams don't report into it yet.

## Measured

"Before" is this branch with only `&& !on_audio_thread()` removed from `run_strips` (the counters are needed to measure). Dev profile throughout, 8-core Mac mini.

**Headless**, opt-in test (`cargo test -p soundcraft-playback -- --ignored`): 16 stereo tracks looping one noise source through an EQ and a compressor each, one callback per 512-frame period at 48 kHz (10.67 ms), all cores but one spinning. Two runs each:

| | p99 | slowest | late callbacks of 1500 |
…

title: setup.playback_engine / setup.hardware: apply device and buffer in the app, don't claim it headless
author: sanderdewijs
body:
## What

`setup.playback_engine` and `setup.hardware` accepted `{device?, buffer_size?}` but only stored them as session values (`engine.device`, `engine.buffer_size`) that nothing reads.

The result was misleading: `setup.playback_engine {buffer_size: 1024}` answered `buffer_size: 1024` while the device kept running at 512 frames. With nothing set, it also reported 1024. Found driving SoundCraft over MCP and confirmed with the callback load meter from #1067: 10.7 ms buffers after the command, 21.3 ms after choosing 1024 in the window.

## Fix

- **In the app**, a programmatic call goes through the same path as Setup ▸ Playback Engine (`ui.audio_device`):
  - `device` becomes the output device, and `buffer_size` reopens the device.
  - `delay_compensation` is still applied through the engine command, once the device change is accepted.
  - The result is the state actually in use: `applied: true`, the device name, `device_buffer` (null when the device default is in use), the sample rate and delay compensation.
- **The menu** still opens the window.
- **Buffer values:** any integer from 16 to 8192, as `ui.audio_device` accepts. Anything else is an error and changes nothing, not even delay compensation. Previously out-of-range values were clamped and 300 was rounded to 512.
- **Headless (CLI without the app):** the request is still stored, but the result says `applied: false`, and `buffer_size` is null until one is set.

- ui-egui:

title: Set plugin parameters and automation by name (#1065, part 3)
author: sanderdewijs
body:
> **Builds on #1076 (and #1072, #1071, #1066).** This PR adds the last three commits: "Engine: resolve a plugin parameter by id or name", "Mix: set plugin parameters and automation by name", and "Docs: …".

## What

Part 3 of #1065: wherever a plug-in parameter id is accepted, its name is accepted too. Sessions keep storing ids.

**One resolver** (`cmd/param_key.rs`):
1. An exact id wins, so existing scripts never change meaning.
2. Then a case-insensitive name: Unicode lowercase, trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed. CLAP's `Module/Name` is matched as the name itself.
3. Otherwise an error:
   - unknown: `<key> is not a parameter of <plugin>; did you mean: <up to 8 Name (id)>`;
   - ambiguous: `<key> matches several parameters of <plugin>: Name (id), … — use the id`.
4. Keys are capped at 200 characters.

**Where it applies:**
- `mix.insert`, `insert_param`, `insert_params`, `instrument`, `instrument_param`. In a `params` object every key is resolved before anything is stored, and two keys landing on the same id are an error.
- Automation (`automation.set_point`, `write_range`, `clear`, `write_to_current`, `edit.paste_to_current_automation`): `plugin:<slot>:<name>` is resolved per target track against the plug-in in that slot, and the lane is stored with the id. An empty slot keeps the key as given, which is today's behaviour.
- Value errors now name the parameter: `` `twintig` is not a value of S-Strum Time (1598) ``.
- Results that echo a parameter include `id` and `name`.

title: ui: Tracks and Groups and Clips in full-height dock columns
author: aiongg
body:
Moves the side panels from split frames into dock columns, using craft-ui's shared docking.

## Layout
- **Edit:** Tracks and Groups is a full-height dock column on the left (168 pt), and Clips one on the right (230 pt). The MIDI editor sits under the session view, between the two docks. Memory Locations and Undo History float, as before.

- Panels dock into columns:
  - dropped on a group's middle, a panel joins it as a tab;
  - on its top or bottom third, it stacks a new group;
  - on a column edge, it makes a new column;
  - at an empty window edge, it makes a new dock.

## Saved layouts
- Saved settings carry a `docking_version`. Settings from before dock columns (no version) load with the new default layouts, once, with every other setting kept. Window configurations reset the same way when recalled.

- A panel with no recorded place, or whose recorded anchor is gone, reopens at its default place:
  - Tracks and Groups and Clips go back into their dock, and a missing dock is rebuilt at its width;

```

On wasm32, `std::fs::File` has no `Drop`, so clippy reports each explicit `drop` of a `File` (or an `Option<File>`) as `drop_non_drop`. `cargo xtask ci` runs clippy for the host only, and `cargo xtask wasm` runs `cargo check`, so neither the gate nor CI reports these errors.

- `Autosave::discard` (`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs:258`) sets `self.lock = None`, which closes the lock file before the folder is removed, on every target.
- The `drop(lock)` in `autosave::leftovers` (`autosave.rs:290`) and the `drop(dst)` in `io::copy_new` (`crates/engine/src/io.rs:1281`) carry `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, as the `DirBuilder` mode call in `Autosave::create` carries `#[cfg(unix)]` (`autosave.rs:191`).
- On the desktop builds, the same files close at the same points as before.

There is no new test: the repository runs no wasm32 tests, and the host code does not change behavior. The evidence is the clippy run above on `main` and the same command on the branch, which exits 0.

body:
